**normalize.hpp applies calibration profiles to raw gamepad samples.**

## API

`apply (const profile&, const raw_sample&, canonical_sample&) noexcept` writes calibrated sticks, triggers, and physical-unit motion allocation-free.

## Contract

`apply` centre/range-corrects, radially clamps, drift-thresholds, rescales measured trigger travel, and debiases/scales motion; valid `profile` assumed, untouched motion remains absent. Depends on `types.hpp`, `utility.hpp`, `profile.hpp`, `sample.hpp`.

entries.response:
**filter.cpp implements frame-time-independent `gamepad::unstable::controller::aim::low_pass` smoothing.**

## Interface

`low_pass::low_pass(seconds time_constant) noexcept` stores `tau_`; `float low_pass::apply(float target, seconds dt) noexcept` returns filtered output; `void low_pass::reset(float value) noexcept` primes `state_`; `void low_pass::reset() noexcept` clears `primed_`.

## Behavior

`apply` bypasses smoothing when `tau_ <= 0`, adopts `target` on the first sample, then computes `alpha = clamp(1 - exp(-dt/tau), 0, 1)` and updates `state_`; `<cmath>` supplies `exp`, `<algorithm>` supplies `clamp`.

entries.response:
**filter.hpp does frame-time-independent exponential smoothing for gamepad aim input.**

## Interface

`low_pass(seconds time_constant) noexcept` constructs a one-pole filter.

`apply(float target, seconds dt) noexcept` advances toward `target` using actual `dt`, returning `float`.

`reset(float value) noexcept` primes `low_pass` at `value`; `reset() noexcept` unprimes it.

`value() const noexcept` returns current `float state_`.

## Behavior

`low_pass` derives smoothing from `tau_`; larger `time_constant` smooths more, while zero passes input through. `reset()` causes the next `apply()` to adopt `target` exactly; `reset(float)` blends the next sample from `value`. `state_` defaults to `0.0f`, and `primed_` defaults to `false`.

## Coupling

`seconds` comes from `support/types.hpp` and timing utilities from `support/utility.hpp`; `clock.hpp` supplies controller clock types.

entries.response:
**integrator.hpp does frame-time-independent aim turn-rate integration with controlled acceleration/deceleration.**

## API

- `turn_integrator::limits` stores `deg_per_s2 accel` and `deg_per_s2 decel`; zero means instantaneous snapping.
- `turn_integrator::advance(deg_per_s target, const limits&, seconds dt) noexcept` ramps `current_` toward `target`, returning trapezoid-integrated `degrees`.
- `turn_integrator::current() const noexcept -> deg_per_s` returns the current rate.
- `turn_integrator::reset() noexcept` sets `current_` to `0 deg/s`.

## Design

`turn_integrator` uses piecewise-linear rate ramps, limiting acceleration/deceleration independently while preserving subdivision-invariant angle integration. `current_` is the sole mutable state.

## Dependencies

`types.hpp` and `utility.hpp` supply controller units/helpers; `clock.hpp` supplies `seconds`; `aim/types.hpp` supplies `degrees`, `deg_per_s`, and `deg_per_s2`.

**deadzone.cpp validates and applies aim-stick deadzone transforms.**

## API

- `validate(const deadzone_params& p, string& why) noexcept -> bool` checks `inner.value`, `outer.value`, and `anti.value` in `[0, 1)`, then requires `inner.value < 1.0f - outer.value`; failures set exact messages: `"inner deadzone must be in [0, 1)"`, `"outer deadzone must be in [0, 1)"`, `"anti-deadzone must be in [0, 1)"`, `"inner deadzone must be below (1 - outer deadzone)"`.

entries.response:
**normalize.cpp does controller stick, trigger, and motion calibration.**

## API

`apply(const profile& p, const raw_sample& raw, canonical_sample& canonical) noexcept` mutates `canonical` using calibration data from `p` and `raw`.

## Calibration behavior

- `apply` processes `stick_count` `stick_sample` entries using `stick_calibration::center_x`, `center_y`, `range_x`, and `range_y`.
- `apply` clamps stick coordinates to `[-1.0f, 1.0f]`, radial-normalizes magnitude above `1.0f`, and snaps magnitude `<= c.drift_threshold` to `{0.0f, 0.0f}` before assigning `stick_sample::calibrated`.
- `apply` rescales `trigger_count` `trigger_sample::normalized` values using `trigger_calibration::min` and `max`, clamps results to `[0.0f, 1.0f]`, and falls back to the driver value when `max - min <= 0.0f`.
- `apply` copies `raw.motion` into `motion_sample`, subtracts `motion_calibration::gyro_bias` and `accel_bias`, then multiplies by `gyro_scale` and `accel_scale`.
- `apply` assigns `canonical.motion` only when `raw.motion` is present.

## Dependencies

`std::sqrt` performs stick magnitude calculation; `std::clamp` enforces stick and trigger bounds; `profile`, `raw_sample`, `canonical_sample`, and calibration/sample types come from `normalize.hpp`.

**graph.cpp validates and evaluates gamepad aim response graphs.**

## Interface

- `aim_graph::make(span<const knot> ks, bool require_monotonic, string& why) -> optional<aim_graph>` constructs a graph or returns `nullopt`, writing validation failure text to `why`.
- `aim_graph::evaluate(float input) const noexcept -> float` saturates outside the knot domain and linearly interpolates within it.

## Validation Contracts

- `aim_graph::make` requires 2–`max_graph_knots` knots, finite `knot::input`/`knot::output` values, strictly increasing `knot::input` values, and inputs within `[0, 1]`.
- `aim_graph::make` sets `aim_graph::monotonic_` when outputs are non-decreasing; `require_monotonic` rejects decreasing outputs.
- `aim_graph::make` emits exact diagnostics: `"an aim graph requires at least two knots"`, `"an aim graph has too many knots"`, `"aim graph knot values must be finite"`, `"aim graph knot inputs must lie in [0, 1]"`, `"aim graph knot inputs must be strictly increasing"`, and `"a monotonic aim graph requires non-decreasing outputs"`.

## Evaluation Invariants

- `aim_graph::evaluate` assumes `knot_count_ >= 2` and strictly increasing inputs, guarded with `assert`.
- `aim_graph::evaluate` returns the first/last `knot::output` for inputs outside the domain and computes `a.output + (b.output - a.output) * t` for segment interpolation.
- `std::isfinite` performs numeric validation; `assert` enforces construction invariants.

**graph.hpp defines allocation-free validated piecewise-linear aim response graphs.**

## API

- `knot` stores `float input` and `float output`.
- `max_graph_knots` is `inline constexpr size_t` `16`.
- `aim_graph::make(span<const knot>, bool require_monotonic, string& why)` returns `optional<aim_graph>`; invalid data yields `nullopt` and a precise `why`.
- `aim_graph::evaluate(float) const noexcept` linearly interpolates, exactly preserves knot outputs, and saturates beyond endpoints.
- `aim_graph::knots() const noexcept` returns `span<const knot>` over initialized knots.
- `aim_graph::monotonic() const noexcept` returns whether outputs are non-decreasing.

## Invariants

`aim_graph` accepts 2–16 knots, finite values, inputs in `[0,1]`, strictly increasing inputs, and optionally non-decreasing outputs; `evaluate` relies on these asserted invariants for deterministic, numerically stable positive-span segments.

## Integration

`types.hpp` supplies `optional`, `span`, `string`, `array`, and `size_t`; `utility.hpp` supplies supporting utilities. `aim_graph` stores knots inline, avoiding allocations.

entries.response:
**types.hpp defines dimension-safe aim-domain scalar and vector types.**

## Types and conversions

- `pi` is `inline constexpr float` equal to `3.14159265358979323846f`.
- `degrees` wraps `float value`, supports `+`, binary/unary `-`, scalar `*`, defaulted `==`, and `std::partial_ordering <=>`.
- `radians` wraps `float value`; `to_radians(degrees) noexcept -> radians` and `to_degrees(radians) noexcept -> degrees` convert using `pi` and 180-degree factors.
- `deg_per_s` wraps `float value`, supports scalar `*`, `+`, defaulted `==`, and `std::partial_ordering <=>`.
- `deg_per_s2` wraps `float value`; `operator*(deg_per_s2, seconds) noexcept -> deg_per_s` integrates angular acceleration over `seconds::count()`.
- `operator*(deg_per_s, seconds) noexcept -> degrees` integrates turn rate over a timestep.
- `axis_input` wraps signed normalized `float value`; `sign() const noexcept -> float` returns `1.0f` for nonnegative values and `-1.0f` otherwise, while `absolute() const noexcept -> float` returns magnitude.
- `magnitude` wraps nonnegative normalized `float value`.
- `screen_vector` contains `float x, y`; `world_vector` contains `float x, y, z`, enforcing screen/world-space separation.
- `dot(world_vector, world_vector) noexcept -> float` computes `x*x + y*y + z*z`.

## Integration and contracts

- `seconds` comes from `component/gamepad/controller/clock.hpp`; support definitions come from `component/gamepad/controller/support/types.hpp` and `utility.hpp`.
- `ostream& operator<<(ostream&, degrees)` and `ostream& operator<<(ostream&, deg_per_s)` are declared for stream formatting and defined elsewhere.
- `degrees` and `deg_per_s` use partial ordering because `float` comparisons must represent NaN; all arithmetic and conversion functions are `constexpr noexcept`.
- `degrees`, `deg_per_s`, and `world_vector` encode dimensional/type boundaries, preventing accidental interchange of angles, rates, normalized inputs, and coordinate spaces.

**measure.cpp computes stick calibration and motion-sensor bias averages.**

## Interface

- `stick_measurer::observe_rest(stick_vector v) noexcept` accumulates rest samples for center estimation.
- `stick_measurer::observe_sweep(stick_vector v) noexcept` tracks absolute axis maxima via `std::fabs`.

- `motion_bias_measurer::finalize(motion_calibration& mc) const noexcept` writes component-wise means when `n_ != 0`; otherwise leaves `mc` unchanged.

entries.response:
**assist.cpp does gamepad aim processing, target lock-on, slowdown scaling, and dominant-axis shaping.**

## Exported symbols

- `aim_processor::aim_processor(config c)` moves `c` into `cfg_` and initializes stateful yaw/pitch acceleration.
- `void aim_processor::reset() noexcept` resets `yaw_` and `pitch_` integrators.
- `aim_frame_output aim_processor::process(const aim_frame_input& in) noexcept` clamps `ads_lerp`, interpolates hip/ADS deadzones and turn rates, applies `apply`, evaluates the configured `graph` or active `curve`, scales by FOV/sensitivity/slowdown, enforces optional `yaw_max`/`pitch_max`, advances acceleration using `in.dt`, and applies pitch inversion.
- `float slowdown_scale(bool target_present, float hip_scale, float ads_scale, float ads_lerp) noexcept` returns `1.0f` without a target; otherwise linearly interpolates scales using clamped `ads_lerp`.
- `stick_vector scale_dominant_axis(stick_vector look) noexcept` preserves the dominant axis and attenuates the subordinate axis by the absolute-magnitude difference; equal axes remain unchanged.
- `aim_frame_output lock_on(const lock_on_target& target, const lock_on_params& params, seconds dt) noexcept` converts relative target/player velocity projected onto view axes into yaw/pitch angular deltas.

## Processing contracts

- `lerp_rate(deg_per_s, deg_per_s, float)` interpolates `.value`; `lerp_deadzone(const deadzone_params&, const deadzone_params&, float)` independently interpolates `inner`, `outer`, and `anti` magnitudes.
- `aim_processor::process` clamps `ads_lerp` to `[0.0f, 1.0f]`, clamps radial `deflection` to `[0.0f, 1.0f]`, and uses `cfg_.ads.curve` when `t >= 0.5f`, otherwise `cfg_.hip.curve`.
- `aim_processor::process` integrates non-negative target speeds before restoring signs, so direction reversal flips at current speed; `invert_pitch` negates the final pitch delta.
- `lock_on` returns `{}` when `target.distance <= 0.0f`; otherwise uses `arc = target.distance * pi` and multiplies projected relative velocity by `180.0f`, axis strength, and `dt.count()`.

## Integration and dependencies

- `assist.cpp` depends on `std_include.hpp`, `component/gamepad/controller/aim/assist.hpp`, `<cmath>`, and `<algorithm>`.
- `aim_processor` couples `deadzone_params`, `stick_vector`, `aim_frame_input`, `aim_frame_output`, `lock_on_target`, `lock_on_params`, `deg_per_s`, `degrees`, `seconds`, `apply`, `evaluate`, `dot`, and acceleration state `yaw_`/`pitch_`.
- `std::lerp`, `std::clamp`, `std::sqrt`, and `std::fabs` define interpolation, bounds, radial magnitude, and sign-independent axis behavior.

**store.hpp persists validated gamepad calibration profiles in per-device files.**

## Interface

`store(const context&, path directory)` binds `context` and storage `directory`; `load(controller::family, optional<uint64_t>) const -> optional<profile>` retrieves a matching profile; `save(const profile&) const -> bool` persists one; `directory() const noexcept -> const path&` exposes `dir_`.

## Behavior

`file_for(controller::family, optional<uint64_t>) const -> path` derives filenames from family and optional `device_key`. `load` rejects malformed content, unsupported versions, invalid profiles, and family/key mismatches; absent files return `nullopt`. `save` writes versioned text profiles, one per file.

`store` depends on `context`, `profile`, `path`, `optional`, `family`, and calibration/controller support types from `context.hpp`, `profile.hpp`, `types.hpp`, and `utility.hpp`.

**aim/assist.hpp does deterministic, stateful gamepad aim processing, slowdown, axis shaping, and velocity-relative lock-on correction.**

## Interface

Namespace: `gamepad::unstable::controller::aim`.

- `aim_profile` stores `deg_per_s yaw_rate`, `deg_per_s pitch_rate`, `deadzone_params deadzone`, and `response_curve curve` for hip-fire/ADS and pitch/yaw contexts.
- `aim_frame_input` carries calibrated `stick_vector look`, `float ads_lerp {0.0f}`, `float fov_scale {1.0f}`, `float sensitivity {1.0f}`, `float slowdown_yaw {1.0f}`, `float slowdown_pitch {1.0f}`, `bool invert_pitch {false}`, optional `deg_per_s yaw_max`, optional `deg_per_s pitch_max`, and `seconds dt {0.0f}`.
- `aim_frame_output` returns `degrees yaw_delta {0.0f}` and `degrees pitch_delta {0.0f}`; positive yaw turns right and positive pre-inversion pitch looks up.
- `aim_processor::config` contains `aim_profile hip`, `aim_profile ads`, `turn_integrator::limits accel`, and nullable `const aim_graph* graph {nullptr}`.
- `aim_processor (config)` constructs the stateful processor; `aim_frame_output process (const aim_frame_input&) noexcept` computes one frame; `void reset () noexcept` clears integrator state.
- `float slowdown_scale (bool target_present, float hip_scale, float ads_scale, float ads_lerp) noexcept` returns the hip/ADS blend when targeting, otherwise `1`.
- `stick_vector scale_dominant_axis (stick_vector look) noexcept` attenuates the subordinate axis by `1 - (greater magnitude - lesser magnitude)`, preserving signs; cardinal input suppresses the weaker axis, while diagonal input remains unchanged.
- `lock_on_target` stores `world_vector target_velocity`, `world_vector player_velocity`, positive-direction `world_vector view_pitch_axis`/`view_yaw_axis`, and `float distance {0.0f}`.
- `lock_on_params` stores `float yaw_strength {0.0f}` and `float pitch_strength {0.0f}`.
- `aim_frame_output lock_on (const lock_on_target&, const lock_on_params&, seconds dt) noexcept` projects relative velocity onto view axes, converts projections into angular rates over `distance`, and integrates them over `dt`; non-positive `distance` produces no adjustment.

## State and contracts

`aim_processor` owns independent `turn_integrator yaw_` and `turn_integrator pitch_`, making acceleration/deceleration persistent across frames and outputs deterministic for fixed config/input sequences. `aim_processor::config::graph` overrides profile-curve shaping when non-null; the pointed `aim_graph` must outlive the processor. `aim_frame_input::ads_lerp` blends hip (`0`) and ADS (`1`) profiles, while `slowdown_yaw` and `slowdown_pitch` use `[0,1]` semantics where `1` means no slowdown. `aim_frame_input::invert_pitch` applies pitch inversion after the positive-up convention. `lock_on_target::view_yaw_axis` must be RIGHT (`+yaw`); callers must negate engine `viewAxis[1]`, which is LEFT.

## Dependencies

`types.hpp` supplies `deg_per_s`, `degrees`, `seconds`, `stick_vector`, `world_vector`, and `optional`; `utility.hpp` supplies shared support utilities. `clock.hpp`, `deadzone.hpp`, `curve.hpp`, `graph.hpp`, `integrator.hpp`, and `sample/axis.hpp` define timing, shaping, graph, integration, and sampled-axis primitives consumed by the declarations.

entries.response:
**validate.cpp does calibration-profile validation for gamepad controllers.**

## Interface

`validate (const profile& p, string& why) noexcept -> bool` rejects invalid `profile` data and writes the first failure reason to `why`.

## Validation Contracts

- `profile::version` must satisfy `1 <= version <= profile::current_version`; error: `"unsupported calibration profile version"`.
- `stick_calibration` fields must be finite; ranges must be `> 0.0f`; `drift_threshold` must be `[0, 1)`; errors identify non-finite values, invalid ranges, or threshold bounds.
- `trigger_calibration` `min`/`max` must be finite with `max > min`.
- `motion` bias/scale fields must be finite.
- `profile::smoothing` must be finite and non-negative.
- `finite(float)` and `finite(const sensor_vec3&)` use `std::isfinite`; `validate` returns `true` only after all checks pass.

entries.response:
**connection.hpp defines transport bindings and the discovered `device_connection` record for gamepad devices.**

## Symbols

- `xinput_binding` stores an XInput `user_index`.
- `hid_binding` stores a HID `wstring path`; path is stable physical identity, while handles open lazily.
- `transport_binding` is `variant<std::monostate, xinput_binding, hid_binding>`; `std::monostate` marks undiscovered/unbound state.
- `same_binding(const transport_binding&, const transport_binding&) noexcept` compares physical attachment identity.
- `device_connection` aggregates `device_id id`, `device_identity identity`, `controller::transport_kind transport`, `connection link`, `capabilities caps`, and `transport_binding binding`.

## Integration

`types.hpp` supplies `user_index`, `wstring`, `transport_kind`, and `connection`; `utility.hpp` supports shared types; `id.hpp`, `identity.hpp`, and `capability.hpp` define device metadata. `device_connection` excludes decoded input/report knowledge; drivers translate reports into samples, while the registry assigns presence-stable `id`.

entries.response:
**discovery reconciles the controller registry with currently reported XInput and HID devices.**

## Interface

- `discovery(const context&, registry&, const transport::xinput_module&)` constructs discovery with shared `context`, mutable `registry`, and XInput transport.
- `void scan()` performs interval-gated reconciliation; suppressed calls only read the clock.
- `void scan_now()` performs unconditional reconciliation for startup or notifications.
- `static constexpr clock::duration interval{chrono::milliseconds(1000)}` defines the 1-second fallback period.

## Behavior

- `scan()` combines `scan_xinput(vector<transport_binding>&)` and `scan_hid(vector<transport_binding>&)`, then `retire_unseen(const vector<transport_binding>&)` removes bindings absent from the current pass.
- `scan_xinput` inspects four XInput user slots; `scan_hid` enumerates present HID gamepad interfaces matching supported USB-family identifiers.
- `discovery` only writes `registry`; `discovery` never opens input devices, decodes reports, or creates drivers.
- `transport::device_notifier notifier_` raises the device-change flag consumed by `scan()`; `scanned_` and `last_scan_` enforce fallback throttling.
- `registry` generation remains unchanged when `scan()` observes the same bindings, preventing downstream work.

**registry.cpp maintains a thread-safe controller-device registry.**

## Interface

- `registry::registry(const context& ctx)` stores `ctx_`.
- `device_id registry::add(device_identity identity, controller::transport_kind t, connection link, capabilities caps, transport_binding binding)` inserts or refreshes a device and returns its `device_id`.
- `bool registry::remove(device_id id)` erases a matching device and reports whether removal succeeded.
- `optional<device_connection> registry::find(device_id id) const` returns a copied device or `nullopt`.
- `void registry::for_each(function_ref<void (const device_connection&)> fn) const` invokes `fn` for each registered device.
- `size_t registry::size() const` returns the device count.

## Behavior and Integration

`add` uses `same_binding` to refresh existing `device_connection` facts in place; new entries use monotonically increasing `next_` IDs, move `binding`, increment `generation_`, and report `device connected: <family> over <transport>/<link>` through `ctx_.report`.

`remove` uses `std::find_if`, increments `generation_`, captures `identity.family`, and reports `device disconnected: <family>` through `ctx_.report`.

`mutex_` guards `devices_`, `find`, `for_each`, and `size`; `add` and `remove` release the lock before `context::report`, while `for_each` executes callbacks under the lock. `generation_` tracks insertion/removal mutations only; refreshes do not increment it.

**registry.hpp defines the thread-safe authoritative registry for attached gamepad devices and stable IDs.**

## Interface

- `registry(const context&)` stores `ctx_` and initializes `next_` to `1`, `generation_` to `0`.
- `device_id add(device_identity, controller::transport_kind, connection, capabilities, transport_binding)` deduplicates equivalent `transport_binding` records, refreshes identity/capabilities, or assigns a never-reused ID; membership changes increment `generation_`.
- `bool remove(device_id)` removes an ID and reports whether removal occurred.
- `optional<device_connection> find(device_id) const` returns a copy, or `nullopt`, remaining valid after `mutex_` release.
- `void for_each(function_ref<void (const device_connection&)>) const` visits records while holding `mutex_`; callbacks must not call `add`, `remove`, `find`, or `size` to avoid deadlock.
- `size_t size() const` returns the current record count.
- `uint64_t generation() const noexcept` atomically loads the membership-change counter.

## State and Integration

`devices_` stores `device_connection` identity/attachment records; `ctx_` supplies controller context; `connection`, `device_identity`, `capabilities`, `transport_binding`, and `controller::transport_kind` come from device/support headers. `mutex_` synchronizes discovery mutations with frame reads, while `generation_` enables atomic unchanged-set checks and avoids per-frame reconciliation copies. Drivers, report decoding, and input samples remain outside `registry`.

**profile.hpp defines versioned per-device gamepad calibration data and family defaults.**

## Public API

- `value_source : uint8_t` distinguishes `built_in`, `measured`, and `user` calibration authority.
- `to_string(value_source) noexcept -> const char*` converts `value_source` to its diagnostic string.
- `stick_calibration` stores normalized stick correction: `center_x/center_y` default `0.0f`, `range_x/range_y` default `1.0f`, and `drift_threshold` default `0.0f`.
- `trigger_calibration` stores normalized trigger travel with `min = 0.0f` and `max = 1.0f`.
- `motion_calibration` stores `sensor_vec3 gyro_bias`, `sensor_vec3 accel_bias`, `gyro_scale = 1.0f`, and `accel_scale = 1.0f`.
- `profile` aggregates `version`, `controller::family family`, optional `uint64_t device_key`, `value_source source`, `array<stick_calibration, stick_count> sticks`, `array<trigger_calibration, trigger_count> triggers`, `motion_calibration motion`, and `smoothing`.
- `profile::current_version` is `uint16_t{1}`; `profile::version` defaults to `current_version`, `family` to `controller::family::unknown`, `source` to `value_source::built_in`, and `smoothing` to `0.0f`.
- `default_profile(controller::family) noexcept -> profile` returns the compiled-in `value_source::built_in` calibration for a controller family.

## Calibration Contracts

- `stick_calibration` operates on driver-normalized coordinates (up/right positive, nominally `[-1, 1]`), correcting resting-center drift and travel range; `drift_threshold` treats residual calibrated magnitude as rest.
- `trigger_calibration` operates in normalized `[0, 1]` space and narrows measured resting/full-press travel.
- `motion_calibration` subtracts `gyro_bias`/`accel_bias` before scaling raw counts into gyro rad/s and accelerometer standard gravities.
- `profile::device_key` optionally binds calibration to one physical device; `profile::version` rejects unsupported serialized formats; `profile::smoothing == 0.0f` disables smoothing.

## Dependencies

`types.hpp` supplies `optional`, `array`, `sensor_vec3`, `stick_count`, and `trigger_count`; `utility.hpp`, `identity.hpp`, `axis.hpp`, `trigger.hpp`, and `motion.hpp` supply controller-family, device, and sample-domain types.

entries.response:
**identity.hpp classifies HID controller identities and defines USB ID value types, families, and known identifiers.**

## Public API

- `vendor_id`: `constexpr explicit vendor_id(uint16_t) noexcept`, `constexpr uint16_t value() const noexcept`, and defaulted `constexpr operator==(vendor_id, vendor_id) noexcept`.
- `product_id`: `constexpr explicit product_id(uint16_t) noexcept`, `constexpr uint16_t value() const noexcept`, and defaulted `constexpr operator==(product_id, product_id) noexcept`.
- `family`: `enum class family : uint8_t` with `unknown`, `xbox`, `dualshock4`, `dualsense`, and `dualsense_edge`.
- `to_string(family) noexcept`: returns `const char*`.
- `operator<<(ostream&, family)`: serializes `family` to `ostream&`.
- `vendor_sony` and `vendor_microsoft`: inline `constexpr vendor_id` values `0x054C` and `0x045E`.
- `product_ds4_gen1`, `product_ds4_gen2`, `product_ds4_dongle`, `product_dualsense`, and `product_dualsense_edge`: inline `constexpr product_id` values `0x05C4`, `0x09CC`, `0x0BA0`, `0x0CE6`, and `0x0DF2`.
- `device_identity`: aggregates `family family{family::unknown}`, `optional<vendor_id> vendor`, `optional<product_id> product`, and `optional<uint16_t> release`.
- `classify(vendor_id, product_id) noexcept`: returns `family`, yielding `family::unknown` for unsupported USB pairs.

## Contracts and Coupling

`family` selects the native decoder and HID report model; `xbox`, `dualshock4`, `dualsense`, and `dualsense_edge` are distinct decoding contracts. `device_identity` excludes connection and transport, allowing one identity across USB and Bluetooth; `release` is optional USB BCD revision data used only for hardware disambiguation. `types.hpp` supplies `uint16_t`, `uint8_t`, `optional`, and `ostream`; `utility.hpp` supplies shared support definitions.

entries.response:
**store.cpp persists and restores validated gamepad controller calibration profiles in deterministic `.cal` files.**

## Interface

- `store::store(const context& ctx, path directory)` stores `ctx_` and moves `directory` into `dir_`.
- `store::file_for(controller::family family, optional<uint64_t> device_key) const -> path` maps profiles to `controller-<family>.cal` or `controller-<family>-<16-digit lowercase hex key>.cal`.
- `store::save(const profile& p) const -> bool` validates and serializes `p`, returning stream success.
- `store::load(controller::family family, optional<uint64_t> device_key) const -> optional<profile>` parses, validates, identity-checks, and returns a profile or `nullopt`.

## File Format

- `magic` is the exact header token `"gamepad-controller-calibration"`; the first line is `<magic> <version>`.
- `save` emits `family <int>`, `source <int>`, and `device_key <0|1> <uint64_t>`.
- `save` emits `stick <index> <center_x> <center_y> <range_x> <range_y> <drift_threshold>` for every `stick_count` entry.
- `save` emits `trigger <index> <min> <max>` for every `trigger_count` entry.
- `save` emits `motion <gyro_bias.x> <gyro_bias.y> <gyro_bias.z> <accel_bias.x> <accel_bias.y> <accel_bias.z> <gyro_scale> <accel_scale>`.
- `save` terminates with `smoothing <value>` and sets stream precision to `9` for exact `float` round trips.

## Validation and Errors

- `save` calls `validate(const profile&, string&)`; invalid profiles report `errc::calibration_invalid` at `severity::warning` through `ctx_.report` and return `false`.
- `save` calls `filesystem::create_directories(dir_, ec)` best-effort, while file-open failure reports `errc::transport_failure`.
- `load` treats a missing file as `nullopt` without reporting an error.

entries.response:
**bind.hpp bridges the controller binding model with the engine’s authoritative bind table.**

## Interface

- `bind_bridge(const context&, const dvars&)` stores `context` and `dvars` references.
- `bind_bridge::apply_layout(string_view name) -> void` writes a named layout; unknown names, including `"custom"`, select defaults without changing `gpad_buttonConfig`.
- `bind_bridge::apply_configured_layout() -> void` applies `gpad_buttonConfig`; `"custom"` preserves player bindings during startup restoration.
- `bind_bridge::reapply_layout() -> void` reapplies the layout named by `gpad_buttonConfig`, including controls-reset flow through `bindgpbuttonsconfigs`.
- `bind_bridge::note_manual_rebind() noexcept -> void` marks bindings as no longer represented by a named layout.
- `bind_bridge::command_keys(int client, bool controller_in_use, const char* command, int (&keys_out)[2]) noexcept -> size_t` returns up to two matching keynums, `-1` padded, restricted to the active input-source half of the 256-key space.
- `controller_command_for(const char* command) noexcept -> const char*` maps keyboard commands to controller-equivalent commands.

## Binding Semantics

`bind_bridge` isolates engine keynum lookup from the subsystem layout model, with the engine bind table authoritative; `command_keys` avoids engine-wide first-match behavior that could select a mouse binding before a controller binding.

`migrate_controller_commands()` rewrites legacy controller binds to merged commands: `+activate`/`+reload` → `+usereload`, and `+melee_breath` → `+holdbreath`; the rewrite is idempotent and fixes custom-config gameplay/menu mismatches.

## Dependencies

`types.hpp` supplies `string_view`; `utility.hpp`, `context.hpp`, and `dvar.hpp` support controller types, engine context, and dvar access.

entries.response:
**`id.hpp` defines compact, strongly typed identifiers and classifications for gamepad controller discovery, transport, report framing, and XInput slots.**

## Namespace and Dependencies

`gamepad::unstable::controller` imports `uint8_t`, `uint32_t`, `optional`, `nullopt`, `ostream`, and comparison support from `support/types.hpp` and `support/utility.hpp`.

## Exported Symbols

- `class device_id` wraps a monotonically assigned `uint32_t`; `device_id()` yields value `0`, `explicit device_id(uint32_t) noexcept` constructs raw values, `uint32_t value() const noexcept` reads them, `explicit operator bool() const noexcept` tests nonzero validity, and defaulted `operator==`/`operator<=>` provide equality and strong ordering.
- `inline constexpr device_id no_device{}` is the null-device sentinel; `0` means no device and assigned handles are never reused within a process.
- `ostream& operator<<(ostream&, device_id)` serializes `device_id`.
- `enum class transport_kind : uint8_t` enumerates `unknown`, `xinput`, `raw_input`, and `hid`; `xinput` exposes capabilities only, `raw_input` means Windows `WM_INPUT` HID delivery, and `hid` means direct `HidD_*/ReadFile/WriteFile` access.
- `const char* to_string(transport_kind) noexcept` converts `transport_kind` to text; `ostream& operator<<(ostream&, transport_kind)` streams it.
- `enum class connection : uint8_t` enumerates `unknown`, `usb`, `bluetooth`, and `virtualized`; values describe report framing, not necessarily the physical attachment bus.
- `const char* to_string(connection) noexcept` converts `connection` to text; `ostream& operator<<(ostream&, connection)` streams it.
- `class user_index` represents a validated XInput slot; `static constexpr uint8_t count{4}`, `explicit user_index(uint8_t) noexcept`, `static constexpr optional<user_index> try_from(int) noexcept`, `uint8_t value() const noexcept`, and defaulted equality/strong ordering define its API.
- `class report_id` wraps a numbered HID report byte; `report_id()` defaults to `0`, `explicit report_id(uint8_t) noexcept`, `uint8_t value() const noexcept`, and defaulted equality/strong ordering define its API.

## Behavioral Contracts

`user_index::try_from(int)` returns `nullopt` for `v < 0 || v >= count`; valid slots are `[0, 4)`. `report_id` permits `0`, which denotes an unnumbered but meaningful HID report. Drivers must resolve `connection` framing before decoding or emitting reports.

`static_assert(sizeof(report_id) == 1)`, `static_assert(static_cast<uint8_t>(transport_kind::hid) < 4)`, and `static_assert(static_cast<uint8_t>(connection::virtualized) < 4)` pin wire-facing representation assumptions.

## Maintenance Note

`connection` has a TODO to be renamed `framing`, because `usb`/`bluetooth` identify report layouts rather than reliably identifying the physical bus.

entries.response:
**discovery.cpp does rate-limited XInput/HID controller discovery, registry synchronization, capability classification, and departure cleanup.**

## Public interface

`discovery::discovery(const context& ctx, registry& r, const transport::xinput_module& x)` stores `ctx_`, `registry_`, `xinput_`, and constructs `notifier_`.

`discovery::scan()` consumes device notifications, records `clock::now()`, forces scans on notification, and otherwise rate-limits scans by `interval` after the first pass.

`discovery::scan_now()` scans XInput, conditionally scans HID, then retires bindings absent from the current pass.

`discovery::scan_xinput(vector<transport_binding>& seen)` discovers enabled XInput gamepads across `user_index::count` slots.

`discovery::scan_hid(vector<transport_binding>& seen)` enumerates and registers supported HID devices using `hid_enumeration_entry` data.

`discovery::retire_unseen(const vector<transport_binding>& seen)` removes registry devices whose `transport_binding` no longer matches any current binding.

## Capability classification

`capabilities_for(family f) noexcept` maps hardware families to factual capability bitmasks:

- `family::xbox`: `capability::rumble`
- `family::dualshock4`: gyroscope, accelerometer, touchpad, battery, rumble, light bar
- `family::dualsense`: `dualsense_capabilities`
- `family::dualsense_edge`: `dualsense_capabilities | capability::back_buttons`
- `family::unknown`: empty `capabilities`

`dualsense_capabilities` includes gyroscope, accelerometer, touchpad, battery, microphone button, rumble, haptics, adaptive triggers, light bar, and player LEDs; output capabilities describe hardware support even when drivers withhold reports.

## Discovery and registration

`scan_now()` reserves `seen` capacity as `user_index::count + 4`, scans all XInput slots first, and invokes `scan_hid()` only when `seen.empty()` to avoid duplicate PlayStation HID binds under DS4Windows and synchronous Bluetooth feature exchanges on the game thread.

`scan_xinput()` skips unloaded `xinput_`, queries each slot with `xinput_.get_capabilities(i, XINPUT_FLAG_GAMEPAD, caps)`, accepts only `ERROR_SUCCESS`, and registers `device_identity {family::xbox, nullopt, nullopt, nullopt}` with `transport_kind::xinput`, `connection::unknown`, `capabilities_for(family::xbox)`, and `xinput_binding {slot}`.

`scan_hid()` relies on `transport::enumerate(ctx_)` filtering supported families and known links, asserts `classify(vendor, product) != family::unknown` and `e.link != connection::unknown`, then registers HID identity fields `{family, vendor, product, version}` with `hid_binding {e.path}`.

`retire_unseen()` collects departed `device_id` values under `registry_.for_each()` and removes them afterward because `registry_.remove()` also acquires the registry lock; `std::any_of()` and `same_binding()` define binding presence.

## Integration and invariants

`transport::enumerate`, `transport::hid`, `classify`, `registry`, `device_connection`, `device_identity`, `transport_binding`, `xinput_binding`, `hid_binding`, `connection`, `capabilities`, `clock`, and `notifier_` form the discovery boundary.

`scan_hid()` requires `e.link != connection::unknown`; `scan_xinput()` intentionally records `connection::unknown` because XInput decoding is link-independent.

**netmove.cpp implements XOR-packed gamepad movement deltas.**

## Interface

`move_changed(move_delta, move_delta) noexcept -> bool` compares `forward`/`right`.

`pack_move(move_delta, int) noexcept -> uint16_t` packs signed bytes (`forward` low, `right` high), XORs with `key`, masks `0xFFFF`.

`unpack_move(uint16_t, int) noexcept -> move_delta` reverses XOR packing and reinterprets both bytes as `int8_t`.

`netmove.hpp` declares the `gamepad::unstable::controller::engine` API; `std_include.hpp` supplies common types.

**netmove.hpp implements the pure delta-compression codec for gamepad network movement.**

## Interface

`move_delta` stores `int8_t forward {0}` and `int8_t right {0}`, with `constexpr noexcept operator==`.

`move_changed(move_delta from, move_delta to) noexcept` reports baseline differences.

`pack_move(move_delta to, int key) noexcept -> uint16_t` packs both signed bytes into a 16-bit value XORed with `key`.

`unpack_move(uint16_t packed, int key) noexcept -> move_delta` reverses packing exactly, independent of key high bits.

## Integration

`types.hpp` and `utility.hpp` supply support definitions. `move_delta` and codec functions reside in `gamepad::unstable::controller::engine`; engine hooks call them from `MSG_WriteDeltaUsercmdKey`/`MSG_ReadDeltaUsercmdKey` wiring.

- `void install(runtime& rt)` installs key conversion detours and the mouse-move call hook, stores `active_runtime`, and reports `severity::info`/`facility::engine` with `"QoS controller input hooks installed; native usercmd codec retained"`.

## Key Conversion

- `controller_key_name(int key) noexcept` maps engine keynums through `mapping::key_from_keynum` and returns `mapping::key_name`, or `nullptr`.
- `controller_key_from_name(const char* name) noexcept` maps names through `mapping::key_from_name`, returning the mapped integer or sentinel `-1`; null `name` also returns `-1`.
- `keynum_to_string_stub` and `string_to_keynum_stub` are x86 `__declspec(naked)` fallthrough stubs: mapped values return directly, while unmapped values call originals at `0x103185A0` and `0x10318B80`.

- `mouse_move_body(usercmd_s* cmd, int client)` first invokes native `CL_MouseMove` at `game::game_offset(0x102FC4D0)`, preserving client and aim-assist state, then applies `active_runtime->view().apply_move(client, *cmd, frame_seconds())`.

- `mouse_move_stub` extracts stack arguments and bridges the engine call convention.

- Anonymous state uses `runtime* active_runtime`, two `utils::hook::detour` objects, and original-function pointers; `install` must run before hooked execution.

**import.cpp adapts gamepad controller engine calls to game runtime dvars, input events, timing, and memory-backed aim/view state.**

## Interface

- `Dvar_FindVar(const char* name) noexcept -> dvar_t*` forwards to `game::Dvar_FindVar`.
- `Dvar_RegisterBool(const char*, bool, int, const char*) -> dvar_t*`, `Dvar_RegisterFloat(const char*, float, float, float, int, const char*) -> dvar_t*`, `Dvar_RegisterInt(const char*, int, int, int, int, const char*) -> dvar_t*`, and `Dvar_RegisterString(const char*, const char*, int, const char*) -> dvar_t*` return existing dvars or register through `dvars::Dvar_Register*`, narrowing flags to `std::uint16_t`.
- `Dvar_SetBool(dvar_t*, bool) noexcept` and `Dvar_SetInt(dvar_t*, int) noexcept` synchronize `current`, `latched`, and `reset`; `Dvar_SetString(dvar_t*, const char*) noexcept` calls `game::Dvar_SetString` by `dvar->name`.
- `Sys_Milliseconds() noexcept -> int` returns `GetTickCount()`.
- `menu_or_console_active() noexcept -> bool` checks `game_console::is_active()`, missing/disabled `"cl_ingame"`, and nonzero `*game::keyCatchers`.
- `emit_key(int key, bool down, unsigned time) noexcept` invokes `game::CL_KeyEvent(0, key, down ? 1 : 0, time)`.
- `aim_globals(int client) noexcept -> AimAssistGlobals&`, `view_pitch() noexcept -> float&`, and `view_yaw() noexcept -> float&` expose `game::game_offset` memory.
- `frame_seconds() noexcept -> float` clamps address `0x11255D70` milliseconds to `[0, 200]`, then multiplies by `0.001f`.

## Coupling

`set_value<T>` is an internal template with bool-specific `enabled` assignment and integer assignment otherwise; `game::game_offset` bases client aim state at `0x1149D290`, pitch at `0x11A9FEC0`, and yaw at `0x11A9FEC4`.

entries.response:
**dvar.hpp does define the engine-facing typed dvar registry and null-safe readers for gamepad controller state.**

## Interface

Namespace: `gamepad::unstable::controller::engine`.

- `struct dvars` stores resolved `dvar_t*` handles for enablement (`enabled`, `present`, `in_use`, `rumble`), light-bar channels (`light_bar`, `light_bar_r`, `light_bar_g`, `light_bar_b`), stick shaping, named configs, view/aim, acceleration, and assist behavior.
- `dvars register_dvars(const context&)` registers every controller dvar in fixed order, installs known-working defaults, returns resolved handles, and reports the count through `context`.
- `void publish_present(const dvars&, bool present) noexcept` publishes controller attachment through engine-owned `gpad_present`.
- `bool read(dvar_t*, bool fallback) noexcept` reads `dvar_t::current.enabled`, falling back when the handle is null.
- `float read(dvar_t*, float fallback) noexcept` reads `dvar_t::current.value`, falling back when the handle is null.
- `int read(dvar_t*, int fallback) noexcept` reads `dvar_t::current.integer`, falling back when the handle is null.
- `const char* read(dvar_t*, const char* fallback) noexcept` reads `dvar_t::current.string`, falling back when the handle or string is null.

## Dvar bindings

`enabled`, `present`, `in_use`, and `rumble` correspond to `gpad_enabled`, `gpad_present`, `gpad_in_use`, and `gpad_rumble`; `buttons_config` and `sticks_config` correspond to `gpad_buttonConfig` and `gpad_sticksConfig`.

`invert_pitch`, `view_sensitivity`, `sensitivity_level`, and `aim_assist_enabled` map to `input_invertPitch`, `input_viewSensitivity`, `gpad_sensitivity` (console scale `1-10`), and `sv_allowAimAssist`; `accel_enabled`, `accel_rate`, and `scale_view_axis` map to `aim_accel_turnrate_enabled`, `aim_accel_turnrate_lerp`, and `aim_scale_view_axis`.

## Integration and contract

`types.hpp`, `utility.hpp`, `import.hpp`, and `context.hpp` supply engine types, helpers, imported dvar definitions, and registration-count context coupling.

`register_dvars` establishes defaults matching every `read` fallback; `publish_present` is the sole writer of `gpad_present`, while runtime readers consume engine state through `dvars`. Raw dvar values terminate at this boundary before conversion into typed angles, magnitudes, or durations.

entries.response:
**view.hpp turns calibrated gamepad sticks into movement and view-angle updates.**

## Role

`view_driver` owns latched analog-stick state, persistent aim integration, stick-layout resolution, and controller contributions to `usercmd_s`; `observe()` and `idle()` cover frame sampling, while `apply_move()` and `apply_remote_move()` consume latched state later in command construction.

## Public interface

- `view_driver(const context&, const dvars&)` binds runtime `context` and tuning `dvars`.
- `void observe(const canonical_sample&) noexcept` maps the calibrated sample through `mapping::resolved_axes` and latches virtual movement/view axes.
- `void idle() noexcept` clears `axes_` and resets aim integrators when no controller drives the frame.
- `void apply_move(int client, usercmd_s& cmd, float frame_time) noexcept` adds movement to `forwardmove`/`rightmove`, advances view angles after native `CL_MouseMove`, and accounts for left-handed attack/throw mapping.
- `void apply_remote_move(int client, usercmd_s& cmd) noexcept` folds controller movement into remote-control commands.

## State and algorithms

`axes_` stores the most recent shaped stick vectors, decoupling runtime sampling from later command construction. `calibration_` owns the validated aim response graph referenced by `processor_`; both `optional` values remain empty until a successful build, with invalid tuning falling back to unshaped stick input. `tuning_signature_`, `have_signature_`, and `reported_invalid_` implement cached dvar-change detection and invalid-configuration reporting.

`ensure_processor()` rebuilds the aim processor when tuning changes and returns availability; `view_active(int client) const noexcept` gates view motion while menus, console/chat input, or player freeze are active.

## Integration and contracts

`view_driver` depends on `support/types.hpp`, `support/utility.hpp`, `engine/import.hpp`, `context.hpp`, `dvar.hpp`, `aim/assist.hpp`, `aim/calibration.hpp`, `mapping/stick-layout.hpp`, and `sample/sample.hpp`. `gpad_sticksConfig` selects left/right stick roles, while engine aim-assist globals apply slowdown and lock-on. `apply_move()` and `apply_remote_move()` are explicitly `noexcept`; `apply_move()` receives `frame_time` in seconds.

entries.response:
**driver.hpp defines the polymorphic native gamepad-driver boundary and its poll/output contracts.**

## Interface

- `max_reports_per_poll` — `inline constexpr size_t`, fixed at `32`; bounds reports consumed per device per poll, deferring overflow to the next frame.
- `driver` — abstract per-physical-device Strategy-pattern base; owns family-specific decoding/output across one transport.
- `driver::~driver() = default` — virtual destructor.
- `driver::family() const noexcept -> controller::family` — identifies the decoded native controller family.
- `driver::device() const noexcept -> device_id` — identifies the bound physical device.
- `driver::poll(raw_sample& raw, canonical_sample& canonical) noexcept -> bool` — fills native `raw_sample` and game-facing `canonical_sample`; returns `false` for unchanged XInput packet/no HID report and `true` for new state. Caller supplies acquisition timestamp and per-device sequence.
- `driver::submit(const output_request&) noexcept -> void` — honors supported output requests and reports unsupported ones as `output_rejected`; never emits uncertain reports.

## Integration and Contracts

`types.hpp` supplies controller-family/sample-related types; `utility.hpp`, `device/id.hpp`, `device/identity.hpp`, `sample/sample.hpp`, and `driver/output.hpp` supply utility, identity, sampling, and output dependencies. `driver::poll` and `driver::submit` must not throw across the ABI boundary or allocate; hot per-sample decoding remains non-virtual. `max_reports_per_poll` supports draining high-rate HID queues while retaining the newest reading without frame stalls. `driver` uses dynamic dispatch only once per connected device per engine frame.

entries.response:
**decode.cpp decodes PlayStation controller report fields, verifies CRC-32, maps hats, and normalizes stick coordinates.**

## Interface

- `rd_u8(span<const byte> d, size_t off) noexcept -> uint8_t` reads one byte; `assert(off < d.size())` guards bounds.
- `rd_le16(span<const byte> d, size_t off) noexcept -> uint16_t` reads little-endian 16-bit data with `assert(off + 1 < d.size())`.
- `rd_le16s(span<const byte> d, size_t off) noexcept -> int16_t` converts `rd_le16` to signed form.
- `rd_le32(span<const byte> d, size_t off) noexcept -> uint32_t` reads little-endian 32-bit data with `assert(off + 3 < d.size())`.
- `crc32_le(uint32_t crc, span<const byte> data) noexcept -> uint32_t` computes reflected IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 bit-at-a-time using `reflected_polynomial = 0xEDB88320u`.
- `verify_ps_crc32(uint8_t seed, span<const byte> data, uint32_t expected) noexcept -> bool` seeds CRC with `0xFFFFFFFFu`, processes `seed`, complements the data CRC, and compares against `expected`.
- `decode_touch_point(span<const byte> p) noexcept -> ps_touch_point` requires `p.size() >= 4`; decodes contact activity/ID plus packed 12-bit `x` and `y`.
- `apply_hat(button_set& s, uint8_t hat) noexcept -> void` maps hat values `0..7` clockwise from up to `button::dpad_*`; values `>= 8` leave state unchanged.
- `normalize_ps_stick(uint8_t x, uint8_t y) noexcept -> stick_vector` maps byte coordinates around `(128,128)` to clamped `[-1,1]`, inverts Y, and radially clamps magnitude to `1.0f`.

## Coupling and Contracts

`decode.cpp` depends on `decode.hpp` for `byte`, `span`, `ps_touch_point`, `button_set`, `button`, and `stick_vector`, plus `<cassert>`, `<algorithm>`, and `<cmath>`. `crc32_le` favors auditability over lookup-table speed for reports up to 78 bytes; `verify_ps_crc32` requires the device’s reflected CRC convention and standard polynomial. `decode_touch_point` interprets `contact & 0x80u == 0` as active and `contact & 0x7Fu` as ID. `normalize_ps_stick` uses `127.0f` scale, preserving endpoint clamping and diagonal normalization.

entries.response:
**key.hpp translates canonical controller samples into IW4 engine key events.**

## Role and integration

`gamepad::unstable::controller::engine` couples `canonical_sample` input with `context`, `dvars`, `dvar_t`, and `mapping::engine_key`; `key_dispatcher` reproduces `CL_KeyEvent` routing without misclassifying controller input as keyboard input.

`local_client` is `inline constexpr int {0}`, selecting IW4’s sole PC local client for key state, catchers, and menus.

## Public interface

`key_dispatcher(const context&, const dvars&)` stores references to engine context and dvar handles; `g_useholdtime` remains unresolved until runtime registration.

`dispatch(const canonical_sample&) noexcept` performs sample-to-sample edge detection, emits button and stick-direction events, updates controller ownership, and applies menu/scoreboard/UI/binding routing.

`release_all() noexcept` releases every latched controller key through the physical-release path, preventing actions from remaining active after device removal.

`in_use() const noexcept -> bool` reports whether controller input currently owns the active input source.

`note_other_input() noexcept` clears controller ownership after keyboard or mouse activity.

## Event and state model

`key_event` distinguishes `pressed`, `repeated`, and `released`; `repeated` drives held d-pad/menu scrolling while non-menu keys generally repeat only on their initial press.

`buttons_` stores the previous `button_set`; `deflected_` and `was_deflected_` track negative/positive stick states across `axis_count == 4` axes ordered right-x, right-y, left-x, left-y.

`dispatch_apad(unsigned time) noexcept` synthesizes `APAD_*` and `RSTICK_*` direction keys from latched deflection, including sticks already held when a menu opens.

`dispatch_buttons(const canonical_sample&, unsigned time) noexcept` converts canonical button state into engine keys; `emit_button(mapping::engine_key, key_event, unsigned time) noexcept` marks controller usage and refreshes menu scrolling before `emit(mapping::engine_key, key_event, unsigned time) noexcept` performs common event routing.

`ignore_repeat(mapping::engine_key, int repeats, unsigned time) noexcept` filters repeats; `reset_scroll(mapping::engine_key, bool down, unsigned time) noexcept` manages repeat timing; `menu_key_event(mapping::engine_key, bool down) noexcept` and `scoreboard_key_event(mapping::engine_key) noexcept` forward catcher-specific events.

`next_scroll_`, `scroll_hold_start_`, and `scroll_hold_key_` schedule accelerating held d-pad/trigger repeats in engine milliseconds.

## Runtime contracts

`apply_use_hold_time() noexcept` synchronizes `g_useholdtime` with controller ownership: combined `+usereload` reloads on tap and uses on hold only when hold time is positive, while the engine default `0` otherwise causes immediate use.

`use_hold_time_` is a lazily resolved `dvar_t*`; `reported_deadzone_` suppresses duplicate invalid-deadzone reports because stick deadzone dvars are validated on every read.

`set_in_use(bool) noexcept` maintains input-source transitions, and `dispatch(const canonical_sample&) noexcept` must receive every device sample; callers must invoke `release_all() noexcept` when the device disappears.

entries.response:
**view.cpp does gamepad view/movement processing, aim calibration, target assistance, and user-command mutation.**

## Interface

- `view_driver::view_driver(const context& ctx, const dvars& d)` stores `ctx_` and `dvars_`.
- `bool view_driver::ensure_processor()` rebuilds cached aim calibration and processor state when dvar tuning changes.
- `void view_driver::observe(const canonical_sample& sample) noexcept` resolves calibrated left/right sticks through `mapping::stick_layout_from_name`, `mapping::resolve`, and resets invalid axes.
- `void view_driver::idle() noexcept` clears `axes_` and resets `processor_`.
- `bool view_driver::view_active(int) const noexcept` returns `!menu_or_console_active()`.
- `void view_driver::apply_move(int client, usercmd_s& cmd, float frame_time) noexcept` applies movement, aim processing, slowdown, lock-on, and clamped view deltas.
- `void view_driver::apply_remote_move(int, usercmd_s&) noexcept` intentionally performs no work.

## Aim Processor Lifecycle

- `tuning_signature(const dvars& d)` hashes yaw/pitch turn rates, deadzones, acceleration, and `accel_enabled` using `result = result * 31u + std::hash<float>{}(value)`.
- `make_profile(const dvars& d, float yaw, float pitch)` creates linear `aim_profile` values with `deg_per_s` rates, `deadzone_params`, and `response_curve{curve_kind::linear, 1.0f}`.
- `ensure_processor()` uses hip defaults `260.0f/90.0f`, ADS defaults `90.0f/55.0f`, deadzone defaults `0.2f/0.01f`, acceleration default `1200.0f`, and disables acceleration when `accel_enabled` is false.
- `ensure_processor()` clamps `view_sensitivity` to `[0.01f, 30.0f]`, `sensitivity_level` to `[1, 10]`, and scales level by `/ 5.0f`.
- `ensure_processor()` deliberately clears `settings.graph_knots` and sets `settings.graph_monotonic = false` because QoS stores dvar pointers at `0x1149E108`; invalid calibration reports `severity::warning`, `facility::aim`, `errc::graph_invalid`, and `"aim configuration rejected (" + reason + ")"`.

## Movement and View Behavior

- `clamp_move(int value) noexcept` clamps command axes to `[-128, 127]`; `move_scale` is `127.0f`.
- `apply_move()` adds rounded `axes_.forward` and `axes_.side` contributions to `cmd.forwardmove` and `cmd.rightmove`, then exits when `view_active(client)` or `ensure_processor()` fails.
- `apply_move()` clamps `frame_time` to `[0.0f, 0.05f]`, optionally applies `scale_dominant_axis`, and constructs `aim_frame_input` with `adsLerp`, `sensitivity_scale`, `invert_pitch`, and `seconds{frame_time}`.
- `apply_move()` enables slowdown only when aim assist, initialized globals, `slowdown_enabled`, and `best_target()` all succeed; slowdown uses `slowdown_scale(true, 0.4f, 0.5f, globals.adsLerp)`.
- `best_target()` rejects `screenTargetCount` outside `[0, 64]`, requires finite positive `distSqr`, checks range `8192.0f * max(range_scale, 0.0f)`, and tests `clipMins`/`clipMaxs` with `in_region()`.
- `apply_move()` enables lock-on only when `lockon_enabled` is true and `hypot(look.x, look.y) <= lockon_deflection` (default `0.05f`); strengths default to yaw `0.6f` and pitch `0.0f`.
- `apply_move()` accepts only finite `lock_on()` corrections and processor deltas, subtracts deltas from `view_yaw()`/`view_pitch()`, and clamps pitch to `[-85.0f, 85.0f]`.

## Integration and Safety

- `view_driver` couples `context`, `dvars`, `canonical_sample`, `usercmd_s`, `aim_globals`, `AimAssistGlobals`, `aim_calibration`, `turn_integrator`, `mapping`, `slowdown_scale`, and `lock_on`.
- `reported_invalid_` suppresses repeated invalid-configuration warnings; `processor_` and `calibration_` are reset before failed rebuilds.
- `observe()` and `apply_move()` use finite-value guards; `apply_move()` is synchronous and `noexcept` at its command-processing boundary.

entries.response:
**dualsense.hpp decodes DualSense HID reports and defines the first-class DualSense driver.**

## Interface

`decode_dualsense(span<const byte>, connection, raw_sample&, canonical_sample&, bool edge = false) noexcept -> bool` validates and decodes USB report `0x01` (64 bytes) or Bluetooth report `0x31` (78 bytes), leaving outputs untouched on framing, length, or CRC-32 failure.

`dualsense_driver(const context&, transport::hid_device&, device_id)` constructs the driver; `family() const noexcept -> controller::family` returns `controller::family::dualsense`; `device() const noexcept -> device_id` returns `device_`; `poll(raw_sample&, canonical_sample&) noexcept -> bool` reads and decodes input; `submit(const output_request&) noexcept -> void` submits output requests.

`read_and_decode(raw_sample&, canonical_sample&, bool edge) noexcept -> bool` shares HID read/decode logic with the Edge driver and enables Edge handling when `edge` is true.

## Behavioral contracts

`decode_dualsense` selects report framing from `connection`; Bluetooth CRC-32 is checked before field access. `edge` decodes rear-button bits `buttons[2]` bits `4..7` and records back-button capability; standard DualSense leaves those bits uninterpreted.

`dualsense_driver` tracks `ctx_`, `hid_`, `device_`, and `link_`; `bt_output_sequence_` is a per-device Bluetooth output counter wrapping at 16 and unused over USB. `minimal_reported_` suppresses repeated diagnostics for minimal Bluetooth reports.

## Coupling

`decode_dualsense` depends on `types.hpp`, `utility.hpp`, `context.hpp`, `driver.hpp`, and `transport::hid`; DualSense and Edge share `hid-playstation.c`’s `struct dualsense_input_report`. Output for haptics, adaptive triggers, and LEDs remains withheld pending verified report encoding.

`decode_dualshock4` depends on `span`, `byte`, `connection`, `raw_sample`, `canonical_sample`, and PlayStation HID field layouts corresponding to `dualshock4_input_report_common` and USB/Bluetooth wrappers.

entries.response:
**key.cpp does gamepad-to-engine key translation, menu scrolling, fallback command dispatch, and controller-use state management.**

## Role and Integration

`gamepad::unstable::controller::engine::key_dispatcher` consumes `canonical_sample`, applies stick deadzones, tracks button/axis transitions, and emits engine key events through `emit_key`. It couples `context::report` with `severity::warning`, `facility::mapping`, and `errc::calibration_invalid`; `dvars` supplies runtime thresholds and controller-use state; `mapping::engine_key`, `mapping::to_engine_key`, `mapping::apad_input`, `mapping::axis_deflected`, and `mapping::all_engine_keys` define engine mappings; `aim::validate` and `aim::apply` perform deadzone validation and calibration.

## Public Interface

- `key_dispatcher::key_dispatcher (const context& ctx, const dvars& d)` stores immutable `context` and `dvars` references.
- `void key_dispatcher::set_in_use (bool value) noexcept` changes controller-use state, updates `dvars_.in_use`, and invokes `apply_use_hold_time`.
- `void key_dispatcher::apply_use_hold_time () noexcept` lazily finds `"g_useholdtime"` and sets it to `250` while `in_use_` is true, otherwise `0`.
- `void key_dispatcher::note_other_input () noexcept` clears controller-use state through `set_in_use (false)`.
- `void key_dispatcher::dispatch (const canonical_sample& sample) noexcept` validates/applies stick deadzones, updates hysteretic axis deflection state, detects controller activity, dispatches sticks and buttons, then snapshots `sample.buttons`.
- `void key_dispatcher::dispatch_apad (unsigned time) noexcept` translates left/right-stick directional deflections into `pressed`, `repeated`, or `released` `key_event` values, suppressing stick input outside menus/consoles.
- `void key_dispatcher::dispatch_buttons (const canonical_sample& sample, unsigned time) noexcept` compares current buttons against `buttons_`, emitting transitions and held repeats for D-pad and triggers.
- `void key_dispatcher::emit_button (engine_key key, key_event event, unsigned time) noexcept` marks controller use, resets menu scroll state for non-repeat button events, and delegates to `emit`.
- `void key_dispatcher::emit (engine_key key, key_event event, unsigned time) noexcept` translates menu keys to `K_*` events, emits gameplay engine keys below `0xE0`, and queues fallback commands when `engine_binding` is empty.
- `bool key_dispatcher::ignore_repeat (engine_key key, int repeats, unsigned time) noexcept` implements menu repeat timing and D-pad acceleration, returning whether a repeat should be suppressed.
- `void key_dispatcher::reset_scroll (engine_key key, bool down, unsigned time) noexcept` initializes or clears scroll-hold tracking and schedules the first repeat.
- `void key_dispatcher::menu_key_event (engine_key key, bool down)` translates `engine_key` to menu keycodes using the current millisecond timestamp.
- `bool key_dispatcher::scoreboard_key_event (engine_key) noexcept` always returns `false`.
- `void key_dispatcher::release_all () noexcept` releases every `mapping::all_engine_keys` entry, clears button/deflection state, and resets scroll ownership.

## Mapping and Fallback Contracts

`button_keys[]` maps `face_west→button_x`, `face_south→button_a`, `face_east→button_b`, `face_north→button_y`, `l2→button_ltrig`, `r2→button_rtrig`, `l1→button_lshldr`, `r1→button_rshldr`, `start→button_start`, `back→button_back`, `l3→button_lstick`, `r3→button_rstick`, and all four D-pad directions to matching `engine_key` values.

`menu_key` maps `button_a`/`button_start` to `K_ENTER`, `button_b`/`button_back` to `K_ESCAPE`, and D-pad/apad/rstick directions to `K_UPARROW`, `K_DOWNARROW`, `K_LEFTARROW`, or `K_RIGHTARROW`; unsupported keys return `0`.

`fallback_command` maps gameplay keys to `"+gostand"`, `"+stance"`, `"+usereload"`, `"weapnext"`, `"+speed_throw"`, `"+attack"`, `"+smoke"`, `"+frag"`, `"togglemenu"`, `"+scores"`, `"+breath_sprint"`, `"+melee"`, and D-pad `"+actionslot 1"` through `"+actionslot 4"`.

`engine_binding` reads the game binding table at `game::game_offset (0x11263624 + keynum * 12)` for key values `[0,255]`; invalid values return `nullptr`.

`queue_fallback` formats held commands as `"%s %d %u\n"` and released `+commands` as `"-%s %d %u\n"`; one-shot commands format as `"%s\n"` only on press, then call `game::Cbuf_AddText (0, text)`.

## Timing, Thresholds, and State

`scroll_delay_first`, `scroll_delay_rest`, `scroll_delay_min`, `scroll_accel_time`, and `controller_use_hold_time` equal `420`, `210`, `50`, `1500`, and `250` milliseconds respectively. `dispatch` reads default stick deadzone values `0.2f` and `0.01f`, button deadzone `0.13f`, pressed threshold `0.4f`, and hysteresis `0.1f`. `ignore_repeat` accelerates D-pad repeats linearly from `210` toward `50` over `1500` ms while preserving a first-repeat delay of `420` ms.

`dispatch` reports `"invalid stick deadzone; using defaults"` once per dispatcher via `reported_deadzone_`; `release_all` is the lifecycle reset boundary for buttons, axis hysteresis, and scroll state.

**output.hpp defines device-neutral gamepad output requests for controller drivers.**

## Interface

- `rumble_request` — aggregate with `float low_frequency` and `float high_frequency`, both default `0.0f`, normalized to `[0, 1]`.
- `light_bar_request` — RGB aggregate with `uint8_t red`, `green`, `blue`, each default `0`.
- `player_led_request` — aggregate with `uint8_t mask` default `0`; low five bits select LEDs.
- `trigger_effect` — `enum class trigger_effect : uint8_t` with `off`, `feedback`, `weapon`, `vibration`.
- `adaptive_trigger_request` — aggregate with `trigger_side side` (default `trigger_side::left`), `trigger_effect effect` (default `trigger_effect::off`), `uint8_t start_position`, `end_position`, `strength` (all default `0`); positions use `0..9`, strength uses `0..8`.
- `output_request` — `variant<rumble_request, light_bar_request, player_led_request, adaptive_trigger_request>` selecting exactly one driver operation.

## Integration

`output_request` depends on `variant` from `component/gamepad/controller/support/types.hpp` and `trigger_side` from `component/gamepad/controller/sample/trigger.hpp`; `utility.hpp` supplies shared support definitions.

`adaptive_trigger_request` remains device-neutral, while drivers encode raw trigger-effect bytes; `output_request` intentionally excludes raw-report alternatives, requiring drivers to reject unsupported request variants.

entries.response:
**playstation.cpp enables enhanced PlayStation Bluetooth reports and identifies minimal Bluetooth input reports.**

## API

- `enable_extended_reports(const context& ctx, transport::hid_device& hid, device_id device, family device_family) noexcept -> bool` requests DualSense/DualSense Edge serial (`ds_feature_serial`), firmware (`ds_feature_firmware`), then calibration (`ps_feature_calibration`); other families request calibration only and report `severity::warning`/`errc::transport_failure` on failure.
- `minimal_bluetooth_report(span<const byte> r, connection link) noexcept -> bool` returns true only for nonempty Bluetooth reports whose byte 0 equals `ps_report_bt_minimal`.

## Protocol Contracts

- `ps_feature_calibration` is `0x05`; `ds_feature_serial` is `0x09`; `ds_feature_firmware` is `0x20`; `ps_feature_calibration_size` is `41`; `max_feature_size` is `128`; `ps_report_bt_minimal` is `0x01`.
- `read_feature(transport::hid_device& hid, uint8_t report) noexcept -> bool` clamps `hid.feature_report_length()` to `[ps_feature_calibration_size, max_feature_size]`, writes the report ID at buffer index `0`, and calls `hid.get_feature`.
- `enable_extended_reports` treats successful feature reads as a transport side effect that activates enhanced Bluetooth input; failure leaves the controller inactive.

## Coupling

- `transport::hid_device` supplies feature-report length and retrieval; `context::report` emits diagnostics; `rd_u8` from `driver/decode.hpp` parses report bytes.
- `family::dualsense` and `family::dualsense_edge` select the DualSense request sequence; `connection::bluetooth` gates minimal-report detection.

**binding.hpp defines `mapping::binding_table` and `apply_button_layout` for engine-key-to-command bindings.**

## Interface

- `binding_table::bind(engine_key, string)` assigns a command; `binding_table::bind(engine_key, action)` assigns a logical action’s command.
- `binding_table::unbind(engine_key) noexcept` clears one binding; `binding_table::clear() noexcept` clears all bindings.
- `binding_table::command_for(engine_key) const noexcept` returns `const string*`, or `nullptr` when unbound.
- `binding_table::for_each(function_ref<void (engine_key, const string&)>) const` visits bound keys in engine-key order.
- `binding_table::size() const noexcept` returns the number of bound keys.
- `apply_button_layout(binding_table&, string_view)` clears and populates named layouts: `gamepad_default`, `tactical`, `lefty`, `nomad`, `_alt`; unknown names fall back to default.

## Representation and Dependencies

`binding_table::commands_` is `array<string, binding_table::count>`, indexed by `mapping::key_index`; `binding_table::count` equals `engine_key_count`, and empty strings represent unbound keys. `types.hpp` supplies `string`, `string_view`, `array`, `size_t`, and `function_ref`; `key.hpp` supplies `engine_key`; `logical.hpp` supplies `action`.

**xinput.hpp decodes XInput states and defines the Xbox-class controller driver.**

## Interface

- `decode_xinput(const XINPUT_GAMEPAD&, bool has_guide, raw_sample&, canonical_sample&) noexcept` converts XInput state into raw and canonical samples; `has_guide` controls guide-button observability.
- `xinput_driver(const context&, const transport::xinput_module&, device_id, user_index)` constructs a borrowed-module, borrowed-slot driver.
- `xinput_driver::family() const noexcept` returns `controller::family::xbox`.
- `xinput_driver::device() const noexcept` returns `device_id device_`.
- `xinput_driver::poll(raw_sample&, canonical_sample&) noexcept` performs packet-based state polling.
- `xinput_driver::submit(const output_request&) noexcept` submits dual-motor rumble output.

## State and Integration

`xinput_driver` inherits `driver`, references `context`, `xinput_module`, `device_id`, and `user_index`, and tracks per-instance change detection via `uint32_t last_packet_ {0}` plus `bool have_packet_ {false}`. `decode_xinput` preserves XInput-specific analog triggers, guide-button support, packet numbers, and Xbox button semantics; PlayStation devices require separate drivers. `types.hpp`, `utility.hpp`, `context.hpp`, `driver.hpp`, and `xinput-module.hpp` define the coupled sample, runtime, and transport APIs.

entries.response:
**set.hpp manages live gamepad drivers and their HID/XInput resources.**

## Interface

- `set(const context&, const transport::xinput_module&)` initializes non-owning runtime dependencies; `~set()` destroys bound entries.
- `set` is non-copyable via deleted `set(const set&)` and `operator=(const set&)`.
- `reconcile(const registry&) -> void` creates drivers for new devices and removes departed devices; unchanged registry membership returns after one atomic generation check.
- `for_each(function_ref<void(driver&, const device_connection&)>) -> void` visits each bound driver/device pair.
- `submit(device_id, const output_request&) -> void` forwards output to a bound device; unbound IDs are ignored.
- `size() const noexcept -> size_t` returns `entries_.size()`.

## Design

`entry` stores `device_connection device`, optional `unique_ptr<transport::hid_device> hid`, and `unique_ptr<driver> drv`; `drv` may reference `hid`, requiring destruction order `drv` then `hid` and prohibiting entry copying. `bind(const device_connection&, unique_ptr<transport::hid_device>&) -> unique_ptr<driver>` selects family-specific drivers: Xbox-class uses XInput, PlayStation families use dedicated drivers, and unknown/unlinked devices remain unbound without fallback decoding.

## State and Coupling

`ctx_` references `context`; `xinput_` references `transport::xinput_module`; `generation_` tracks registry changes, `reconciled_` gates initial synchronization, and `entries_` owns active bindings. Dependencies include `types.hpp`, `utility.hpp`, `context.hpp`, `registry.hpp`, `driver.hpp`, `hid.hpp`, and `xinput-module.hpp`.

**set.cpp binds, reconciles, iterates, and routes input/output across Xbox and PlayStation controller drivers.**

## Interface

- `set::set (const context& ctx, const transport::xinput_module& x)` stores non-owning `ctx_` and `xinput_` references.
- `set::~set ()` is out-of-line/defaulted so `driver` and transport types require completeness only here.
- `unique_ptr<driver> set::bind (const device_connection& d, unique_ptr<transport::hid_device>& hid)` constructs a family-specific driver or returns `nullptr`.
- `void set::reconcile (const registry& r)` synchronizes active `entries_` with registry membership.
- `void set::for_each (function_ref<void (driver&, const device_connection&)> fn)` invokes `fn` for every active driver/device pair.
- `void set::submit (device_id id, const output_request& request)` forwards `request` to the matching driver and silently ignores unknown `id`.

## Binding behavior

- `set::bind` maps `family::xbox` to `xinput_driver`, requiring `std::get_if<xinput_binding>(&d.binding)` and passing `ctx_`, `xinput_`, `d.id`, and `b->index`.
- `set::bind` maps `family::dualshock4`, `family::dualsense`, and `family::dualsense_edge` to `dualshock4_driver`, `dualsense_driver`, and `dualsense_edge_driver`, respectively.
- `set::bind` requires non-null `hid` for PlayStation families and asserts `hid->link() == connection::usb || hid->link() == connection::bluetooth`.
- `enable_extended_reports (ctx_, *hid, d.id, d.identity.family)` must succeed for Bluetooth PlayStation devices; failure returns `nullptr` because minimal reports are undecodable.
- `family::unknown`, invalid bindings, absent HID handles, and unsupported families return `nullptr`.

## Reconciliation and ownership

- `set::reconcile` caches `registry::generation()` in `generation_` and skips work when `reconciled_ && g == generation_`.
- `set::reconcile` snapshots `registry` via `r.for_each` before slow HID operations or lock reacquisition.
- `std::erase_if(entries_)` retires entries whose `device.id` is absent; `entry` owns the borrowed `hid` lifetime alongside `drv`.
- `transport::open (ctx_, b->path)` opens `hid_binding` paths; null handles skip binding after transport-side error reporting.
- `set::reconcile` reports `errc::none` for release/bind events and `errc::unsupported_device` with `severity::warning` when `bind` returns null.

## Coupling

- `set.cpp` includes `set.hpp`, `xinput.hpp`, `dualshock4.hpp`, `dualsense.hpp`, `dualsense-edge.hpp`, and `playstation.hpp`.
- `context::report`, `registry::generation`, `registry::for_each`, `device_connection::identity`, `device_connection::binding`, `device_connection::transport`, `entry`, `driver::submit`, `transport::open`, `connection`, `family`, `xinput_binding`, and `hid_binding` define the surrounding contracts.
- `std::variant` access uses `std::get_if`; `std::any_of`, `std::none_of`, and `std::erase_if` implement membership synchronization.

entries.response:
**binding.cpp does controller binding storage and button-layout application for gamepad mappings.**

## Exported interface

- `binding_table::bind(engine_key k, string command)` stores a command at `key_index(k)`.
- `binding_table::bind(engine_key k, action a)` converts `action` through `command(a)` and stores it.
- `binding_table::unbind(engine_key k) noexcept` clears the `engine_key` slot.
- `binding_table::clear() noexcept` clears every command in `commands_`.
- `binding_table::command_for(engine_key k) const noexcept` returns `const string*`, or `nullptr` for an unbound key.
- `binding_table::for_each(function_ref<void (engine_key, const string&)>) const` visits non-empty bindings using `all_engine_keys`.
- `binding_table::size() const noexcept` counts non-empty bindings.
- `apply_button_layout(binding_table& t, string_view name)` clears and repopulates `t` from layout-name flags.

## Layout behavior

`apply_button_layout` lowercases `name`, then detects substring flags `tactical`, `lefty`, `nomad`, and `_alt`; `tactical` swaps `action::melee` to `button_b` and `action::stance` to `button_rstick`, while the default reverses those assignments.

`lefty` maps `button_ltrig`/`button_rtrig` to fire/ADS, `button_lshldr` to nomad sprint or frag, `button_rshldr` to special grenade, and `button_rstick` to sprint; the default maps triggers conventionally, swaps shoulder actions under `_alt`, and maps `button_lstick` to nomad jump/stand or sprint.

Shared mappings always assign start/menu, back/scoreboard, X/use-reload, Y/next-weapon, D-pad directions/action slots 1–4, and A/jump-stand.

## Coupling and contracts

`index_of` delegates to `key_index`; `lowercase` uses `std::tolower` with unsigned-char conversion; `contains` uses `string::find` and `string::npos`. `commands_`, `count`, `all_engine_keys`, `engine_key`, `action`, `command`, `function_ref`, `string`, and `string_view` are required mapping-layer types/constants.
