**dualsense.cpp decodes DualSense USB/Bluetooth input reports and submits validated rumble, lighting, LED, and supported haptic output through `dualsense_driver`.**

## Public Interface

- `decode_dualsense(span<const byte> r, connection link, raw_sample& raw, canonical_sample& canonical, bool edge) noexcept -> bool` validates framing/CRC, decodes sticks, triggers, buttons, motion, touch, battery, and capabilities into `raw_sample` and `canonical_sample`.
- `dualsense_driver::dualsense_driver(const context& ctx, transport::hid_device& hid, device_id device)` stores `ctx_`, `hid_`, `device_`, and `link_ = hid.link()`.
- `dualsense_driver::read_and_decode(raw_sample& raw, canonical_sample& canonical, bool edge) noexcept -> bool` drains up to `max_reports_per_poll` HID reports and retains the newest valid decoded sample.
- `dualsense_driver::poll(raw_sample& raw, canonical_sample& canonical) noexcept -> bool` delegates to `read_and_decode(raw, canonical, false)`, disabling DualSense Edge back-button decoding.
- `dualsense_driver::submit(const output_request& request) noexcept -> void` encodes and writes supported output through `encode_dualsense_output`; rejected requests are reported and ignored.

## Report Framing

- `resolve_frame(span<const byte> r, connection link, size_t& common) noexcept -> bool` accepts USB reports only when `r.size() >= ds_size_usb`, `rd_u8(r, 0) == ds_report_usb`, with `ds_report_usb = 0x01`, `ds_size_usb = 64`, and `ds_common_usb = 1`.
- `resolve_frame` accepts Bluetooth reports only when `r.size() >= ds_size_bt`, `rd_u8(r, 0) == ds_report_bt`, and `verify_ps_crc32(ps_input_crc_seed, r.first(ds_size_bt - 4), rd_le32(r, ds_size_bt - 4))` succeeds, with `ds_report_bt = 0x31`, `ds_size_bt = 78`, and `ds_common_bt = 2`.
- `connection` values other than `connection::usb` and `connection::bluetooth` cause `resolve_frame` and `decode_dualsense` to return `false`.
- `read_and_decode` allocates `array<byte, ds_size_bt>` and treats zero-length or failed `hid_.read()` results as poll termination.

## Input Mapping

- `decode_dualsense` reads sticks at `b + 0..3`, assigns `raw.sticks`, and fills `canonical.sticks` with raw coordinates plus `normalize_ps_stick()` values.
- `decode_dualsense` reads analog L2/R2 values at `b + 4` and `b + 5`, stores `raw.triggers`, and normalizes canonical trigger values as `value / 255.0f`.
- `decode_dualsense` reads button bytes at `b + 7..10`; `b0` maps face buttons and hat input, `b1` maps `l1`, `r1`, `l2`, `r2`, `back`, `start`, `l3`, and `r3`, and `b2` maps `guide`, `touchpad`, and `mute`.
- `decode_dualsense` invokes `apply_hat(btns, static_cast<uint8_t>(b0 & 0x0Fu))`, maps face bits `0x10`, `0x20`, `0x40`, `0x80` to west/south/east/north, and preserves packed `b0..b3` in `raw.buttons`.
- `decode_dualsense` maps Edge-only `b2` bits `0x10`, `0x20`, `0x40`, `0x80` to `edge_fn_left`, `edge_fn_right`, `edge_paddle_left`, and `edge_paddle_right` only when `edge == true`.
- `decode_dualsense` reads signed little-endian gyro values at `b + 15`, `b + 17`, `b + 19`, acceleration values at `b + 21`, `b + 23`, `b + 25`, and a 32-bit device timestamp at `b + 27`.
- `decode_dualsense` decodes two four-byte touch contacts at `b + 32` and `b + 36` through `decode_touch_point`, assigning `canonical.touch` and `raw.touch`.
- `decode_dualsense` interprets battery `st0 = rd_u8(r, b + 52)`, with `capacity = st0 & 0x0F` and `charging = (st0 >> 4) & 0x0F`; charging codes `0x0` and `0x1` yield discharging/charging with `min(capacity * 10 + 5, 100)`, `0x2` yields full/100%, and other codes yield unknown status without usable capacity.
- `decode_dualsense` resets `canonical.motion` because calibrated physical-unit motion is assigned by a later calibration stage.

## Capabilities and Output

- `decode_dualsense` assigns `capabilities` for `gyroscope`, `accelerometer`, `touchpad`, `battery`, `rumble`, `haptics`, `adaptive_triggers`, `light_bar`, `player_leds`, and `microphone_button`; `edge == true` additionally adds `back_buttons`.
- `dualsense_driver::submit` uses `array<byte, ds_output_bt_size>` and `bt_output_sequence_` with `encode_dualsense_output(request, link_, bt_output_sequence_, buf)`.
- `dualsense_driver::submit` reports `errc::output_rejected` with `"DualSense driver ignores an output request it cannot encode (adaptive triggers are not yet enabled)"` when encoding returns `nullopt`.
- `dualsense_driver::submit` reports `errc::output_rejected` with `"DualSense output report write failed"` when `hid_.write()` fails.
- `encode_dualsense_output` supports verified-layout rumble, light-bar, and player-LED output while rejecting adaptive-trigger effects.

## Diagnostics and Dependencies

- `read_and_decode` drops malformed reports and reports `severity::warning`, `facility::decode`, `errc::report_malformed`, and `"DualSense report failed framing or CRC validation and was dropped"`.
- `read_and_decode` recognizes `minimal_bluetooth_report(r, link_)`, logs `severity::info`, `facility::decode`, `errc::none`, and `"DualSense is still sending minimal Bluetooth reports and produces no input; the controller did not switch to its extended report"` once via `minimal_reported_`.
- `decode_dualsense` depends on `decode.hpp` for `rd_u8`, `rd_le16s`, `rd_le32`, `normalize_ps_stick`, `decode_touch_point`, `apply_hat`, and `minimal_bluetooth_report`.
- `resolve_frame` depends on `playstation.hpp` for `connection`, `ps_input_crc_seed`, and `verify_ps_crc32`; `submit` depends on `output-report.hpp` for `output_request`, `ds_output_bt_size`, and `encode_dualsense_output`.

**output-report.cpp encodes DualShock 4 and DualSense rumble/LED requests into USB or Bluetooth HID output reports.**

## Public Interface

- `optional<size_t> encode_dualshock4_output(const output_request& r, connection link, span<byte> out) noexcept` validates `link` and buffer capacity, emits USB (`0x05`) or Bluetooth (`0x11`) framing, encodes `rumble_request` or `light_bar_request`, seals Bluetooth reports with CRC-32, and returns encoded size or `nullopt`.
- `optional<size_t> encode_dualsense_output(const output_request& r, connection link, uint8_t& bt_sequence, span<byte> out) noexcept` validates framing inputs, encodes `rumble_request`, `light_bar_request`, or `player_led_request`, advances the Bluetooth sequence nibble, seals Bluetooth reports, and returns encoded size or `nullopt`.

## Encoding Contracts

- `encode_dualshock4_output` selects `ds4_output_usb_size`/`ds4_output_bt_size`, uses common-field bases `1`/`3`, and zero-fills the complete report before writing fields.
- `encode_dualshock4_output` maps `rumble_request.high_frequency` to `motor_right` at `base + 3`, `rumble_request.low_frequency` to `motor_left` at `base + 4`, and `light_bar_request.{red,green,blue}` to `base + 5..7`.
- `encode_dualsense_output` selects `ds_output_usb_size`/`ds_output_bt_size`, uses bases `1`/`3`, and zero-fills output before encoding.
- `encode_dualsense_output` maps rumble to `base + 2/+3`, light-bar RGB to `base + 44..46`, and `player_led_request.mask & 0x1F` to `base + 43`.
- `to_byte(float v) noexcept` clamps normalized magnitudes to `[0,1]` and rounds `v * 255.0f` via `+ 0.5f`; `put(span<byte>, size_t, uint8_t)` asserts bounds before byte assignment.
- `encode_dualshock4_output` rejects non-`usb`/non-`bluetooth` links, undersized buffers, `player_led_request`, and adaptive-trigger variants.
- `encode_dualsense_output` rejects non-`usb`/non-`bluetooth` links, undersized buffers, and unsupported adaptive-trigger variants.

## Bluetooth Integrity and State

- `seal_bt_crc(span<byte> b) noexcept` computes CRC-32 over the report prefix using `ps_output_crc_seed` (`0xA2`), initializes with `0xFFFFFFFFu`, complements the result, and writes little-endian CRC bytes into the final four positions.
- `encode_dualshock4_output` writes Bluetooth report ID `0x11`, hardware-control flags `ds4_hwctl_hid | ds4_hwctl_crc32` (`0x80 | 0x40`).
- `encode_dualsense_output` writes Bluetooth report ID `0x31`, stores `(bt_sequence & 0x0F) << 4` in byte `1`, writes `ds_output_tag` (`0x10`) in byte `2`, then updates `bt_sequence = (bt_sequence + 1) & 0x0F`.
- `ds4_flag0_motor` (`0x01`), `ds4_flag0_led` (`0x02`), `ds_flag0_compatible_vibration` (`0x01`), `ds_flag0_haptics_select` (`0x02`), `ds_flag1_lightbar_enable` (`0x04`), and `ds_flag1_player_leds_enable` (`0x10`) control device interpretation.

## Dependencies and Design

- `output_request`, `rumble_request`, `light_bar_request`, `player_led_request`, `connection`, `byte`, `span`, `optional`, `crc32_le`, and report-size constants come from `output-report.hpp`/`decode.hpp` and shared project headers.
- `std::variant` visitation through `std::get_if` implements a type-dispatch strategy; `std::clamp`, `std::fill_n`, and `assert` enforce normalization, deterministic zeroed layouts, and programmer-error bounds checks.
- `noexcept` encoders return `nullopt` for validation or capability failures; unsupported layouts are intentionally not guessed.

**key.cpp maps controller `engine_key` values, numeric IDs, and stable string names.**

## Public interface

- `bool is_controller_key(int keynum) noexcept` checks whether `keynum` maps via `key_from_keynum`.
- `size_t key_index(engine_key key) noexcept` finds `key` in `all_engine_keys`, returning sentinel index `0` when absent.
- `const char* key_name(engine_key k) noexcept` returns the canonical name from `key_names`.
- `optional<engine_key> key_from_name(string_view name) noexcept` performs case-insensitive lookup through `iequals`, returning `nullopt` for unknown names.
- `optional<engine_key> key_from_keynum(int keynum) noexcept` converts numeric IDs by scanning `all_engine_keys`, returning `nullopt` when unmatched.

## Mapping contract

`key_names` contains exactly `engine_key_count` entries enforced by `static_assert`; canonical strings are `BUTTON_A`, `BUTTON_B`, `BUTTON_X`, `BUTTON_Y`, `BUTTON_LSHLDR`, `BUTTON_RSHLDR`, `BUTTON_START`, `BUTTON_BACK`, `BUTTON_LSTICK`, `BUTTON_RSTICK`, `BUTTON_LTRIG`, `BUTTON_RTRIG`, `DPAD_UP`, `DPAD_DOWN`, `DPAD_LEFT`, `DPAD_RIGHT`, `APAD_UP`, `APAD_DOWN`, `APAD_LEFT`, `APAD_RIGHT`, `RSTICK_UP`, `RSTICK_DOWN`, `RSTICK_LEFT`, `RSTICK_RIGHT`.

`key_name` assumes `engine_key` values align with `all_engine_keys`; `key_index`’s `0` fallback is safe only under that enum invariant.

## Dependencies and behavior

`std_include.hpp` supplies shared aliases such as `string_view`, `optional`, and `nullopt`; `key.hpp` defines `engine_key`, `engine_key_count`, and `all_engine_keys`; `<cctype>` supports unsigned-char-safe `std::tolower` in `iequals`.

entries.response:
**stick-layout.hpp maps physical gamepad sticks to logical movement and view axes.**

## Interface

- `enum class virtual_axis : uint8_t`: `side`, `forward`, `yaw`, `pitch`.
- `const char* to_string(virtual_axis) noexcept`: converts `virtual_axis` to its stable name.
- `enum class stick_layout : uint8_t`: `standard`, `southpaw`, `legacy`, `legacy_southpaw`.
- `const char* to_string(stick_layout) noexcept`: converts `stick_layout` to its stable name.
- `stick_layout stick_layout_from_name(string_view) noexcept`: parses `gpad_sticksConfig`; unknown names resolve to `stick_layout::standard`.
- `virtual_axis axis_for(stick_layout, stick which, bool horizontal) noexcept`: resolves a physical stick component; `horizontal=true` selects the horizontal axis.
- `struct resolved_axes`: normalized scalar fields `float side`, `forward`, `yaw`, `pitch`, each defaulting to `0.0f`.
- `resolved_axes resolve(stick_layout, stick_vector left, stick_vector right) noexcept`: permutes calibrated canonical vectors into logical axes with sign handling.

## Design Contracts

`resolve` performs only layout permutation and sign handling; deadzones, response curves, turn rates, and usercmd byte scaling remain downstream. `resolved_axes` carries raw movement deflections and aim-processing view values, never angles. `virtual_axis` separates logical meaning from physical stick placement.

## Dependencies

`types.hpp` supplies `string_view`, `stick`, and `stick_vector`; `utility.hpp` supplies shared controller utilities; `sample/axis.hpp` supplies axis-related definitions.

entries.response:
**xinput.cpp decodes XInput controller state, suppresses unchanged packets, and submits rumble output.**

## Interface

- `decode_xinput(const XINPUT_GAMEPAD& g, bool has_guide, raw_sample& raw, canonical_sample& canonical) noexcept` copies device-native axes/triggers/buttons into `raw`, then fills normalized `canonical_sample` state.
- `xinput_driver::xinput_driver(const context& ctx, const transport::xinput_module& module, device_id device, user_index index)` stores `ctx_`, `module_`, `device_`, and `index_`.
- `xinput_driver::poll(raw_sample& raw, canonical_sample& canonical) noexcept -> bool` reads `XINPUT_STATE` through `module_.get_state`, decodes new packets, and returns whether a sample was published.
- `xinput_driver::submit(const output_request& request) noexcept -> void` converts `rumble_request` into `XINPUT_VIBRATION`; non-rumble requests are rejected informationally.

## Decoding Contracts

- `normalize_stick(int16_t rx, int16_t ry) noexcept -> stick_vector` divides axes by `thumb_full_scale` (`32767.0f`), clamps each component to `[-1.0f, 1.0f]`, and radially clamps magnitude above `1.0f`; deadzones and response curves remain owned by the aim layer.
- `decode_trigger(uint8_t raw) noexcept -> trigger_sample` returns `{raw, static_cast<float>(raw) / 255.0f}`.
- `decode_buttons(uint16_t w, bool have_guide) noexcept -> button_set` maps XInput A/B/X/Y, D-pad, shoulders, thumb clicks, start, and back bits to `button::face_*`, `button::dpad_*`, `button::l1/r1`, `button::l3/r3`, `button::start`, and `button::back`.
- `xinput_gamepad_guide` equals `0x0400`; `button::guide` is decoded only when `have_guide` is true because the extended ordinal-100 runtime entry point exposes the otherwise-masked guide bit.
- `button::l2` and `button::r2` become digital trigger states when the corresponding raw value is greater than `XINPUT_GAMEPAD_TRIGGER_THRESHOLD`.
- `canonical_sample::touch`, `canonical_sample::motion`, and `canonical_sample::battery` are reset empty; `canonical_sample::caps` is always `capability::rumble`.
- `raw_sample::sticks`, `raw_sample::triggers`, and `raw_sample::buttons` retain XInput-native values; `canonical_sample` receives raw and normalized sticks plus trigger samples.

## Polling and Output

- `xinput_driver::poll` treats any `module_.get_state(...) != ERROR_SUCCESS` as an empty slot, clears `have_packet_`, and returns `false`; discovery owns arrival/removal.
- `xinput_driver::poll` uses `XINPUT_STATE::dwPacketNumber` as a change detector, returning `false` for unchanged packets and updating `last_packet_` only for published state.
- `scale_motor(float v) noexcept -> WORD` clamps `v` to `[0.0f, 1.0f]` and scales by `65535.0f` for `XINPUT_VIBRATION::wLeftMotorSpeed` or `wRightMotorSpeed`.
- `xinput_driver::submit` maps `rumble_request::low_frequency` to the left motor and `high_frequency` to the right motor; failed `module_.set_state` calls report `severity::warning`, `facility::driver`, and `errc::output_rejected`.
- `xinput_driver::submit` reports unsupported light-bar, player-LED, and adaptive-trigger requests with `severity::info`, `facility::driver`, and `errc::output_rejected`, using `"XInput driver ignores a non-rumble output request"`.

## Coupling

- `xinput.cpp` depends on `component/gamepad/controller/driver/xinput.hpp`, `XINPUT_GAMEPAD`, `XINPUT_STATE`, `XINPUT_VIBRATION`, XInput button constants, `XINPUT_GAMEPAD_TRIGGER_THRESHOLD`, `transport::xinput_module`, and `context::report`.
- `xinput_driver` follows a driver Strategy pattern: `poll` supplies canonical input while `submit` handles the transport-specific output capability.

**physical.cpp maps physical gamepad inputs to engine keys and evaluates analog-stick deflection.**

## Public interface

- `optional<engine_key> to_engine_key(button b) noexcept` maps standard `button` values to `engine_key`; `guide`, `touchpad`, `mute`, Edge paddles/functions, and `count` return `nullopt`.
- `engine_key to_engine_key(const apad_input& a) noexcept` maps left-stick directions to `apad_*` and right-stick directions to `rstick_*`; invalid directions fall back to `*_up`.
- `optional<engine_key> to_engine_key(const physical_input& p) noexcept` dispatches `physical_input` variants through `std::get_if<button>` or `std::get<apad_input>`.
- `bool axis_deflected(float value, bool positive, bool was_down, float pressed, float hysteresis) noexcept` tests `value > threshold` for positive axes or `value < -threshold` otherwise, with `threshold = pressed + (was_down ? -hysteresis : hysteresis)`.

## Mapping contracts

`button` mappings include `face_south→button_a`, `face_east→button_b`, `face_west→button_x`, `face_north→button_y`, shoulder/trigger/stick buttons, `start`, `back`, and all four `dpad_*` keys. `apad_input` deliberately keeps left and right sticks independently bindable because shared base-engine keys would collide. `physical_input` requires a `button` or `apad_input` alternative; unexpected variants can throw through `std::get`.

## Coupling

`physical.cpp` depends on `std_include.hpp`, `component/gamepad/controller/mapping/physical.hpp`, `std::variant`, `button`, `apad_input`, `physical_input`, `stick`, `stick_direction`, `engine_key`, `optional`, and `nullopt` within `gamepad::unstable::controller::mapping`.

**key.hpp defines IW4x controller-to-engine key identifiers and lookup APIs.**

## Interface

- `engine_key : int` enumerates 24 controller keys: face buttons `0x01–0x04`, shoulders `0x05–0x06`, start/back `0x0E–0x0F`, sticks/triggers `0x10–0x13`, d-pad `0x14–0x17`, left-stick APAD `0x1C–0x1F`, and right-stick directions `0xE0–0xE3`.
- `all_engine_keys : array<engine_key, 24>` stores every supported key in stable enumeration order.
- `engine_key_count : size_t` equals `all_engine_keys.size()`.
- `key_index(engine_key) noexcept -> size_t` maps an `engine_key` to its zero-based `all_engine_keys` index.
- `is_controller_key(int keynum) noexcept -> bool` recognizes whether a raw engine key number belongs to the controller-key set.
- `key_name(engine_key) noexcept -> const char*` returns engine-compatible names such as `"BUTTON_A"` and `"APAD_RIGHT"`.
- `key_from_name(string_view) noexcept -> optional<engine_key>` resolves a case-insensitive engine key name, returning `nullopt` for unknown/non-controller names.
- `key_from_keynum(int) noexcept -> optional<engine_key>` resolves a numeric key, returning `nullopt` for unknown/non-controller values.

## Contracts and Integration

`engine_key` is the boundary between physical controller inputs and engine binding/key-event systems; key names remain semantic-neutral, while `key_name`, `key_from_name`, and `key_from_keynum` preserve compatibility with keyboard binding tables.

`engine_key::rstick_right` must remain below `256`; the `static_assert` enforces direct indexing into the engine’s `keys[256]` state array.

`types.hpp` supplies `array`, `optional`, `size_t`, and `string_view`; `utility.hpp` supplies related support utilities. All declarations reside under `gamepad::unstable::controller::mapping`.

**axis.hpp defines normalized gamepad stick types and the four-stage stick-sample pipeline.**

## Public API

- `stick` enum class (`uint8_t`) identifies `left` or `right` analog sticks.
- `stick_count` is `inline constexpr size_t {2}`.
- `to_string(stick) noexcept` returns `const char*`.
- `stick_vector` stores normalized `float x`, `float y`; `magnitude() const noexcept` returns Euclidean length.
- `stick_raw` stores device-preserved `int32_t x`, `int32_t y`.
- `stick_sample` aggregates `raw`, `normalized`, `calibrated`, and `filtered` stages.

## Contracts

- `stick_vector` components target `[-1, 1]`; magnitude may temporarily exceed `1` before radial clamping.
- `stick_raw` retains unmodified device units for calibration/diagnostics; XInput uses signed 16-bit axis counts.
- `stick_sample::filtered` is the game-path input; aim-layer deadzones/curves and smoothing follow driver-populated `raw`/`normalized`.

## Dependencies

`types.hpp` supplies fixed-width and size types; `utility.hpp` supplies shared controller utilities.

entries.response:
**dualshock4.cpp decodes DualShock 4 HID input reports and submits USB/Bluetooth output reports.**

## Public Interface

- `bool decode_dualshock4(span<const byte> r, connection link, raw_sample& raw, canonical_sample& canonical) noexcept` validates framing, decodes sticks, buttons, triggers, motion, battery, touchpad, capabilities, and canonical normalization.
- `dualshock4_driver::dualshock4_driver(const context& ctx, transport::hid_device& hid, device_id device)` stores `ctx`, `hid`, `device`, and `hid.link()` as `link_`.
- `bool dualshock4_driver::poll(raw_sample& raw, canonical_sample& canonical) noexcept` drains up to `max_reports_per_poll` HID reports and retains the newest valid decoded sample.
- `void dualshock4_driver::submit(const output_request& request) noexcept` encodes and writes a connection-specific DualShock 4 output report.

## Report Framing

`resolve_frame(span<const byte> r, connection link, size_t& common, size_t& max_touch) noexcept` rejects unknown `connection` values, short reports, incorrect report IDs, and invalid Bluetooth CRC-32 values before decoding.

- `ds4_report_usb = 0x01`, `ds4_size_usb = 64`, `ds4_common_usb = 1`, and `ds4_max_touch_usb = 3` define USB framing.
- `ds4_report_bt = 0x11`, `ds4_size_bt = 78`, `ds4_common_bt = 3`, and `ds4_max_touch_bt = 4` define Bluetooth framing.
- Bluetooth `resolve_frame` reads the little-endian CRC at `ds4_size_bt - 4` and verifies `verify_ps_crc32(ps_input_crc_seed, r.first(ds4_size_bt - 4), crc)`.
- `array<byte, ds4_size_bt> buf` accommodates the largest input report; Bluetooth reports include a trailing four-byte CRC.

## Input Mapping

`decode_dualshock4` interprets the common block relative to `b`:

- `b + 0..3` contains `lx`, `ly`, `rx`, and `ry`; `normalize_ps_stick` converts both raw stick pairs into canonical normalized values while `raw.sticks` preserves device bytes.
- `b + 4` contains the four face-button bits (`0x10`, `0x20`, `0x40`, `0x80`) and the low-nibble hat value; `apply_hat` maps the hat to canonical directional buttons.
- `b + 5` maps bits `0x01..0x80` to `button::l1`, `button::r1`, `button::l2`, `button::r2`, `button::back`, `button::start`, `button::l3`, and `button::r3`.
- `b + 6` maps `0x01` to `button::guide`/PS and `0x02` to `button::touchpad`; the complete three-byte button state is preserved in `raw.buttons` as `b0 | (b1 << 8) | (b2 << 16)`.
- `b + 7` and `b + 8` populate left/right `trigger_side` values, with canonical trigger magnitudes normalized by division through `255.0f`.
- `b + 9` supplies `motion.device_timestamp`; signed little-endian values at `b + 12`, `b + 14`, `b + 16` populate `motion.gyro.angular_velocity`, while `b + 18`, `b + 20`, `b + 22` populate `motion.accel.acceleration`.
- `raw.motion` retains raw device counts; `canonical.motion.reset()` delegates physical-unit conversion to the calibration stage and device calibration feature report.
- `b + 29` supplies battery `cap = st0 & 0x0F` and cable state `st0 & 0x10`; `ds4_battery_full = 11` plus cable attachment yields `battery_state::status::full` and `100`, otherwise `cap * 10` is clamped to `100` with charging/discharging status.
- `b + 32` supplies `num_touch`; values `1..max_touch` decode points from `b + 34` and `b + 38` through `decode_touch_point(r.subspan(off, 4))`, while other values clear `canonical.touch`.
- `canonical.caps` always advertises `capability::gyroscope | capability::accelerometer | capability::touchpad | capability::battery | capability::rumble | capability::light_bar`.

## Polling and Error Contracts

`dualshock4_driver::poll` treats valid reports as newest-state updates, bounded by `max_reports_per_poll`; zero-length or unavailable `hid_.read` results terminate draining.

`minimal_bluetooth_report(r, link_)` identifies non-malformed minimal Bluetooth reports, which are discarded because they lack extended motion/touch data; `minimal_reported_` suppresses repeated informational diagnostics.

`ctx_.report` emits `facility::decode` with `errc::none` for the first minimal-report notice and `errc::report_malformed` with `"DualShock 4 report failed framing or CRC validation and was dropped"` for rejected reports.

## Output and Integration

`dualshock4_driver::submit` allocates `array<byte, ds4_output_bt_size> buf` and calls `encode_dualshock4_output(request, link_, buf)`; absent length produces `facility::driver`, `errc::output_rejected`, and `"DualShock 4 driver ignores an output request it cannot encode for this connection"`.

`hid_.write(span<const byte>(buf.data(), *n))` sends encoded output; write failure reports `facility::driver`, `errc::output_rejected`, and `"DualShock 4 output report write failed"`.

`decode.hpp` supplies `rd_u8`, `rd_le16`, `rd_le16s`, `rd_le32`, and `decode_touch_point`; `output-report.hpp` supplies `ds4_output_bt_size` and `encode_dualshock4_output`; `playstation.hpp` supplies `normalize_ps_stick`, `verify_ps_crc32`, and `ps_input_crc_seed`; `std_include.hpp` supplies project aliases such as `span`, `array`, `optional`, `byte`, and `uint8_t`.

`input_frame` aggregates `device_id device`, `controller::family family`, `connection link`, `uint64_t sequence`, `latency_span timing`, and `canonical_sample state`, with defaults `family::unknown`, `connection::unknown`, and zero-initialized values.

**motion.hpp defines typed controller sensor-motion samples in `gamepad::unstable::controller`.**

## Exported symbols

- `sensor_vec3 { float x, y, z; }` stores controller-frame vector components, defaulting to `0.0f`.

- `accel_sample { sensor_vec3 acceleration; }` stores proper acceleration in standard gravities (`1 g = 9.80665 m/s^2`).

## Dependencies

`types.hpp` supplies `optional`; `utility.hpp` supplies controller support utilities. `sensor_vec3` deliberately prevents mixing sensor-frame vectors with screen/world-space aim vectors.

entries.response:
**button.hpp defines device-neutral gamepad button identities and a constexpr 32-bit button-set abstraction.**

## Public API

- `enum class button : uint8_t` enumerates positional buttons (`face_*`, `dpad_*`, `l1/r1`, `l2/r2`, `l3/r3`, `start`, `back`, `guide`, `touchpad`, `mute`, Edge paddles/functions) plus sentinel `button::count`.
- `to_string(button) noexcept` returns a textual button name as `const char*`.
- `class button_set` stores held buttons in `uint32_t bits_`; `button::count <= 32` is enforced by `static_assert`.
- `button_set() constexpr` creates an empty set.
- `down(button) const noexcept` tests membership; `set(button, bool) noexcept` mutates membership.
- `any() const noexcept` reports whether any bit is set; `value() const noexcept` exposes the raw `uint32_t` mask.
- `pressed_since(button_set prev) const noexcept` computes current-down/previous-up edges; `released_since(button_set prev) const noexcept` computes current-up/previous-down edges.
- `operator==(button_set, button_set) noexcept = default` compares masks.

## Design Contracts

`button` names physical positions rather than Xbox/PlayStation labels; logical actions and engine-key translation belong to `controller/mapping`. `button::l2` and `button::r2` represent fully pressed trigger states while analog values remain in trigger samples. `button_set::mask` maps each enumerator to `uint32_t {1} << static_cast<uint32_t>(b)`, making `button_set` allocation-free, trivially copyable, constexpr-friendly, and stateless for edge detection.

## Dependencies

`types.hpp` supplies fixed-width types such as `uint8_t` and `uint32_t`; `utility.hpp` supplies shared controller utilities.

entries.response:
**stick-layout.cpp maps controller stick layouts to virtual axes and resolves stick vectors into movement/view outputs.**

## Public API

- `const char* to_string(virtual_axis a) noexcept` maps `side`, `forward`, `yaw`, `pitch`; unknown values return `"unknown"`.
- `const char* to_string(stick_layout l) noexcept` maps layouts to exact names: `"thumbstick_default"`, `"thumbstick_southpaw"`, `"thumbstick_legacy"`, `"thumbstick_legacysouthpaw"`; invalid values default to `"thumbstick_default"`.
- `stick_layout stick_layout_from_name(string_view name) noexcept` lowercases input and recognizes the exact layout names above; unknown input returns `stick_layout::standard`, with compound `thumbstick_legacysouthpaw` tested first.
- `virtual_axis axis_for(stick_layout l, stick which, bool horizontal) noexcept` selects `virtual_axis` based on stick and layout.
- `resolved_axes resolve(stick_layout l, stick_vector left, stick_vector right) noexcept` converts both stick vectors into `resolved_axes`.

## Mapping Semantics

`axis_for` applies the Southpaw pattern by swapping movement/look sticks; `stick_layout::legacy` additionally swaps horizontal roles, assigning movement-stick X to `yaw` and view-stick X to `side`. Vertical roles remain `forward` for movement and `pitch` for view.

`resolve` iterates `stick::left` and `stick::right`, dispatching X/Y components through `axis_for`; `side` and `forward` use `squared`, while `yaw` and `pitch` preserve raw components.

## Internal Contracts

`lowercase(string_view s) -> string` performs unsigned-character-safe `std::tolower` transformation via `std::transform`.

`squared(float component, stick_vector v) noexcept -> float` returns `std::clamp(v.magnitude() * component, -1.0f, 1.0f)`, implementing squared movement mapping while leaving view-axis shaping to the aim layer.

## Dependencies

`std_include.hpp` supplies project aliases such as `string`, `string_view`; `stick-layout.hpp` defines `virtual_axis`, `stick_layout`, `stick`, `stick_vector`, and `resolved_axes`; `<cctype>` supports `std::tolower`, and `<algorithm>` supplies `std::transform` and `std::clamp`.

entries.response:
**ring.hpp bounds lock-free input-frame transfer between one producer and one consumer.**

## Interface

- `frame_ring<Capacity>` — templated SPSC bounded queue in `gamepad::unstable::controller`; exports `static constexpr size_t capacity`.
- `push(const input_frame& f) noexcept -> bool` — enqueues `input_frame`; returns `false` on full capacity and increments `dropped()`.
- `try_pop(input_frame& out) noexcept -> bool` — dequeues oldest `input_frame`; returns `false` when empty.
- `occupancy() const noexcept -> size_t` — reports queued frames, potentially stale to external observers.
- `dropped() const noexcept -> uint64_t` — reports lifetime overflow drops.

## Invariants

- `Capacity` requires `Capacity >= 2`; otherwise static assertion emits `"a ring needs at least two slots to distinguish states"`.
- `Capacity` requires power-of-two alignment via `(Capacity & (Capacity - 1)) == 0`; otherwise emits `"ring capacity must be a power of two"`.
- `mask` equals `Capacity - 1`; `head_` and `tail_` are free-running counters, with slots addressed by `counter & mask`.
- `head_` is producer-owned; `tail_` is consumer-owned; `buf_` is fixed inline `array<input_frame, Capacity>` and performs no allocation.
- `push` drops newest frames when `h - t >= Capacity`; `try_pop` distinguishes empty state with `t == h`.
- `push` asserts `f.sequence > last_sequence_ || h == 0`; `last_sequence_` is producer-only monotonic-sequence bookkeeping.

## Concurrency and Coupling

- `atomic<size_t> head_`, `tail_` use acquire/release publication and relaxed owner access for SPSC synchronization.
- `atomic<uint64_t> dropped_` uses relaxed increments/loads.
- `types.hpp` supplies `array`, `atomic`, `memory_order_*`, and integer types; `utility.hpp` supplies support utilities; `frame.hpp` defines `input_frame`.

entries.response:
**device-notify.hpp implements interrupt-driven HID device-change notification via a message-only window and worker thread.**

## Interface

- `device_notifier(const context&)` creates notification state and starts the message-pump thread.
- `~device_notifier()` tears down thread/window resources.
- `device_notifier(const device_notifier&) = delete` and `operator=(const device_notifier&) = delete` enforce non-copyability.
- `bool consume() noexcept` atomically clears and returns `pending_`, reporting each change once.

## Design

`run(const context&) noexcept` owns Windows `WM_DEVICECHANGE` handling; `window_` stores the created `HWND`, while `thread_` pumps messages and otherwise sleeps. `pending_` is deliberately coarse: it signals that the HID-device set may have changed, leaving full reconciliation to discovery and polling fallback. `pending_.exchange(false, std::memory_order_acquire)` makes frame-rate polling cheap and thread-safe.

## Dependencies

`context`, `types.hpp`, and `utility.hpp` supply controller/runtime integration; `<thread>` and `<atomic>` implement lifecycle and synchronization.

entries.response:
**sample.hpp does define raw and canonical gamepad samples plus battery-state formatting.**

## API

- `battery_state` stores `status state {status::unknown}` and `optional<uint8_t> percent` (`0..100` when reported).
- `battery_state::status` enumerates `unknown`, `discharging`, `charging`, `full`.
- `to_string(battery_state::status) noexcept` returns `const char*`.
- `raw_sample` stores device-native `array<stick_raw, stick_count> sticks`, `array<uint16_t, trigger_count> triggers`, `uint32_t buttons`, and optional `motion_sample`, `touchpad`, `battery_state`.
- `canonical_sample` stores device-neutral `button_set buttons`, `array<stick_sample, stick_count> sticks`, `array<trigger_sample, trigger_count> triggers`, optional `touchpad`, `motion_sample`, `battery_state`, plus `capabilities caps`.

## Contracts

`raw_sample` preserves minimally decoded units, button bits, and layouts for calibration/diagnostics; gameplay excludes it. `canonical_sample` preserves capability absence via empty `optional` values, distinguishes absent from zero, and uses `caps` for feature presentation without driver inspection. `DualSense` may populate touch/motion, while `XInput` may leave them empty.

## Dependencies

`types.hpp` and `utility.hpp` supply shared aliases; `axis.hpp`, `button.hpp`, `trigger.hpp`, `touch.hpp`, `motion.hpp`, and `capability.hpp` define component types. Symbols reside in `gamepad::unstable::controller`.

**xinput-module.hpp does runtime XInput DLL loading and safe controller API forwarding.**

## Interface

- `xinput_module(const context&)` loads the highest-capability available XInput variant.
- `~xinput_module()` releases the owned `HMODULE`.
- `xinput_module` is non-copyable and non-movable; resolved function pointers remain valid only while `handle_` is mapped.
- `bool loaded() const noexcept` reports `handle_ != nullptr`.
- `const char* dll_name() const noexcept` returns the loaded DLL name or `"none"`.
- `bool has_guide_button() const noexcept` reports `get_state_ex_ != nullptr`.
- `DWORD get_state(DWORD, XINPUT_STATE&) const noexcept` forwards state queries.
- `DWORD get_capabilities(DWORD, DWORD, XINPUT_CAPABILITIES&) const noexcept` forwards capability queries.
- `DWORD set_state(DWORD, XINPUT_VIBRATION&) const noexcept` forwards vibration commands.

## Runtime Contracts

`xinput_module::load` resolves XInput entry points by name at runtime, avoiding import-library process-load failure; unavailable runtimes return `ERROR_DEVICE_NOT_CONNECTED`. `get_state_ex_` resolves ordinal `100`, preserving the guide button masked by public `XInputGetState`; `get_state_`, `get_capabilities_`, and `set_state_` use WINAPI-compatible signatures.

## Coupling

`xinput_module` depends on `context`, `support/types.hpp`, `support/utility.hpp`, Windows `HMODULE`, `DWORD`, `XINPUT_STATE`, `XINPUT_CAPABILITIES`, and `XINPUT_VIBRATION`.

entries.response:
**device-notify.cpp does HID device-change notification via a hidden Windows message window.**

## Interface

- `device_notifier::device_notifier(const context& ctx)` starts a dedicated `std::thread` executing `run(ctx)`.
- `device_notifier::~device_notifier()` posts `WM_CLOSE` to the stored `HWND` and joins `thread_`.
- `device_notifier::run(const context& ctx) noexcept` registers the window class, creates the message-only window, subscribes to HID interface notifications, pumps messages, unregisters notifications, and clears `window_`.

## Notification Flow

- `window_class` is the exact class name `L"gamepad_controller_devnotify"`.
- `window_proc(HWND w, UINT msg, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp) noexcept` handles `WM_DEVICECHANGE`, `WM_CLOSE`, and `WM_DESTROY`, delegating other messages to `DefWindowProcW`.
- `DBT_DEVICEARRIVAL` and `DBT_DEVICEREMOVECOMPLETE` set `pending_` through `flag_of(HWND w)` using `std::memory_order_release`; other device-change events are ignored.
- `WM_CLOSE` calls `DestroyWindow(w)`, while `WM_DESTROY` calls `PostQuitMessage(0)` and terminates the `GetMessageW` loop.
- `flag_of(HWND w)` retrieves the `std::atomic<bool>*` stored in `GWLP_USERDATA`, sharing the atomic consumed by `device_notifier::consume`.

## Windows Integration

- `RegisterClassExW` installs `window_proc`; `ERROR_CLASS_ALREADY_EXISTS` is accepted, while other registration failures trigger `ctx.report`.
- `CreateWindowExW` creates a zero-sized `HWND_MESSAGE` window and stores it in `window_` with `std::memory_order_release`.
- `HidD_GetHidGuid` supplies the HID class GUID for `DEV_BROADCAST_DEVICEINTERFACE_W`; `RegisterDeviceNotificationW` uses `DEVICE_NOTIFY_WINDOW_HANDLE`.
- `UnregisterDeviceNotification` releases `notify` after message-loop shutdown.
- `GetMessageW`, `TranslateMessage`, and `DispatchMessageW` keep the notifier thread blocked until notification or destruction.

## Failure Contract

- `ctx.report(severity::warning, facility::discovery, errc::transport_failure, "...")` reports class registration, window creation, or HID registration failures.
- Exact fallback messages are `"device-change window class registration failed; discovery will poll"`, `"device-change window creation failed; discovery will poll"`, and `"HID device-change registration failed; discovery will poll"`.
- `notify == nullptr` preserves discovery through its polling fallback.

entries.response:
**xinput-module.cpp dynamically loads Windows XInput runtimes and exposes validated state, capability, and vibration calls.**

## Public Interface

- `xinput_module::xinput_module(const context& ctx)` invokes `load(ctx)`.
- `xinput_module::~xinput_module()` releases `handle_` with `FreeLibrary` when non-null.
- `void xinput_module::load(const context& ctx)` resolves and reports the first usable XInput DLL.
- `DWORD xinput_module::get_state(DWORD user_index, XINPUT_STATE& out) const noexcept` prefers `get_state_ex_`, then `get_state_`.
- `DWORD xinput_module::get_capabilities(DWORD user_index, DWORD flags, XINPUT_CAPABILITIES& out) const noexcept` invokes `get_capabilities_`.
- `DWORD xinput_module::set_state(DWORD user_index, XINPUT_VIBRATION& vibration) const noexcept` invokes `set_state_`.

## Runtime Loading

- `variants` probes exactly `"xinput1_4.dll"`, `"xinput1_3.dll"`, `"xinput9_1_0.dll"` in descending capability order via `LoadLibraryA`.
- `get_state_`, `get_capabilities_`, and `set_state_` require `GetProcAddress`; missing any symbol triggers `FreeLibrary(h)` and fallback probing.
- `get_state_ex_` resolves ordinal `100` using `GetProcAddress(h, reinterpret_cast<const char*> (100))`; absence disables guide-button decoding but does not reject the DLL.
- `handle_`, `name_`, `get_state_`, `get_state_ex_`, `get_capabilities_`, and `set_state_` are assigned only after mandatory entry-point validation.

## Reporting and Failure Contracts

- `ctx.report` emits `severity::info`, `facility::transport`, `errc::none` with `"XInput loaded via "` plus the DLL name and either `" (guide button available)"` or `" (no guide button)"`.
- `ctx.report` emits `severity::warning`, `facility::transport`, `errc::transport_failure` with `"no XInput runtime could be loaded; XInput controllers will not be available"` when probing fails.
- `get_state`, `get_capabilities`, and `set_state` return `ERROR_DEVICE_NOT_CONNECTED` when their corresponding function pointer is unavailable.

## Integration

- `LoadLibraryA`, `GetProcAddress`, `FreeLibrary`, `HMODULE`, `DWORD`, and XInput structs couple `xinput_module` to the Windows runtime.
- `context`, `severity`, `facility::transport`, `errc`, `string`, and function-pointer aliases from `xinput-module.hpp` define reporting and ABI contracts.

entries.response:
**hid.hpp defines the platform-independent HID transport interface and enumeration/opening API for supported gamepad controllers.**

## Public symbols

- `hid_attributes` aggregates `vendor_id vendor`, `product_id product`, and `optional<uint16_t> version`.
- `hid_device` is an abstract, non-throwing HID endpoint interface with virtual destructor `~hid_device() = default`.
- `hid_device::link() const noexcept` returns `connection`, identifying USB/Bluetooth report framing.
- `hid_device::attributes() const noexcept` returns `hid_attributes` discovered from the device.
- `hid_device::feature_report_length() const noexcept` returns the maximum declared feature-report size, or `0` when none exists.
- `hid_device::read(span<byte> buf) noexcept` returns `optional<size_t>`: byte count, `0` for no pending report, or `nullopt` for error/disconnect.
- `hid_device::write(span<const byte> buf) noexcept` writes one output report, with `buf[0]` as report ID, returning `optional<size_t>` or `nullopt` on failure.
- `hid_device::get_feature(span<byte> buf) noexcept` exchanges a feature report, requiring `buf.size() >= feature_report_length()` and `buf[0]` as report ID; returns success as `bool`.
- `hid_device::set_feature(span<const byte> buf) noexcept` submits a feature report and returns success as `bool`.
- `hid_enumeration_entry` stores `wstring path`, `hid_attributes attributes`, `connection link {connection::unknown}`, and `size_t input_report_length {0}`.
- `classify_link(size_t input_report_length) noexcept` returns `connection`: length `64` maps to USB, `78` maps to Bluetooth, and all other lengths map to `connection::unknown`.
- `enumerate(const context&)` returns `vector<hid_enumeration_entry>` for present, supported controller-family HID interfaces.
- `open(const context&, const wstring& path)` returns `unique_ptr<hid_device>` or `nullptr` when opening or validation fails.

## Contracts and integration

- `hid_device` is an abstraction boundary: drivers and decode tests consume captured report bytes without Windows I/O, while `transport/hid.cxx` owns concrete OS-handle reads/writes.
- `hid_enumeration_entry::path` is the stable interface identity required by `open`; `link` remains `connection::unknown` for unsupported report lengths and such devices are not driver-bound.
- `enumerate` filters unrelated HID families/collections, performs queries only, reports failures through `context`, and returns partial results rather than throwing.
- `open` re-reads attributes, report length, and link after a possible unplug/replug race; ambiguous or unsupported devices are rejected, while read-only opening remains valid when writing is unavailable.
- `hid_device::feature_report_length` controls `get_feature` buffer sizing because platform transfer size derives from the buffer, not report ID.
- `types.hpp`, `utility.hpp`, `context.hpp`, `id.hpp`, and `identity.hpp` supply `optional`, `span`, `vector`, `unique_ptr`, `byte`, `connection`, controller IDs, and device identity types.

entries.response:
**mouse_input.cpp installs and manages Windows/raw-mouse hooks for game mouse input, cursor hiding, and gamepad activity tracking.**

## Role and Integration

`mouse_input::component` integrates `component_interface`, `scheduler`, `gamepad`, `game::main_window`, `game::keyCatchers`, `dvars::m_rawInput`, and `utils::hook`; `REGISTER_COMPONENT(mouse_input::component)` registers lifecycle ownership.

`post_load() override` schedules a `scheduler::loop` on `scheduler::main` every `100ms` to install the game callsite hook, install the window procedure hook, and synchronize raw-input registration.

`pre_destroy() override` calls `uninstall_wnd_proc()` and `restore_mouse_event_callsite()` during component teardown; `post_load()` registers the same cleanup through `scheduler::on_shutdown`.

## Hook and Input Pipeline

`install_hooks_if_ready()` waits until `is_window_ready()` succeeds for 10 consecutive loop ticks, snapshots 5 bytes at `game::game_offset(0x102C3934)`, then patches that callsite with `utils::hook::call(..., mouse_event_callsite_stub)`.

`install_wnd_proc_if_ready()` requires `callsite_patched`, a valid `HWND`, and `dvars::m_rawInput`; it replaces `GWLP_WNDPROC` through `SetWindowLongPtrA` and stores `original_wnd_proc`.

`wnd_proc_stub(HWND, UINT, WPARAM, LPARAM) -> LRESULT` resets `raw_mouse_x`/`raw_mouse_y` on inactive `WM_ACTIVATEAPP`, reports `WM_MOUSEMOVE` activity when raw input is disabled, returns `TRUE` after `SetCursor(nullptr)` for hidden cursors on `WM_SETCURSOR`, and accumulates `RIM_TYPEMOUSE` deltas from `WM_INPUT` via `GetRawInputData`.

`mouse_event_body(int y, int x, int dx, int dy) -> int` stores `pending_event`, reports ordinary mouse activity unless `raw_input_registered` or key catcher bit `0x10` applies, suppresses events when `gamepad::should_hide_cursor()` is true, and otherwise forwards to the original game routine.

`mouse_event_body()` substitutes `raw_mouse_x - old_x` and `raw_mouse_y - old_y` only when raw input is enabled, the window is foreground, the cursor is not captured (`*game::keyCatchers & 0x10`), and nonzero raw deltas exist; zero deltas and all fallback states call `call_original_mouse_event()` unchanged.

`mouse_event_callsite_stub()` is a naked x86 `__cdecl` bridge preserving `esi`, `edi`, and `ebx`, adapting registers/stack arguments into `mouse_event_body()`.

`call_original_mouse_event_stub()` is a naked x86 bridge that invokes `original_mouse_event_address = game::game_offset(0x102FD5D0)` using `original_call_state` and records `original_call_result`.

## State and Lifecycle Contracts

`register_raw_input()` registers mouse usage page `0x01`, usage `0x02`, with `RIDEV_INPUTSINK`; `unregister_raw_input()` removes that device using `RIDEV_REMOVE` and clears accumulated deltas.

`update_raw_input_state()` follows `dvars::m_rawInput->current.enabled`, registering only after `wnd_proc_hooked` and unregistering when disabled.

`restore_mouse_event_callsite()` restores the exact 5-byte `original_mouse_event_call` snapshot; `uninstall_wnd_proc()` unregisters raw input and restores `original_wnd_proc`.

`mouse_event_state` carries `int x`, `y`, `dx`, and `dy`; `callsite_patched`, `wnd_proc_hooked`, `raw_input_registered`, `ready_ticks`, `raw_mouse_x`, `raw_mouse_y`, `pending_event`, `original_call_state`, and `original_call_result` are process-local hook state.

entries.response:
**draw_version.cpp draws the configurable Project: Consolation watermark and game version text in the renderer pipeline.**

## Interface

- `draw_version::component::post_load() override` registers a renderer-pipeline scheduler loop invoking `cg_draw_watermark()` and `cg_draw_version()`.
- `REGISTER_COMPONENT(draw_version::component)` is commented out, so the component is currently not registered.

## Rendering Behavior

- `cg_draw_watermark()` requires enabled `dvars::cg_drawWatermark`, registers `"fonts/objectivefont"`, and draws `"Project: Consolation"` bottom-right at `watermark_font_scale = 0.25f`, with margins `watermark_margin_x = 8.0f` and `watermark_margin_y = 6.0f`.
- `cg_draw_version()` requires enabled `dvars::cg_drawVersion`, reads the `"version"` dvar through `game::Dvar_FindVar("version")`, registers `"fonts/consolefont"`, and draws the version bottom-right using `cg_drawVersionX` default `50.0f` and `cg_drawVersionY` default `18.0f`.
- `draw_text_shadowed()` emits `game::R_AddCmdDrawText` twice: shadow at `(x + shadow_offset_x, y + shadow_offset_y)` and foreground at `(x, y)`, with offsets `1.0f, 1.0f`, `shadow_color = {0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.65f}`, and `text_color = {0.86f, 0.82f, 0.72f, 0.60f}`.
- `watermark_font_scale = 0.25f` and `version_font_scale = 1.0f` control text scaling; `R_TextWidth` uses `0x7FFFFFFF` or `std::numeric_limits<int>::max()` character limits.

## Layout and Dependencies

- `resolve_layout_width(const game::ScreenPlacement&)` selects `max(realViewportSize)` then `max(virtualViewableMax)`, falling back to `640.0f`.
- `resolve_layout_height(const game::ScreenPlacement&)` selects `min(realViewportSize)` then `min(virtualViewableMax)`, falling back to `480.0f`.
- `get_layout_width()` and `get_layout_height()` query `game::ScrPlace_GetViewPlacement()`.
- `get_text_width()` returns scaled `game::R_TextWidth`; `get_line_height()` uses `Font_s::pixelHeight`, defaulting to `18.0f * scale`.
- Null/empty text, missing `Font_s`, missing fonts, invalid viewport width, and empty version dvar values abort drawing safely.
- `game::R_RegisterFont`, `game::R_AddCmdDrawText`, `game::R_TextWidth`, `game::Dvar_FindVar`, `dvars::*`, and `scheduler::pipeline::renderer` define runtime coupling and renderer lifecycle.

entries.response:
**xlive.cpp disables debugger detection in `xlive.dll`, hooks anti-debugging NT APIs, and continuously clears process debug state.**

## Public Interface

- `void apply_early()` clears PEB debug flags, installs NTDLL detours, patches `xlive.dll`, and starts `peb_cleaner_thread`.
- `class component final : public component_interface` overrides `void post_load()` to repeat `clear_peb_debug_flags()` and `patch_xlive()` after component loading.
- `component::post_load()` is defined, but `REGISTER_COMPONENT(xlive::component)` remains disabled under `DEBUG`.

## Anti-Debugging Hooks

- `nt_query_information_process_stub(HANDLE, UINT, PVOID, ULONG, PULONG) -> LONG` spoofs `process_debug_port = 7u` as zero with `status_success = 0x00000000L`, spoofs `process_debug_object_handle = 0x1Eu` as null with `status_port_not_set = 0xC0000353L`, and reports `process_debug_flags = 0x1Fu` as `1`; other classes delegate through `nt_query_information_process_hook`.
- `nt_set_information_thread_stub(HANDLE, UINT, PVOID, ULONG) -> LONG` returns `status_success` for `thread_hide_from_debugger = 0x11u`, otherwise invokes `nt_set_information_thread_hook`.
- `nt_set_information_process_stub(HANDLE, UINT, PVOID, ULONG) -> LONG` accepts `process_debug_flags` changes without effect and delegates all other classes through `nt_set_information_process_hook`.
- `nt_query_system_information_stub(UINT, PVOID, ULONG, PULONG) -> LONG` delegates through `nt_query_system_information_hook`, then rewrites `system_kernel_debugger_information = 0x23u` output bytes to `KernelDebuggerEnabled = FALSE` and `KernelDebuggerNotPresent = TRUE` when `status_success` and `info_len >= 2`.
- `nt_get_context_thread_stub(HANDLE, PCONTEXT) -> LONG` delegates through `nt_get_context_thread_hook` and zeros `CONTEXT_DEBUG_REGISTERS` fields `Dr0`, `Dr1`, `Dr2`, `Dr3`, `Dr6`, and `Dr7` on successful queries.
- `nt_set_context_thread_stub(HANDLE, const CONTEXT*) -> LONG` copies debug-register contexts, zeros `Dr0`–`Dr3`, `Dr6`, and `Dr7`, then invokes `nt_set_context_thread_hook` with the sanitized copy.
- `nt_set_debug_filter_state_stub(ULONG, ULONG, BOOLEAN) -> LONG` always returns `status_success`.
- `nt_yield_execution_stub() -> LONG` delegates to `nt_yield_execution_hook`.
- `is_debugger_present_stub() -> BOOL` always returns `FALSE`; `check_remote_debugger_present_stub(HANDLE, PBOOL) -> BOOL` writes `FALSE` when `present != nullptr` and returns `TRUE`.
- `output_debug_string_a_stub(LPCSTR)` and `output_debug_string_w_stub(LPCWSTR)` discard debug output.

## Patching and PE/Import Handling

- `mem_write(void*, const void*, size_t) -> bool` temporarily changes protection to `PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE`, copies bytes with `memcpy`, calls `FlushInstructionCache`, restores protection, and reports `VirtualProtect` failure.
- `scan(uint8_t*, size_t, const uint8_t*, size_t) -> uint8_t*` performs an exact byte-pattern search and returns `nullptr` for empty patterns, undersized images, or missing signatures.
- `get_module_range(const char*, uint8_t*&, size_t&) -> bool` resolves a module with `GetModuleHandleA`, validates `IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE` and `IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE`, and returns `IMAGE_NT_HEADERS::OptionalHeader.SizeOfImage`.
- `patch_xlive_imports(uint8_t*, size_t)` scans `IMAGE_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR` entries for case-insensitive `"kernel32.dll"` or `"kernel32"` and replaces `IsDebuggerPresent`, `CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent`, `OutputDebugStringA`, and `OutputDebugStringW` IAT entries via `mem_write`; malformed access is suppressed by `__try/__except (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER)`.
- `patch_peverifyhash(uint8_t*, size_t)` searches the 22-byte `prologue` signature, falls back to `peverifyhash_rva = 0x000F36B3u`, and overwrites the target with `ret_success = { 0x31, 0xC0, 0xC2, 0x0C, 0x00 }`, making `PEVerifyHash` return success with `ret 0x0C`.
- `patch_peverifyhash()` skips absent signatures, already-patched `ret_success`, or unexpected bytes; `dbg()` records `"PEVerifyHash patch skipped: signature missing"`, `"PEVerifyHash patch already applied"`, `"PEVerifyHash patch skipped: unexpected bytes at +0x%X"`, and `"PEVerifyHash patch applied at +0x%X"` in `DEBUG`.

## Lifecycle and Coupling

- `hook_ntdll()` installs `utils::hook::detour` instances for `NtQueryInformationProcess`, `NtSetInformationThread`, `NtSetInformationProcess`, `NtQuerySystemInformation`, `NtGetContextThread`, `NtSetContextThread`, `NtSetDebugFilterState`, and `NtYieldExecution` using `GetProcAddress`.
- `clear_peb_debug_flags()` uses x86 FS offsets `0x18` and `0x30`, clears PEB byte offset `0x02` (`BeingDebugged`) and DWORD offset `0x68` (`NtGlobalFlag`), and safely returns when the PEB is null.
- `peb_cleaner_thread(LPVOID) -> DWORD` runs indefinitely, calling `clear_peb_debug_flags()` followed by `Sleep(16)`, so `apply_early()` intentionally creates a persistent thread and immediately closes its handle.
- `patch_xlive()` targets only the loaded `"xlive.dll"` module and applies `patch_peverifyhash()` plus `patch_xlive_imports()`.
- `dbg(const char*, ...)` formats into a 512-byte buffer and emits `[xlive] ` through `OutputDebugStringA` in `DEBUG`; the release implementation is a no-op.
- `std_include.hpp`, `utils/hook.hpp`, `loader/component_loader.hpp`, and `xlive.hpp` supply Windows types, detour machinery, component integration, and xlive declarations.

entries.response:
**clock.hpp defines the monotonic timing primitives for the gamepad controller subsystem.**

## Exports

- `clock` aliases `chrono::steady_clock` as `base`, with `base::time_point` (`time_point`) and `base::duration` (`duration`); `static_assert(base::is_steady, "...")` enforces monotonicity.
- `clock::now() noexcept -> time_point` returns `base::now()`.
- `clock::since_epoch() noexcept -> duration` returns process-relative elapsed time from a first-use-fixed epoch.
- `timestamp` aliases `clock::time_point`.
- `seconds` aliases `chrono::duration<float>`; `milliseconds` aliases `chrono::duration<float, std::milli>`.
- `latency_span` stores `timestamp acquired{}` and `timestamp consumed{}`; `latency_span::latency() const noexcept -> clock::duration` computes `consumed - acquired`.

## Contracts

`clock`, `timestamp`, and `latency_span` form one comparable time source for acquisition, publication, and consumption; `latency_span::latency()` assumes `consumed >= acquired` and performs no validation. `types.hpp` and `utility.hpp` supply required controller support and chrono dependencies.

entries.response:
**context.hpp does define the shared, non-owning service view passed through controller subsystems.**

## Interface

- `context(diagnostic_sink& sink, bool developer) noexcept` stores a borrowed `diagnostic_sink` and immutable developer-mode flag.
- `diagnostic_sink& diagnostics() const noexcept` returns the shared diagnostic sink.
- `bool developer() const noexcept` gates verbose reporting and developer-only tooling without changing decoding.
- `void report(severity, facility, errc, device_id, string message) const` reports device-scoped diagnostics.
- `void report(severity, facility, errc, string message) const` reports diagnostics without a device identifier.

## Design

`context` owns no services or mutable state; runtime-owned `diagnostic_sink` is shared across device, driver, sample, aim, and engine layers. `clock.hxx` remains a directly consulted stateless monotonic source rather than a context dependency. `types.hpp`, `utility.hpp`, `error.hpp`, `diagnostic.hpp`, and `device/id.hpp` supply shared types.

**ultrawide.cpp does runtime ultrawide/custom-aspect-ratio management through game dvars, renderer memory, console commands, and lifecycle hooks.**

## Role and Integration

`ultrawide::component` integrates with `component_interface` and registers through `REGISTER_COMPONENT(ultrawide::component)`. `post_load()` schedules initialization on `scheduler::main`; `pre_destroy()` clears `dvars::r_aspectRatioCustomEnable`, `dvars::r_aspectRatioCustom`, and `dvars::r_ultrawideCustomMode`.

`game::game_offset()` resolves hard-coded renderer addresses; `game::Dvar_FindVar()` accesses `wideScreen`, `r_isWideScreen`, and diagnostic `cl_ingame`; `dvars::Dvar_RegisterBool`, `Dvar_RegisterFloat`, and `Dvar_RegisterString` create persistent configuration; `command::add` and `command::execute` implement console control; `console::info` reports usage, state, and errors.

## Public Symbols

- `ultrawide::component` — `final` component class derived from `component_interface`.
- `ultrawide::component::post_load() override` — registers dvars and commands inside a one-shot main-thread scheduler callback.
- `ultrawide::component::pre_destroy() override` — nulls the three ultrawide dvar pointers.

## Configuration and Commands

`r_aspectRatioCustomEnable` is a saved bool defaulting to `0`, controlling custom ratio activation.

`r_aspectRatioCustom` is a saved float defaulting to `16.0f / 9.0f`, clamped to `4.0f / 3.0f` through `63.0f / 9.0f`; its documented ratio is width divided by height.

`r_ultrawideCustomMode` is a saved string defaulting to `"disabled"` and stores a custom `WxH` resolution for Consolation.

`setcustomres` requires `<width>x<height>`, writes `r_customMode`, `r_ultrawideCustomMode`, `r_aspectRatioCustomEnable`, and `r_aspectRatioCustom`, then queues `vid_restart`; invalid input prints `"usage: setcustomres <width>x<height>\n"`.

`clearcustomres` resets sticky state, writes `"disabled"` to `r_customMode` and `r_ultrawideCustomMode`, disables `r_aspectRatioCustomEnable`, and queues `vid_restart`.

`dumpultrawide` prints enabled/custom values, `cl_ingame`, `game::keyCatchers` as `0x%X`, scalar aspect, renderer ratio, monitor/render aspects, `wideScreen`, and `r_isWideScreen`; unavailable pointers serialize as `-1` or `0`.

## Aspect-Ratio Algorithm

`parse_resolution(const std::string& text, int& width, int& height) -> bool` parses exactly two positive integers with `std::sscanf(text.c_str(), "%ix%i", &width, &height) == 2`; malformed or non-positive dimensions fail.

`sync_sticky_custom_resolution_state()` parses `r_ultrawideCustomMode->current.string`, enabling `sticky_custom_resolution_enabled` and computing `sticky_custom_ratio` when valid; invalid or absent state falls back to `false` and `16.0f / 9.0f`.

`set_bool_dvar(game::dvar_s* dvar, bool value)` synchronizes `current.enabled`, `latched.enabled`, and `reset.enabled`; `set_float_dvar(game::dvar_s* dvar, float value)` synchronizes the corresponding `.value` fields.

`apply_custom_aspect_ratio()` captures original values once, forces sticky custom settings, clamps the active ratio, preserves `aspect_ratio_scalar`, updates renderer/monitor/render aspect fields, and synchronizes `wideScreen` plus `r_isWideScreen` using the `1.5f` widescreen threshold.

## Renderer Contracts

`aspect_ratio_scalar` is `0x1127BAEC`; `custom_mode_fullscreen_gate` is `0x103BE1C9` but currently unused.

`renderer_aspect_ratio`, `renderer_monitor_width`, `renderer_monitor_height`, `renderer_render_width`, `renderer_render_height`, `renderer_monitor_aspect`, and `renderer_render_aspect` resolve `0x10E271AC`, `0x10E27190`, `0x10E27194`, `0x10E27198`, `0x10E2719C`, `0x10E271B0`, and `0x10E271B4`.

`apply_custom_aspect_ratio()` computes monitor aspect as `monitor_height * custom_ratio / monitor_width` and render aspect as `custom_ratio * render_height / render_width`; disabled mode restores captured renderer values.

**filesystem.cpp does prioritized filesystem search-path management and hooks engine startup, script execution, and install-path resolution.**

## Public API

- `std::string read_file(const std::string& path)` searches registered paths in priority order and returns the first readable file or `{}`.
- `bool read_file(const std::string& path, std::string* data, std::string* real_path)` fills file contents and optionally the resolved path, returning `false` when unresolved.
- `bool find_file(const std::string& path, std::string* real_path)` resolves the first existing file and writes its path to `real_path`.
- `bool exists(const std::string& path)` checks whether any registered search path contains `path`.
- `void enable_engine_search_paths(bool enable)` toggles engine-path registration and immediately registers paths when enabled.
- `bool engine_search_paths_enabled()` returns `engine_paths_enabled`.
- `void register_path(const std::filesystem::path& path)` prepends unique paths after `initialized` becomes true.
- `void unregister_path(const std::filesystem::path& path)` removes matching registered paths after initialization.
- `std::vector<std::string> get_search_paths()` returns paths in lookup priority order.
- `std::vector<std::string> get_search_paths_rev()` returns paths in reverse lookup order.
- `class component final : public component_interface` installs filesystem hooks through `post_load()`.

## Search-Path State

- `get_search_paths_internal()` owns a process-lifetime `std::deque<std::filesystem::path>`; `register_path()` uses `push_front`, so later registrations override earlier ones.
- `fs_startup_stub(const char* name)` sets `initialized`, resets `engine_paths_registered`, and registers `.`, `consolation`, `raw`, `userraw`, plus `%APPDATA%\Activision\Quantum of Solace\players`.
- `get_default_players_directory()` uses `SHGetFolderPathA(..., CSIDL_APPDATA, ..., SHGFP_TYPE_CURRENT, ...)`; failure returns an empty string.
- `register_engine_search_paths()` requires `engine_paths_enabled`, `!engine_paths_registered`, and a nonempty `std::filesystem::current_path()`.
- `add_engine_search_path()` calls game offset `0x10272AE0` for `"consolation"`, `"raw"`, and `"userraw"` rooted at the current directory.
- `register_path()` and `unregister_path()` are no-ops before `initialized`; `can_insert_path()` compares paths exactly without canonicalization.

## `exec` Behavior

- `normalize_exec_path(std::string path)` appends `.cfg` when no extension exists after the final `/` or `\`.
- `exec_stub()` delegates to `exec_hook` unless command nesting has exactly two args, the requested path is nonempty, or `read_file()` fails.
- `exec_stub()` delegates `config_mp.cfg` and `gfxConfig.cfg` case-insensitively via `_stricmp`.
- `exec_stub()` logs `execing %s from %s\n`, appends a terminal newline when absent, injects contents with `game::Cbuf_AddText(0, ...)`, and returns `1`.
- `exec_disk_log_stub()` logs resolved files as `execing %s from %s\n` or unresolved files as `execing %s from disk\n`.

## Engine Integration

- `component::post_load()` detours `0x10272D80` with `fs_startup_stub` and `0x103F5960` with `exec_stub`.
- `component::post_load()` jumps `0x10274AA0` to `sys_default_install_path_stub`, which returns `utils::nt::get_host_module().get_folder()`.
- `component::post_load()` redirects call site `0x103F589B` to `exec_disk_log_stub`; `REGISTER_COMPONENT(filesystem::component)` activates registration.
- `fs_startup_hook`, `exec_hook`, `game::command_id`, `game::cmd_argc`, `game::cmd_argv`, `game::Com_Printf`, and `utils::io` define runtime coupling and require the targeted 32-bit game layout, including inline `__asm` in `add_engine_search_path()`.

**sounds.cpp overrides streamed music files with mod-provided assets and patches Miles Sound System stream handling.**

## Public Interface

- `sounds::component` is a `component_interface` implementation exposing `post_load()` and `pre_destroy()`.
- `sounds::component::post_load() -> void` detours `_AIL_set_stream_loop_block@12`, then redirects `music_stream_callsite_1`, `music_stream_callsite_2`, `music_stream_callsite_3`, `ail_open_stream_callsite_1`, and `ail_open_stream_callsite_2`.
- `sounds::component::pre_destroy() -> void` clears `ail_set_stream_loop_block_hook`.
- `REGISTER_COMPONENT(sounds::component)` is commented out, so automatic component registration is disabled in the shown source.

## Override Resolution

- `find_music_override(const char*** request) -> std::string` checks alias and streamed-file metadata, generates ordered candidates, and returns the first path accepted by `filesystem::find_file`.
- `sanitize_name(std::string value) -> std::string` replaces `\ / : * ? " < > |` with `_` before alias-derived lookup.
- Alias candidates use exact formats `sounds/music/{}.mp3` and `sounds/music/{}.wav`.
- File metadata candidates use exact formats `sounds/music/{}`, `sounds/music/{}.mp3`, and `sounds/music/{}.wav`.
- `try_get_alias_name(const char*** request) -> const char*` reads `(*request)[0]`; `try_get_file_info(const char*** request) -> const streamed_sound_file_view*` reads `(*request)[4]`.
- `streamed_sound_file_view` stores `const char* directory` and `const char* name`; guarded readers use MSVC `__try/__except (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER)` to tolerate invalid engine pointers.
- `add_candidate(std::vector<std::string>& candidates, const std::string& value) -> void` rejects empty and duplicate paths.

## Hook Behavior

- `open_music_stream_stub(const char*** request, int index) -> int` resolves `current_override_path`, optionally calls `show_override_notice`, invokes `streamed_sound_open_function` at `game::game_offset(...)`, then clears thread-local state via `gsl::finally`.
- `ail_open_stream_stub(int driver, const char* filename, int flags) -> int` resolves `_AIL_open_stream@12` from `mss32.dll`, substitutes `current_override_path`, and returns `0` when the export is unavailable.
- `ail_set_stream_loop_block_stub(int stream, int loop_start, int loop_end) -> void` suppresses loop-block updates for overrides; otherwise forwards through `ail_set_stream_loop_block_hook`.
- `current_override_path` is `thread_local`; `override_notice_mutex` and `last_notified_override` deduplicate debug notices across threads.

**profile_patches.cpp does profile-config migration, decryption, deduplication, synchronization, and lifecycle integration for Quantum of Solace multiplayer profiles.**

## Role and Integration

`profile_patches::component` implements `component_interface` and registers through `REGISTER_COMPONENT(profile_patches::component)`; `post_load()` installs commands, scheduler callbacks, and shutdown synchronization.

`game::game_offset`, `game::dvar_s`, and `game::Com_Printf` couple profile handling to engine memory, dvars, and console output; `utils::io::read_file`, `write_file`, and `file_exists` handle filesystem access; `SHGetFolderPathA` resolves `%APPDATA%`; `command::add` exposes console commands; `scheduler::once`, `scheduler::loop`, and `scheduler::on_shutdown` control lifecycle execution.

## Public Interface

`profile_patches::component::post_load() override` schedules initialization on `scheduler::main`, polls profile changes every `250ms`, and exports stock configuration back to the custom file during shutdown.

`REGISTER_COMPONENT(profile_patches::component)` makes `profile_patches::component` discoverable by the component loader.

## Paths, Dvars, and Constants

`default_profile_config_name` is `"config_mp.cfg"`; `custom_profile_config_name` is `"consolation_mp.cfg"`; `decrypted_profile_config_name` is `"consolation_mp_decrypted.cfg"`.

`get_dvar_string(std::size_t dvar_ptr_address)` reads a `game::dvar_s*` through `game::game_offset`; offsets `0x114E7068` and `0x10806824` represent the players-root dvar and profile-name dvar.

`get_players_directory()` prefers the configured players-root dvar, otherwise resolves `CSIDL_APPDATA` and appends `"Activision\\Quantum of Solace\\players"`; `get_profile_name()` returns the configured profile string or `""`.

`join_path(const std::string& base, const std::string& leaf)` preserves existing trailing `\\` or `/`, returns `leaf` for an empty base, and otherwise inserts `\\`.

`build_profile_file_path(const char* filename)` returns `<players-directory>\\<profile-name>\\<filename>` or `{}` when either directory or profile name is unavailable.

`build_profile_config_path()` targets `"config_mp.cfg"`; `build_custom_profile_config_path()` targets `"consolation_mp.cfg"`; `build_legacy_shared_config_path()` targets the custom filename directly under the players directory.

`build_runtime_config_path()` aliases the profile-scoped custom config; `build_decrypted_output_path()` targets the profile-scoped decrypted filename, falling back to the players directory when necessary.

## Config Recognition and Normalization

`looks_like_plaintext_config(const std::string& data)` rejects empty data and data with fewer than `85%` printable characters, then requires `"seta "`, `"set "`, or `"unbindall"`.

`to_lower(std::string value)` lowercases keys using unsigned-character-safe `std::tolower`; `trim_copy(const std::string& value)` removes leading and trailing spaces, tabs, carriage returns, and newlines.

`find_canonical_dvar_name(const std::string& key)` canonicalizes case-insensitive spellings for `con_outputHeightScale`, `cg_fovScale`, `input_viewSensitivity`, `ui_smallFont`, `ui_bigFont`, `ui_extraBigFont`, `r_lodScale`, `m_rawInput`, `bot_maxHealth`, `g_debugVelocity`, and `g_debugLocalization`.

`try_parse_dvar_assignment(std::string& line, std::string* key)` recognizes only lines beginning with exact prefixes `"seta "` or `"set "`, extracts and lowercases the dvar key, and rewrites recognized names to canonical casing.

`should_strip_runtime_only_dvar(const std::string& key)` removes `r_aspectratiocustom`, `r_aspectratiocustomenable`, `r_custommode`, and `r_ultrawidecustommode`.

`dedupe_config_text(const std::string& data)` preserves non-assignment lines, normalizes recognized assignments, removes runtime-only dvars, and retains only the last assignment for each lowercased key; output uses `"\r\n"` when input contains CRLF, otherwise `"\n"`.

`dedupe_custom_profile_config()` operates only when `should_use_custom_profile_config()` detects an existing plaintext-like custom config, rewriting it only when deduplication changes content.

## Decryption and Conversion

`decrypt_in_place(std::string& data)` invokes the engine `__stdcall` transform at `game::game_offset(0x103ECCA0)` with the mutable data pointer and `int` byte length.

`try_decode_config_to_plaintext(std::string& data)` accepts recognized plaintext unchanged, otherwise decrypts in place and validates with `looks_like_plaintext_config`.

`convert_config_to_path(const std::string& source_path, const std::string& fallback_path, const std::string& output_path, const char* command_name)` loads `source_path` first, falls back to `fallback_path`, decrypts non-plaintext input, validates the result, writes `output_path`, and emits diagnostic messages through `print_profile_message`; empty output paths, missing sources, invalid decrypted data, and write failures return `false`.

`migrate_config()` converts the profile-scoped stock config, or runtime custom config as fallback, into `consolation_mp_decrypted.cfg`.

`convert_config()` converts legacy shared custom config, or stock profile config as fallback, into the profile-scoped custom config.

`import_custom_profile_config_into_stock()` reads the profile-scoped custom config or legacy shared config, decodes and deduplicates plaintext, writes custom plaintext, re-encrypts a copy with `decrypt_in_place`, and writes encrypted stock config.

`export_stock_profile_config_to_custom()` reads and decodes stock config, deduplicates plaintext, and writes the custom profile config.

## Console Commands

`profile_decrypt_config` invokes `migrate_config()`.

`profile_convert_config` invokes `convert_config()`, `dedupe_custom_profile_config()`, `import_custom_profile_config_into_stock()`, and `print_runtime_config_path()`.

`profile_sync_config` invokes `import_custom_profile_config_into_stock()` and reports `^3profile:config synced %s into %s\n` or `^1profile:config failed to sync plaintext config into stock profile config\n`.

`profile_show_config_path` invokes `print_runtime_config_path()`.

`profile_dedupe_config` invokes `dedupe_custom_profile_config()` and then prints the runtime path.

`print_profile_message(const char* fmt, ...)` formats into a fixed `1024`-byte buffer via `vsnprintf` and sends channel `16` output through `game::Com_Printf`.

`print_runtime_config_path()` emits `^3profile:config runtime config path is unavailable\n` for unavailable paths or `^3profile:config %s\n` for resolved paths.

## Lifecycle Behavior

`post_load()` uses `scheduler::once(..., scheduler::main)` to register commands and perform initial deduplication.

`post_load()` uses `scheduler::loop(..., scheduler::main, 250ms)` with static `imported_profile` and `missing_profile` sentinels to avoid repeated work; profile changes trigger `import_custom_profile_config_into_stock()`, while missing sources suppress retries until the profile name changes.

`post_load()` uses `scheduler::on_shutdown(...)` to call `export_stock_profile_config_to_custom()` followed by `dedupe_custom_profile_config()`.

`post_load()` deliberately leaves the game’s active config filename and save path unchanged, so automatic engine-path patching remains disabled while signed-in startup-freeze behavior is investigated.

entries.response:
**diagnostic.cpp does controller diagnostic stringification, sink formatting, and console emission.**

## Public symbols

- `const char* to_string(facility f) noexcept` maps all `facility` values to lowercase labels; unknown values fall back to `"runtime"`.
- `const char* to_string(severity s) noexcept` maps `severity::info`, `severity::warning`, and `severity::error`; unknown values fall back to `"info"`.
- `void logging_sink::consume(const diagnostic& d)` formats and emits one diagnostic through `console::info`, `console::warn`, or `console::error`.
- `void report(diagnostic_sink& sink, severity level, facility origin, errc code, device_id device, string message)` constructs `diagnostic{level, origin, code, device, move(message)}` and calls `sink.consume`.

## Behavioral contracts

`logging_sink::consume` emits `controller: <facility>: <message> [<code>] device=<id>\n`; `[<code>]` is omitted for `errc::none`, and `device=<id>` is omitted when `d.device` is empty. `to_string(facility)` recognizes `runtime`, `discovery`, `transport`, `driver`, `decode`, `sample`, `calibration`, `mapping`, `aim`, `steam`, `engine`, `debug`.

## Coupling

`diagnostic.cpp` depends on `diagnostic.hpp` types and `component::engine::console::console.hpp`; `logging_sink::consume` relies on one-shot console accumulator flushing per emitted line.
