entries.response:
**hid.cpp does Windows HID enumeration, capability classification, overlapped I/O, and feature-report transport for supported PlayStation gamepads.**

## Public interface

Namespace: `gamepad::unstable::controller::transport`.

- `connection classify_link (size_t input_length) noexcept` maps `78` to `connection::bluetooth`, `64` to `connection::usb`, and every other length to `connection::unknown`.
- `vector<hid_enumeration_entry> enumerate (const context& ctx)` discovers present HID game-pad collections, filters supported PlayStation vendor/product identities, classifies USB/Bluetooth framing, and reports unsupported framing through `ctx.report`.
- `unique_ptr<hid_device> open (const context& ctx, const wstring& path)` opens a HID interface with overlapped I/O, retries read-only access after read/write failure, re-queries capabilities, validates controller identity/framing, and returns a configured `windows_hid_device` through the `hid_device` interface.

## HID device implementation

- `windows_hid_device` implements `hid_device` with `HANDLE handle_`, `hid_attributes attributes_`, `connection link_`, `size_t input_length_`, `size_t feature_length_`, `OVERLAPPED overlapped_`, and fixed `array<byte, max_report_size> buf_`.
- `windows_hid_device::link () const noexcept` returns the `connection` selected by `classify_link`.
- `windows_hid_device::attributes () const noexcept` returns the cached `hid_attributes`.
- `windows_hid_device::feature_report_length () const noexcept` returns the clamped `feature_length_`.
- `windows_hid_device::read (span<byte> out) noexcept` maintains one outstanding overlapped `ReadFile`, returns `size_t(0)` for `ERROR_IO_INCOMPLETE`, copies completed bytes from `buf_` into `out`, truncates to `out.size()`, and re-arms the next read.
- `windows_hid_device::write (span<const byte> buf) noexcept` returns `nullopt` when `writable_` or `buf` is invalid, otherwise submits overlapped `WriteFile` with a per-call manual-reset event and returns the completed byte count.
- `windows_hid_device::get_feature (span<byte> buf) noexcept` requires `buf.size() >= feature_length_` and calls `HidD_GetFeature`; `HidD_GetFeature` sizes transfers from the supplied buffer and rejects shorter buffers with `ERROR_INVALID_USER_BUFFER`.
- `windows_hid_device::set_feature (span<const byte> buf) noexcept` requires writable access and a non-empty buffer, then calls `HidD_SetFeature` through `const_cast<byte*>`.
- `windows_hid_device::writable (bool w) noexcept` updates the output/feature-write permission flag.
- `windows_hid_device::issue_read () noexcept` resets `overlapped_.hEvent`, clears `OVERLAPPED::Internal` and `OVERLAPPED::InternalHigh`, starts `ReadFile`, and treats synchronous completion or `ERROR_IO_PENDING` as an active read.
- `~windows_hid_device ()` cancels active reads with `CancelIoEx`, blocks through `GetOverlappedResult`, closes `overlapped_.hEvent`, and closes `handle_`; `CancelIo` is intentionally avoided because teardown may run on a different thread.

## Enumeration pipeline

- `enumerate` obtains the HID interface class GUID through `HidD_GetHidGuid` and enumerates `DIGCF_PRESENT | DIGCF_DEVICEINTERFACE` entries via `SetupDiGetClassDevsW` and `SetupDiEnumDeviceInterfaces`.
- `interface_path (HDEVINFO set, SP_DEVICE_INTERFACE_DATA& iface)` performs the `SetupDiGetDeviceInterfaceDetailW` two-call size/query idiom and returns an `optional<wstring>` device path.
- `open_for_query (const wstring& path) noexcept` calls `CreateFileW` with desired access `0` and sharing `FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE`, allowing capability inspection without contending for exclusive controller handles.
- `query_caps (HANDLE h) noexcept` obtains `PHIDP_PREPARSED_DATA` through `HidD_GetPreparsedData`, extracts `HIDP_CAPS` via `HidP_GetCaps`, frees preparsed data with `HidD_FreePreparsedData`, and returns `collection_caps`.
- `collection_caps` stores `size_t input_report_length`, `size_t feature_report_length`, `uint16_t usage_page`, and `uint16_t usage`.
- `usage_page_generic_desktop` equals `0x01`; `usage_game_pad` equals `0x05`, so only the Generic Desktop/Game Pad top-level collection is accepted.
- `enumerate` caches `HIDD_ATTRIBUTES::VendorID`, `HIDD_ATTRIBUTES::ProductID`, and `HIDD_ATTRIBUTES::VersionNumber`, rejects `classify(vendor, product) == family::unknown`, and emits `hid_enumeration_entry {move(*path), hid_attributes {vendor, product, attrs.VersionNumber}, link, caps->input_report_length}`.
- `enumerate` reports `errc::transport_failure` with `"unable to enumerate HID device interfaces"` when `SetupDiGetClassDevsW` fails.
- `enumerate` reports `errc::ambiguous_identity` with `"HID device " + to_string(classify(vendor, product)) + " reports an input report of " + std::to_string(caps->input_report_length) + " bytes; the drivers decode 64-byte (USB) and 78-byte (Bluetooth) framing, so no driver is bound"` for recognized controllers with unknown report lengths.
- `enumerate` always calls `SetupDiDestroyDeviceInfoList (set)` before returning discovered entries.

## Open and validation behavior

- `open` first requests `GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE` with `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` and sharing `FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE`; failure triggers a `GENERIC_READ` retry and sets `writable = false`.
- `open` reports `errc::transport_failure` with `"unable to open a HID device interface"` when both `CreateFileW` attempts fail.
- `open` re-queries `HidD_GetAttributes` and `query_caps` after opening because the device may detach or change between enumeration and activation.
- `open` reports `errc::transport_failure` with `"opened HID device does not answer its capabilities"` when capability acquisition fails.
- `open` rejects `classify(vendor, product) == family::unknown` or `classify_link(caps->input_report_length) == connection::unknown`, reports `errc::ambiguous_identity` with `"opened HID device is not a controller we can decode"`, and closes the handle.
- `open` reports `severity::info`, `facility::transport`, `errc::none`, and `"HID device opened read-only; output reports unavailable"` after successful read-only fallback.
- `windows_hid_device` clamps `input_length` and `feature_length` with `std::min(..., max_report_size)` before any transfer.

## Behavioral contracts and constants

- `max_report_size` is `128`, fixing the non-allocating input buffer capacity and limiting both HID report lengths.
- `usb_input_report_length` is `64`; `bluetooth_input_report_length` is `78`; `classify_link` uses report-descriptor lengths rather than interface-path or physical-bus detection.
- `connection::usb` and `connection::bluetooth` identify report framing/layout, including report ID position, common-block offset, and optional trailing CRC-32; they do not independently guarantee the physical transport bus.
- `read` returns `nullopt` for a missing event, failed read, or invalid transport state; `read` returns `size_t(0)` while a read remains in flight.
- `write` and `set_feature` are disabled after read-only opening; `get_feature` remains available when `feature_length_` is satisfied.
- `windows_hid_device` is non-copyable through deleted `windows_hid_device (const windows_hid_device&)` and `operator=`.
- `HANDLE`, `HDEVINFO`, `SP_DEVICE_INTERFACE_DATA`, `HIDD_ATTRIBUTES`, `HIDP_CAPS`, `OVERLAPPED`, `HidD_*`, `HidP_GetCaps`, `SetupDi*`, `CreateFileW`, `ReadFile`, `WriteFile`, `CancelIoEx`, and `GetOverlappedResult` couple the implementation to Windows HID, SetupAPI, and overlapped kernel I/O.
- `std_include.hpp` supplies project aliases such as `optional`, `nullopt`, `span`, `array`, `vector`, `wstring`, `unique_ptr`, `byte`, and `move`; `hid.hpp` supplies `hid_device`, `hid_enumeration_entry`, `hid_attributes`, `connection`, `context`, `vendor_id`, `product_id`, `family`, `severity`, `facility`, and `errc`.

entries.response:
**diagnostic.hpp defines structured gamepad diagnostics, sinks, severity/facility taxonomies, and reporting APIs.**

## Public symbols

- `facility : uint8_t` enumerates `runtime`, `discovery`, `transport`, `driver`, `decode`, `sample`, `calibration`, `mapping`, `aim`, `steam`, `engine`, `debug`.
- `to_string(facility) noexcept` returns `const char*`.
- `severity : uint8_t` enumerates `info`, `warning`, `error`.
- `to_string(severity) noexcept` returns `const char*`.
- `diagnostic` stores `severity level {severity::info}`, `facility origin {facility::runtime}`, `errc code {errc::none}`, `device_id device {}`, and `string message`; `no_device` denotes device-independent conditions.
- `diagnostic_sink` defines virtual `~diagnostic_sink() = default` and pure virtual `consume(const diagnostic&)`.
- `logging_sink : diagnostic_sink` overrides `consume(const diagnostic&)`, formatting records for the logger.
- `report(diagnostic_sink&, severity, facility, errc, device_id, string)` builds and dispatches one record.
- Inline `report(diagnostic_sink&, severity, facility, errc, string)` delegates with `no_device` and `move(message)`.

## Integration and design

`types.hpp` supplies `string`, `move`, and related support types; `utility.hpp`, `error.hpp`, and `device/id.hpp` supply utility, `errc`, `device_id`, and `no_device`. `diagnostic_sink` uses the Observer/Strategy pattern for test/debug sinks, while `logging_sink` is the default logger adapter; virtual dispatch remains off the hot path.

**error.hpp defines stable gamepad controller error codes, string/stream formatting, and cold-path exception transport.**

## Public API

`errc : uint8_t` enumerates `none`, `device_unavailable`, `ambiguous_identity`, `unsupported_device`, `transport_failure`, `report_malformed`, `report_truncated`, `checksum_mismatch`, `output_rejected`, `calibration_invalid`, `calibration_version`, `graph_invalid`, `binding_invalid`, `steam_unavailable`, `steam_unsuitable`, `hook_failed`, and `dvar_registration`.

`errc` is the shared identity for throwing and non-throwing diagnostic channels; `to_string` tokens are machine-grep-able and stable.

`types.hpp` supplies `uint8_t`, `string`, `ostream`, and `runtime_error`; `utility.hpp` supplies related controller support utilities.

entries.response:
**gsc.cpp does custom GSC script loading, execution, replacement, asset lookup, and compile-error integration through game-engine hooks.**

## Public Interface

- `add_function(const char* name, game::function_t func, int type)` lowercases `name` via `utils::string::to_lower` and stores `{call=func, developer=type}` in `scr_functions`.
- `add_method(const char* name, game::method_t func, int type)` lowercases `name` and stores `{call=func, developer=type}` in `scr_methods`.
- `gsc::component` is a `component_interface` implementation whose `post_load()` installs all active hooks and registers the `replacefunc` GSC function.
- `REGISTER_COMPONENT(gsc::component)` registers `gsc::component` with the component loader.

## Script Loading and Execution

- `load_script(const std::string& name)` calls `game::Scr_LoadScript(name.data())`, retrieves `"main"` and `"init"` handles through `game::Scr_GetFunctionHandle`, and records nonzero handles in `main_handles` or `init_handles`; `custom_script_name` is computed as `name + ".gsc"s` but unused.
- `load_scripts(const std::filesystem::path& root_dir, const std::filesystem::path& subfolder)` scans `root_dir/subfolder`, filters filenames ending in `.gsc`, derives a root-relative path without the final four characters, and forwards the base name to `load_script`.
- `load_gametype_script_stub()` invokes engine offset `0x101A8A70`, then scans every `filesystem::get_search_paths()` entry under `scripts/` and `scripts/mp/`.
- `g_load_structs_stub()` executes every `main_handles` entry with `game::Scr_ExecThread`, releases each result through `game::RemoveRefToObject`, then invokes engine offset `0x10188010`.
- `save_reigstered_weapons_stub()` executes every `init_handles` entry with `game::Scr_ExecThread`, releases each result, then invokes engine offset `0x10179920`; the misspelled identifier is part of the source API.
- `main_handles` and `init_handles` retain engine script handles until the `scheduler::on_shutdown` callback clears them.

## Custom Raw-File Resolution

- `read_raw_script_file(const std::string& name, std::string* data)` returns `true` when `filesystem::read_file(name, data)` succeeds and otherwise returns `false`; the fallback `DB_XAssetExists`/`DB_GetRawBuffer` implementation is disabled in comments.
- `load_custom_script(const char* file_name)` memoizes `game::RawFile*` values in `loaded_scripts`, rejects unreadable or empty files, allocates `RawFile`, null-terminated `name`, and null-terminated `buffer` through `utils::memory::allocate`, and sets `len` to `source_buffer.size() + 1`.
- `find_script(game::XAssetType type, const char* name, int allow_create_default)` checks `load_custom_script(name)` before delegating to `game::DB_FindXAssetHeader_Internal(type, name, allow_create_default).rawfile`.
- `GSC_DUMPING` enables `find_script` output to `gsc_dump/%s` using `utils::io::write_file` and logs `Dumped %s`.
- `loaded_scripts` stores allocated script assets without an explicit deallocation path; `scheduler::on_shutdown` clears map entries but does not visibly free the allocated `RawFile`, name, or buffer memory.

## Function and Method Dispatch

- `player_get_method_stub(const char** name)` resolves lowercase-compatible registered methods from `scr_methods`, returning `game::scr_method_t::call`, and falls back to engine offset `0x1015AD00`.
- `scr_get_function_stub(const char** name, int* type)` resolves `scr_functions`, writes `game::scr_function_t::developer` into `*type`, returns `game::scr_function_t::call`, and falls back to engine offset `0x10197460`.
- `player_get_method_stub` and `scr_get_function_stub` are currently inactive because their `utils::hook::call` sites in `component::post_load()` are commented out.
- `replacefunc` requires exactly two parameters; otherwise it logs `replacefunc: two parameters are required.\n` through `console::error` and returns.
- `get_code_pos_for_param(int index)` validates `index < game::scrVmPub->outparamcount` and `VAR_FUNCTION` type, invokes engine error offset `0x10235640` with exact messages `"get_code_pos_for_param: Index is out of range!\n"` or `"get_code_pos_for_param: Invalid type! (Expects a function as parameter)\n"`, and returns `""` on failure.
- `set_replaced_pos(const char* what, const char* with)` rejects empty strings with `Invalid parameters passed to set_replaced_pos\n`, warns when `replaced_functions` already contains `what`, and stores the `what -> with` code-position mapping.
- `get_replaced_pos(const char* pos)` assigns `replaced_pos` from `replaced_functions[pos]` when present; `replaced_pos` is reset to `nullptr` after VM redirection.
- `vm_execute_stub()` is an x86 inline-assembly VM redirection stub that substitutes `edx` with `replaced_pos`, reads one opcode byte, updates engine globals at `0x116377F8` and `0x11738440`, and returns through `0x10237866`; its jump hook at `0x1023784C` is commented out.

## Compile-Error Reporting

- `format(va_list* ap, const char* message)` formats into a `static thread_local char buffer[0x1000]` using `vsnprintf_s(buffer, _TRUNCATE, message, *ap)` and returns `{}` when formatting fails.
- `Scr_PrintSourcePos(const char* a2, const char* a3, unsigned int a4)` truncates source text to 1023 bytes, converts tab characters (`'\t'`) to spaces, strips a trailing carriage return (`'\r'`), annotates savegames with `" (savegame)"`, and logs `(file '%s'%s, line %d)\n`.
- `compile_error_stub(const char* fmt, ...)` formats the variadic error, prints the exact banner `******* script compile error *******`, reports source position using globals `0x118B5224` and `0x118B522C`, and terminates with `game::Com_Error(..., "script compile error\n%s\n%s\n(see console for details)\n", ...)`.
- `compile_error_2_stub(const char* fmt, ...)` formats the error, resolves a code position with `game::Scr_FormatCodePos`, prints the same compile-error banner, and terminates through `game::Com_Error` using the same error template.
- `compile_error_hook` detours engine offset `0x1022DD40` to `compile_error_stub`; `compile_error_2_hook` detours `0x1022DC70` to `compile_error_2_stub`.

## Hook and Lifecycle Contract

- `component::post_load()` calls `load_gametype_script_stub` at `0x101A8ED4`, `g_load_structs_stub` at `0x101AD1FA`, `save_reigstered_weapons_stub` at `0x101AD27A`, and `find_script` at `0x1022DC10`.
- `scheduler::on_shutdown` clears `main_handles`, `init_handles`, `replaced_functions`, and `loaded_scripts`; `scr_functions` and `scr_methods` are not cleared.

entries.response:
**fastfiles.cpp hooks asset linking and file I/O to support fastfile/Scaleform overrides, diagnostics, deferred patch-zone loading, and asset enumeration.**

## Public Interface

- `enum_assets(const game::XAssetType type, const std::function<void(game::XAssetHeader)>& callback, const bool include_override)` delegates to `game::DB_EnumXAssets_FastFile`, adapting its `(game::XAssetHeader, void*)` callback ABI to `std::function<void(game::XAssetHeader)>`; `include_override` controls override-asset inclusion.
- `component final : public component_interface` registers runtime hooks through `post_load()`.
- `component::post_load()` detours Win32 `CreateFileA` and `game::DB_LinkXAssetEntry`, then schedules deferred patch loading on `scheduler::main` after `250ms`.

## File Resolution and I/O Overrides

- `create_file_a_stub(const LPCSTR file_name, const DWORD desired_access, const DWORD share_mode, const LPSECURITY_ATTRIBUTES security_attributes, const DWORD creation_disposition, const DWORD flags_and_attributes, const HANDLE template_file)` preserves the original `CreateFileA` ABI, redirects qualifying Scaleform reads, then retries missing zone fastfiles from fallback roots.
- `is_read_open_request(const DWORD desired_access, const DWORD creation_disposition)` accepts reads when `desired_access & (GENERIC_READ | FILE_GENERIC_READ) != 0` and `creation_disposition` is `OPEN_EXISTING` or `OPEN_ALWAYS`.
- `is_scaleform_file_path(const char* file_name)` normalizes `/` to `\` and matches `.gfx`/`.swf` paths containing `\scaleform\` or `\ui_mp\`.
- `is_zone_fastfile_path(const char* file_name)` normalizes `/` to `\` and matches case-insensitive `.ff` paths containing `\zone\`.
- `find_scaleform_file(const char* file_name)` searches only the basename under `consolation/ui_mp/scaleform` in host-module, executable, and current-working-directory roots.
- `find_zone_file(const std::string& zone_file_name)` searches direct and recursive files under six roots, comparing filenames with `_stricmp`.
- `zone_lookup_roots()` returns `{host/zone, host/consolation/zone, exe/zone, exe/consolation/zone, cwd/zone, cwd/consolation/zone}`.
- `scaleform_lookup_roots()` returns `{host/consolation/ui_mp/scaleform, exe/consolation/ui_mp/scaleform, cwd/consolation/ui_mp/scaleform}`.
- `create_file_a_stub` logs `^5Opening Scaleform file %s\n` and `^5Loading Scaleform override %s\n`; failed zone fallback restores the original `GetLastError()` via `SetLastError`.

## Asset-Linking Diagnostics and Normalization

- `db_link_xasset_entry_stub(game::XAssetEntry* entry, const int allow_override)` normalizes rawfile names before invoking `db_link_xasset_entry_hook`, tracks source/linked zones, and logs Scaleform or `debug_xasset` asset-link records.
- `normalize_rawfile_name(game::XAssetEntry* entry)` converts backslashes to slashes for `game::ASSET_TYPE_RAWFILE` names, storing up to `1024` normalized names in `normalized_rawfile_names[1024][256]`; each name is copied with `strncpy_s(..., _TRUNCATE)` and the ring index is `normalized_rawfile_name_index++ % 1024`.
- `is_scaleform_asset_name(const char* asset_name)` lowercases slash-normalized names and matches `.gfx`, `.swf`, `scaleform`, `mpsysmodeselect`, `mpxbplaylistselect`, `cmsharedplatform`, `gfxfontlib`, `pcsharedlibrary`, or `cmsharedlibrary`.
- `get_asset_name(const game::XAssetEntry* entry)` returns `"<null>"` for absent data, `"<invalid>"` for out-of-range `asset.type`, `"<unnamed>"` for empty names, or `game::DB_GetXAssetName` output.
- `get_asset_zone_index(const game::XAssetEntry* entry)` returns `entry->zoneIndex` cast to `unsigned char`, or sentinel `0`.
- `get_zone_name(const unsigned char zone_index)` and `get_zone_flags(const unsigned char zone_index)` index the `game::XZone` table at `game::game_offset(0x10AB8188)`; `get_zone_name` returns `"<none>"` for an empty zone name.
- `debug_xasset()` enables verbose logging only when `utils::flags::has_flag("debug_xasset")` is true.
- `print_zone_list(const char* prefix, const game::XZoneInfo* zone_info, const int zone_count, const int sync)` emits `zoneCount`, `sync`, zone names, `allocFlags`, and `freeFlags` only under `debug_xasset`.
- `print_zone_load_state(const char* action, const std::vector<game::XZoneInfo>& zones)` logs `Loading fastfile '%s'\n` for debug loading and `"%s zone '%s'\n"` otherwise.
- `zone_name_equals(const char* lhs, const char* rhs)` performs null-safe case-insensitive comparison with `_stricmp`; `ends_with_ignore_case(const std::string& value, const std::string& suffix)` performs case-insensitive suffix matching.

## Deferred Patch Fastfiles

- `common_fastfiles_seen`, `patch_mp_loaded`, and `patch_consolation_loaded` become true when incoming or linked assets originate from `common_mp`, `patch_mp`, or `patch_consolation`.
- `patch_mp_attempted` and `patch_consolation_attempted` enforce one loading attempt per process after `common_fastfiles_seen`.
- `make_override_zone(const char* zone_name)` creates `game::XZoneInfo` with `name = zone_name`, `allocFlags = 0x11`, and `freeFlags = 0`.
- `zone_file_exists(const char* zone_name)` checks for `<zone_name>.ff` through `find_zone_file`.
- `get_pending_patch_zones()` queues existing `patch_mp` and `patch_consolation` zones, logs `^1Skipping override fastfile '%s' because it was not found\n`, and marks each attempted before filesystem lookup.
- `load_patch_fastfiles_after_common()` submits pending zones through `game::DB_LoadXAssets(..., patch_sync)` with `patch_sync = 0`, waits via `game::DB_WaitXAssets()`, refreshes UI gametype data through `gametypes::refresh_ui_gametype_list()` when `patch_consolation` is expected, and reports either loaded zones or `^3Submitted patch fastfile(s), but no linked assets were observed yet: %s\n`.
- `has_zone(const game::XZoneInfo* zone_info, const int zone_count, const char* name)` performs null/count validation and case-insensitive zone-name membership testing; `join_zone_names(const std::vector<game::XZoneInfo>& zones)` formats names as comma-separated `", "` text.

## Integration and Lifecycle

- `component::post_load()` installs `utils::hook::detour create_file_a_hook` on `CreateFileA` and `utils::hook::detour db_link_xasset_entry_hook` on `game::DB_LinkXAssetEntry`.
- `component::post_load()` schedules a repeating callback that returns `scheduler::cond_continue` until `common_fastfiles_seen`, then calls `load_patch_fastfiles_after_common()` and returns `scheduler::cond_end`.
- `REGISTER_COMPONENT(fastfiles::component)` exposes the component to the loader.
- `game::Com_Printf(16, ...)` is the logging boundary; `utils::nt::get_host_module()` and `GetModuleFileNameA` determine lookup roots; `std::filesystem` operations use `std::error_code` to avoid filesystem exceptions.

entries.response:
**console.cpp does Windows console allocation, input handling, game-output interception, colored display, history management, and file logging for Project Consolation.**

## Exported Interface

- `print(const int type, const char* fmt, ...)` formats variadic text with `format`, then routes it through `dispatch_message(type, result)` for console output, game-console storage, color selection, and logging.
- `match_compare(const std::string& input, const std::string& text, const bool exact) -> bool` returns `true` when `exact` requires `text == input`, or when non-exact mode finds `input` as a substring of `text`.
- `showDevConsole() -> void` sleeps for `500ms`, calls `game::Sys_ShowConsole()`, then pumps `GetMessageA`, `TranslateMessage`, and `DispatchMessageA` until the message loop ends.
- `console::component final : component_interface` allocates/configures the Windows console in its constructor, installs hooks in `post_load()`, and tears down hooks/thread/handles in `pre_destroy()`.
- `REGISTER_COMPONENT(console::component)` registers `console::component` with the loader component system.

## Console Lifecycle

- `component::component()` calls `AllocConsole()`, `AttachConsole(GetCurrentProcessId())`, redirects `stdin` to `CONIN$`, redirects `stdout`/`stderr` to `CONOUT$`, and initially hides `GetConsoleWindow()` with `SW_HIDE`.
- `component::post_load()` creates `printf_hook` over `printf` and `com_printf_hook` over `game::game_offset(0x103F6400)`, shows the console, sets a versioned title, creates `con.kill_event`, and starts the named `"Console"` thread through `utils::thread::create_named_thread`.
- `component::pre_destroy()` clears `printf_hook` and `com_printf_hook`, sets `con.kill`, signals `con.kill_event`, posts `WM_QUIT` to `con.thread_id`, cancels synchronous I/O, joins `con.thread`, hides/frees the console, closes `con.kill_event`, and resets `con.thread_id`.
- `con.thread` waits on `STD_INPUT_HANDLE`, `con.kill_event`, and queued window messages through `MsgWaitForMultipleObjects(..., 100, QS_ALLINPUT)`.
- `game_window_closed()` ignores missing windows before first observation, then treats a missing `*game::main_window` lasting more than `3s` as shutdown.
- `con.thread` handles `WM_QUIT`, `WM_CLOSE`, and `WM_DESTROY` by enqueueing `game::Cbuf_AddText(0, "quit\n")`; other messages pass through `TranslateMessage` and `DispatchMessageA`.

## Input State and Rendering

- `con` stores `kill`, `thread`, `kill_event`, `thread_id`, a fixed `char buffer[512]`, `cursor`, `history_index`, and a `std::deque<std::string> history`.
- `handle_input(INPUT_RECORD record)` handles resize events, key-down events, cursor movement, editing, command submission, and history navigation under `print_mutex`.
- `VK_UP` and `VK_DOWN` navigate `con.history`, clamp `con.history_index` to `[-1, history.size()-1]`, copy selected entries into `con.buffer`, and refresh through `clear()`/`update()`.
- `VK_LEFT` and `VK_RIGHT` clamp `con.cursor` to the current `strlen(con.buffer)` range; `VK_BACK` removes one byte with `std::memmove`; `VK_ESCAPE` clears the input buffer.
- `VK_RETURN` removes a duplicated selected history entry, pushes non-empty input to the front, caps `con.history` at `10` entries, submits `utils::string::va("%s\n", con.buffer)` through `game::Cbuf_AddText(0, ...)`, logs `"]%s\n"`, prints `"]%s\r\n"`, and clears `con.buffer`.
- `get_max_input_length() -> size_t` derives the input limit from the console window width and `sizeof(con.buffer)`; insertion is rejected when `strlen(con.buffer) + 1 >= get_max_input_length()`.
- `update()` hides the cursor, rewrites `con.buffer` at position `0`, restores `con.cursor`, and shows the cursor; `clear_output()` overwrites the displayed input with spaces based on `strlen(con.buffer)`.
- `handle_resize()` calls `clear()` followed by `update()`; `clear()` resets `con.buffer`, `con.cursor`, and the console cursor position.
- `set_cursor_pos(int x)` and `show_cursor(bool show)` manipulate `CONSOLE_SCREEN_BUFFER_INFO` and `CONSOLE_CURSOR_INFO` on `OUTPUT_HANDLE`.
- `get_attribute(int type) -> uint8_t` maps `con_type_info` to `7` (white), `con_type_warning` to `6` (yellow), `con_type_error` to `4` (red), and `con_type_debug` to `3` (cyan), defaulting to `7`.

## Output Hooks and Classification

- `printf_stub(const char* fmt, ...) -> int` formats through `format`, calls `write_log`, appends to `game_console::append_output`, forwards to `game::CL_ConsolePrint(0, 6, result.c_str(), 0, 0, 0)`, and returns the original `printf` status through `invoke_printf("%s", result.data())`.
- `com_printf_stub(int channel, const char* fmt, ...) -> void` formats/logs game output, forwards the formatted string to the original `com_printf_hook`, classifies color prefixes and keyword substrings, applies suppression rules, and dispatches colored output.
- `format(va_list* ap, const char* message) -> std::string` uses thread-local `char buffer[0x1000]` and `vsnprintf_s(buffer, _TRUNCATE, message, *ap)`; negative results return `{}` and successful results preserve the reported byte count.
- `dispatch_message(int type, const std::string& message) -> int` logs unless `skip_dispatch_log`, appends through `game_console::append_output`, clears the input line, sets `get_attribute(type)`, prints `message`, restores info color, adds `"\n"` when needed, refreshes input, and returns the original print result.
- `dispatch_split_debug_message(const std::string& message) -> int` logs `"debug:" + message`, appends only `message`, prints `"debug:"` in `con_type_error` color and the body in `con_type_warning` color, then restores `con_type_info`.
- `com_printf_stub` recognizes `^1` as `con_type_error`, `^3` as `con_type_warning`, and `^5` as `con_type_debug`, stripping the two-byte prefix for display.
- `error_substrings` forces `con_type_error` for `"Unable to"`, `"Couldn't reset"`, and `"nat type is Strict"`.
- `warning_substrings` forces `con_type_warning` for `"Unable to"`, `"Missing asset"`, `"Couldn't find"`, `"Unknown command"`, `"is read only"`, `"is not a valid value"`, `"is write protected"`, `"already defined"`, `"Adding channel:"`, `"Hiding channel:"`, `"will use the shock"`, `"WARNING:"`, and `"nat type is Moderate"`.
- `debug_substrings` forces `con_type_debug` for `"GamerProfile_LogInProfile took"`, `"connection status has changed"`, `"signed in to live"`, `"Reading profile"`, `"Loaded zone"`, `"Loading fastfile"`, `"nat type is Open"`, `"LOADING..."`, `"xuid"`, and `"execing"`.
- `com_printf_stub` handles `"^1debug:^3 "` specially through `dispatch_split_debug_message(result.substr(10))`, with `skip_dispatch_log` preventing duplicate log writes.
- `com_printf_stub` dispatches `"Velocity change:"` only when `game::Dvar_FindVar("g_debugVelocity")` exists and `current.enabled` is true.
- `com_printf_stub` suppresses repeated `"XUserReadProfileSettings"` messages using static `xsignin`; the first occurrence emits `"Reading XUserProfileSettings"` and omits the original message when it contains `"took 0ms"`.

## Logging and Version Contracts

- `get_log_paths() -> std::vector<std::filesystem::path>` tries `current_path() / "consolation" / "console.log"`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Project-Consolation/console.log`, and `%TEMP%/Project-Consolation-console.log`, in that order.
- `write_log(const std::string& message)` serializes initialization and appends through `utils::io::write_file`; the first writable path receives `"console: logging to %s\n"`, and messages without a trailing newline receive `"\n"`.
- `write_log` uses `log_mutex`, `log_initialized`, and `log_path`; failure across all paths emits `OutputDebugStringA("console: failed to open console.log\n")` and disables further writes.
- `skip_dispatch_log` is `thread_local`; `printf_stub` and direct command submission log independently, while `com_printf_stub` prevents duplicate dispatch logging.
- `build_display_version() -> std::string` combines `VERSION_PRODUCT`, `VERSION_BUILD` (default `"0"`), the first seven characters of `GIT_HASH`, `"-dbg-"` under `DEBUG` or `"-nightly-"` otherwise, and `"-dirty"` when `GIT_DIRTY` is true.
- `normalize_build_date(const char* raw_date) -> std::string` returns `{}` for null input and repeatedly collapses adjacent spaces via the exact search pattern `"  "` to normalize `__DATE__`.
- `component::post_load()` formats the title as `"Project: Consolation [" + build_display_version() + " | " + normalize_build_date(__DATE__) + " " + __TIME__ + "] - Console"`.

## Coupling and Synchronization

- `printf_hook` and `com_printf_hook` depend on `utils::hook::detour`; `invoke_printf` falls back to `std::printf` when `printf_hook.get_original()` is unavailable.
- `game_console::append_output`, `game::Cbuf_AddText`, `game::CL_ConsolePrint`, `game::Dvar_FindVar`, `game::main_window`, and `game::Sys_ShowConsole` form the game integration boundary.
- `print_mutex` is recursive because `dispatch_message`, `clear_output`, and `update` nest console-rendering operations; `log_mutex` serializes lazy log-file initialization and writes.
- `con.thread` and `con.kill_event` define shutdown signaling; `CancelSynchronousIo` handles a potentially blocked console read before `con.thread.join()`.

entries.response:
**minidump.cpp creates in-memory Windows minidumps from exception context.**

## Interface

`create_minidump(const LPEXCEPTION_POINTERS exceptioninfo) -> std::string` writes and returns minidump bytes for the supplied exception pointers.

## Implementation

`get_minidump_type()` combines `MiniDumpIgnoreInaccessibleMemory`, `MiniDumpWithHandleData`, `MiniDumpScanMemory`, `MiniDumpWithProcessThreadData`, `MiniDumpWithFullMemoryInfo`, `MiniDumpWithThreadInfo`, and `MiniDumpWithUnloadedModules`.

`get_temp_filename()` uses `GetTempPathA` and `GetTempFileNameA` with prefix `"Consolation -"`.

`write_dump_to_temp_file()` calls `MiniDumpWriteDump` on the current process and creates a temporary `FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE` handle; failure shows `"Minidump Error"` and terminates with exit code `123`.

`read_file()` flushes, rewinds, and reads through a `0x2000`-byte buffer, returning `{}` on `ReadFile` failure.

`gsl::finally` guarantees `CloseHandle` after `create_minidump`; `dbghelp.lib` is required.

entries.response:
**patches.cpp does runtime engine patching, dvar customization, branding, offline-mode support, gameplay fixes, and security guards for Project: Consolation.**

## Public symbols

- `patches::enforce_ads_sprint_interrupt(game::usercmd_t* cmd) -> void` clears `game::BUTTON_SPRINT` whenever `cmd->buttons` contains `game::BUTTON_ADS`; null `cmd` returns immediately.
- `patches::component final : component_interface` registers the patch component through `REGISTER_COMPONENT(patches::component)` and implements `post_load()`.
- `patches::component::post_load() -> void` installs all hooks, dvar overrides, startup replacements, security self-tests, and periodic dvar flag repairs.

## Version and branding

- `build_shortversion_string() -> std::string` starts with `VERSION_PRODUCT`, appends `-dbg` under `DEBUG`, appends `-nightly` for non-`DEBUG`/non-`NDEBUG` builds, and leaves release builds unchanged.
- `build_build_label() -> std::string` truncates `GIT_HASH` to seven characters and appends `-dirty` when `GIT_DIRTY` is true.
- `build_timestamp_label() -> std::string` returns the exact compile-time format `__DATE__ + " " + __TIME__`.
- `build_game_date_string() -> std::string` returns `__DATE__`.
- `build_version_string() -> std::string` returns the exact format `Project: Consolation <shortversion> build <build-label> <timestamp> win-x86`.
- `VERSION_BUILD` defaults to the string `"0"` when undefined, although this file does not otherwise consume it.
- `create_window_ex_stub(...) -> HWND` intercepts `CreateWindowExA`; `"JB_MP"` windows receive the title `"Project: Consolation - Multiplayer"`.
- `create_window_ex_stub(...)` reads `r_fullscreen`, `r_borderless`, `vid_xpos`, and `vid_ypos`; window position changes apply only when `r_fullscreen` is disabled.
- `create_window_ex_stub(...)` converts non-fullscreen borderless windows to `WS_POPUP`, removes caption/frame/system styles, removes dialog/client/edge extended styles, and adds `WS_EX_APPWINDOW`.

## Offline mode

- `local_offline_mode_requested() -> bool` recognizes flags `"offline"`, `"local_offline"`, and `"local-offline"` through `utils::flags::has_flag`.
- `apply_local_offline_mode_patches() -> void` redirects `game::game_offset(0x10240B30)` and `game::game_offset(0x10240A30)` to `ret_one`, then NOPs five bytes at `game::game_offset(0x102489A1)`.
- `ret_one(DWORD*, int) -> int` always returns `1` for bypassed XLive playlist/stat checks.
- `apply_local_offline_mode_patches()` suppresses the XSessionCreate zero-session failure branch associated with `XBOXLIVE_NETCONNECTION` and logs `"local offline mode: online storage/session checks bypassed\n"`.
- `post_load()` registers read-only `cl_offlineMode` with the detected flag state and applies offline patches when `local_offline_mode_requested()` is true.
- `XLIVELESS` conditionally applies `apply_local_offline_mode_patches()` whenever `offline_mode` is false, so enabling `XLIVELESS` broadens bypass activation.

## Security guards and self-tests

- `k_huffman_max_decoded_bytes` and `k_huffman_max_compressed_bytes` equal `0x20000` bytes; `k_ui_replace_directive_max_len` equals `0x100`; `k_party_member_join_max_message_bytes` equals `0x4000`.
- `bounded_length(const char* value, std::size_t max_len) -> std::size_t` performs null-safe bounded NUL scanning and returns at most `max_len`.
- `CL_ParseServerMessage_huffman_guard(int a1, std::uint32_t* a2) -> unsigned int` delegates null `a2` to the original detoured function, rejects `a2[5] < a2[7]`, and rejects compressed lengths above `k_huffman_max_compressed_bytes`.
- `CL_ParseServerMessage_huffman_guard(...)` reports underflow through `game::Com_Error(".\\cl_parse_mp.cpp", 1243, 1, "Huffman compressed msg cursor underflow detected\n")`.
- `CL_ParseServerMessage_huffman_guard(...)` reports oversized Huffman data through `"Huffman compressed msg exceeded safe decode limit (%u > %u)\n"` and returns `0` after either rejection.
- `UI_ReplaceDirective_guard(int ArgList, char* a2, int a3, unsigned __int8 a4) -> char*` bounds-checks both `ArgList` reinterpreted as `const char*` and `a2` with `bounded_length(..., k_ui_replace_directive_max_len + 1)`.
- `UI_ReplaceDirective_guard(...)` rejects inputs exceeding `0x100` bytes, logs `"UI_ReplaceDirective: rejected oversized directive input\n"`, returns `a2`, and otherwise invokes the original detour.
- `PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin_guard(char a1, std::uint32_t* a2, int a3, __int64 a4, int a5, std::uint32_t* a6) -> int` delegates null `a2` or `a6`, rejects `a6[5] < a6[7]`, and rejects unread messages above `0x4000` bytes.
- `PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin_guard(...)` logs malformed cursor input as `"PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin: rejected malformed message cursor\n"` and oversized input as `"PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin: rejected oversized message (%zu bytes)\n"`.
- `PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin_self_test() -> bool` constructs a cursor with `packet_cursor[5] = 0` and `packet_cursor[7] = 1`, verifies the guard returns `0`, and logs pass/fail.
- `UI_ReplaceDirective_self_test() -> bool` uses a `0x110`-byte non-NUL oversized input, `0xDEADBEEF`/`0xCAFEBABE` canaries, and a `0x110`-byte output to verify rejection, return-pointer preservation, canary integrity, and NUL termination.
- `register_security_guard_self_test() -> void` registers the `securityGuardSelfTest` console command, runs both self-tests, and prints `"securityGuardSelfTest: party=%s ui=%s\n"`.

## Dvar handling

- `dvar_enabled(const char* name) -> bool` converts boolean, integer, float, string, and enumeration dvars into enabled state; strings treat empty, `"0"`, case-insensitive `"false"`, and case-insensitive `"off"` as disabled.
- `dvar_int_value(const char* name, int fallback = 0) -> int` converts boolean, integer, float, string, and enumeration dvars to integers, returning `fallback` when absent or when a string value is null.
- `make_dvar_saved_and_writable(const char* name) -> void` clears `read_only`, `write_protected`, and `latched`, then sets `saved`.
- `make_dvar_debug_writable(const char* name) -> void` additionally clears `cheat_protected` before setting `saved`.
- `find_dvar(std::unordered_map<std::string, T>& map, const std::string& name) -> T*` implements map lookup for dvar override tables.
- `find_dvar(std::unordered_set<std::string>& set, const std::string& name) -> bool` implements membership lookup for dvar name sets.
- `Dvar_RegisterNew_Stub(const char* dvarName, game::DvarType type, unsigned short flags, char* desc, int unk, game::DvarValue value, game::DvarLimits domain) -> game::dvar_s*` intercepts registration and applies typed overrides from `dvars::overrides::register_bool_overrides`, `register_int_overrides`, `register_float_overrides`, and `register_string_overrides`.

**runtime.hpp defines `gamepad::unstable::controller::runtime`, the non-copyable process-wide owner and frame lifecycle coordinator for the controller subsystem.**

## Public interface

- `runtime (bool developer)` constructs diagnostics, shared services, device discovery, drivers, calibration, and engine bridges; `~runtime ()` tears them down.
- `runtime (const runtime&) = delete`, `runtime& operator= (const runtime&) = delete`, `runtime (runtime&&) = delete`, and `runtime& operator= (runtime&&) = delete` prevent duplication of process-global engine hooks.
- `context make_context () noexcept` returns a cheap borrowed service view; `diagnostic_sink& diagnostics () noexcept` exposes `sink_`.
- `void engine_ready ()` registers engine dvars/commands and acquires configured bindings once engine systems exist.
- `void frame ()` advances one engine input frame; it must not throw across the engine ABI or allocate on the per-frame acquisition path.
- `device_id active () const noexcept` returns the currently followed device or `no_device`; `const input_frame& latest () const noexcept` returns its latest published frame.
- `engine::key_dispatcher& keys () noexcept`, `engine::bind_bridge& binds () noexcept`, and `engine::view_driver& view () noexcept` expose engine integration bridges.
- `bool driving () const noexcept` is true only when `active_ != no_device`, `keys_.in_use ()`, and `engine::read (dvars_.enabled, true)` all hold.
- `const engine::dvars& dvars () const noexcept` exposes dvar definitions; `size_t device_count () const noexcept` returns `drivers_.size ()`.

## Ownership and integration

`runtime` owns `logging_sink sink_`, `context ctx_`, `transport::xinput_module xinput_`, `registry devices_`, `discovery discovery_`, `driver::set drivers_`, `calibration::store calibration_`, `engine::dvars dvars_`, `engine::key_dispatcher keys_`, `engine::bind_bridge binds_`, and `engine::view_driver view_` in declaration order.

`mod::controller_module` creates the single process instance, while subsystems receive borrowed `context` values instead of locating services through `runtime`.

`engine_ready_` gates one-time engine initialization; `frame ()` is called through the engine input hook surface.

## State and behavior

`bool advance (driver::driver&, const device_connection&, input_frame& out)` polls one driver and fills `out` when a reading is produced.

`const calibration::profile& profile_for (controller::family)` lazily loads one profile per family; `profiles_` is `array<optional<calibration::profile>, 5>`, and `static_assert (static_cast<size_t> (controller::family::dualsense_edge) == 4, "profiles_ is indexed by family and must cover every one")` enforces family-index coverage.

`void apply_light_bar ()` sends PlayStation light-bar output only when `lit_device_` or packed `lit_colour_` changes; `lit_device_ == no_device` means no output has been applied.

`active_` selects the single device whose most recent reading drives singular engine key/view state; `latest_` stores its last frame.

`sequence_` monotonically numbers subsystem samples, while `last_published_` records the sequence visible to the engine; `had_device_` tracks prior-frame presence so departing devices can release held keys.

## Dependencies

`support/types.hpp` and `support/utility.hpp` supply shared types/utilities; `clock.hpp`, `diagnostic.hpp`, device registry/discovery, `driver::set`, `xinput-module.hpp`, `sample/frame.hpp`, `calibration/store.hpp`, and engine dvar/key/bind/view headers define the owned subsystem boundaries.

**entities.cpp serializes, parses, filters, and mutates map entity dictionaries for entity conversion workflows.**

## Public interface

- `std::string Entities::Build()` emits each entity as `{\n`, followed by `"key" "value"\n` pairs, and `}\n`.
- `std::vector<std::string> Entities::GetModels()` returns unique nonempty `model` values, excluding brushmodels whose first character is `*` or `?` and excluding exact `"com_plasticcase_green_big_us_dirt"`.
- `bool Entities::ConvertVehicles()` rewrites entities with `targetname == "destructible"` and `utils::string::starts_with(entity["destructible_type"], "vehicle")`, setting `targetname = "destructible_vehicle"` and `sound_csv_include = "vehicle_car_exp"`; returns whether any entity changed.
- `bool Entities::ConvertTurrets()` rewrites `classname == "misc_turret"` with `weaponinfo = "turret_minigun_mp"` and `model = "weapon_minigun"`; returns whether any turret changed.
- `void Entities::DeleteOldSchoolPickups()` erases entities containing `weaponinfo` or `targetname == "oldschool_pickup"`, except `classname == "misc_turret"`, logging `Erased weapon %s from map ents\n`.
- `void Entities::AddRemovedSModels()` is currently a no-op; commented code sketches restoration of removed static models as `script_model` entities.
- `void Entities::parse(std::string buffer)` parses quoted key/value pairs into `this->entities`, lowercases keys via `utils::string::to_lower`, and throws `std::runtime_error("Parsing error!")` on invalid quote-state transitions.

## Parsing and coupling

`Entities::parse` uses `PARSE_AWAIT_KEY`, `PARSE_READ_KEY`, `PARSE_AWAIT_VALUE`, and `PARSE_READ_VALUE` state sentinels, treating `{` as entity start and `}` as entity termination; malformed structural input outside quote transitions is not generally validated. `Entities::Build` and `Entities::parse` implement the map entity text format but do not escape embedded quotes or backslashes.

`Entities::GetModels`, `Entities::ConvertVehicles`, `Entities::ConvertTurrets`, and `Entities::DeleteOldSchoolPickups` mutate or inspect `std::unordered_map<std::string, std::string>` entries held by `Entities::entities`. `console::info`, `utils::string::starts_with`, `game/game.hpp`, and `game/structs.hpp` support logging, matching, and planned engine integration.

`ConvertVehicles` indexes `entity["destructible_type"]` after checking only `classname`, potentially inserting a missing key; `DeleteOldSchoolPickups` similarly indexes `(*i)["model"]` during logging, potentially inserting missing data.

**component_interface.hpp defines the polymorphic asset-component lifecycle interface.**

## Interface

**scheduler.cpp schedules delayed callbacks across async, main-frame, and renderer pipelines.**

## Public API

- `on_shutdown(const std::function<void()>& callback)` appends `callback` to `shutdown_callbacks`, invoked after `g_shutdown_game_hook`.
- `schedule(const std::function<bool()>& callback, const pipeline type, const std::chrono::milliseconds delay)` creates a `task` with `last_call = high_resolution_clock::now()` and queues it in `pipelines[type]`.
- `loop(const std::function<void()>& callback, const pipeline type, const std::chrono::milliseconds delay)` wraps `callback` with `cond_continue` and delegates to `schedule`.
- `once(const std::function<void()>& callback, const pipeline type, const std::chrono::milliseconds delay)` wraps `callback` with `cond_end`, causing task removal after execution.
- `component final : public component_interface` integrates scheduler startup, hooks, and shutdown lifecycle through `post_start()`, `post_load()`, and `pre_destroy()`.

## Scheduling Model

- `task` stores `handler`, `interval`, and `last_call`; `task_pipeline::execute()` runs eligible handlers when `now - last_call >= interval`.
- `task_pipeline::add()` writes to `new_callbacks_`; `task_pipeline::merge_callbacks()` transfers pending tasks into `callbacks_`, allowing scheduling from concurrent contexts.
- `callbacks_` uses `utils::concurrency::container<task_list, std::recursive_mutex>`; `new_callbacks_` uses the default concurrency container.
- `execute(const pipeline type)` asserts and bounds-checks `type`, then dispatches to `pipelines[type]`.
- `kill` terminates the `"Async Scheduler"` thread; async execution polls `game_window_closed()` every `10ms`.
- `game_window_closed()` requires a previously observed valid `game::main_window`, then treats a missing/invalid window lasting longer than `3` seconds as shutdown.

## Hooks and Lifecycle

- `component::post_load()` installs `r_end_frame_hook` at `0x103C1050`, `main_frame_hook` at `game::game_offset(0x103F7470)`, and `g_shutdown_game_hook` at `game::game_offset(0x101AB0B0)`.
- `main_frame_stub()` invokes `main_frame_hook`, then executes `pipeline::main` through `gsl::finally`.
- `render_frame_stub()` executes `pipeline::renderer` before invoking `r_end_frame_hook`.
- `component::pre_destroy()` sets `kill` and joins `thread` when joinable; `component::post_start()` creates the named `"Async Scheduler"` thread via `utils::thread::create_named_thread`.
- `REGISTER_COMPONENT(scheduler::component)` registers the lifecycle component; `utils::hook`, `utils::concurrency`, `utils::thread`, and `game::main_window` are key integration points.

## API

`component_loader` exports `premature_shutdown_trigger` (`std::exception`, `what()` → `"Premature shutdown requested"`), `installer<T>` (static-asserts `T : component_interface`, registers `std::make_unique<T>()`), and `get<T>()` → `T*`.

**runtime.cpp orchestrates controller discovery, polling, calibration, input dispatch, view latching, engine integration, and PlayStation light-bar output.**

## Role and Dependencies

`gamepad::unstable::controller::runtime` owns the controller runtime lifecycle and coordinates `context`, `xinput`, `devices`, `discovery`, `drivers`, `calibration`, `keys`, and `view`.

`calibration_directory()` resolves `std::filesystem::current_path()` and appends `"players" / "controller"`; filesystem errors return an empty base `path`.

`runtime::~runtime()` is out-of-line and defaulted so subsystem types can remain forward-declared in `runtime.hpp`.

## Public Interface

`runtime::runtime(bool developer)` initializes `developer_`, `ctx_`, `xinput_`, `devices_`, `discovery_`, `drivers_`, `calibration_`, `keys_`, `binds_`, and `view_`, then reports severity `info`, facility `runtime`, error `errc::none`, and exact message `"controller runtime initialized"`.

`context runtime::make_context() noexcept` returns a new `context(sink_, developer_)`.

`void runtime::engine_ready()` is idempotent through `engine_ready_`; it registers dvars via `engine::register_dvars(ctx_)`, registers commands via `engine::register_commands(ctx_, *this)`, applies `binds_.apply_configured_layout()`, performs eager `discovery_.scan_now()`, and then marks `engine_ready_`.

`const calibration::profile& runtime::profile_for(controller::family f)` lazily loads `calibration_.load(f, nullopt)` into `profiles_`, falling back to `calibration::default_profile(f)` when no stored profile exists.

`bool runtime::advance(driver::driver& d, const device_connection& dc, input_frame& out)` polls `d` into stack-allocated `raw_sample` and `canonical_sample`, applies `calibration::apply(profile_for(dc.identity.family), raw, canonical)`, and writes `input_frame` metadata with `dc.id`, `dc.identity.family`, `dc.link`, incremented `sequence_`, `latency_span{acquired, timestamp{}}`, and `canonical`; `false` from `d.poll()` aborts publication.

`void runtime::apply_light_bar()` drives only `dualshock4`, `dualsense`, or `dualsense_edge` devices advertising `capability::light_bar`.

`void runtime::frame()` executes the per-frame discovery, reconciliation, publication, polling, dispatch, view, and light-bar workflow.

## Frame State and Selection

`runtime::frame()` marks `CONTROLLER_ZONE("controller::frame")` and `CONTROLLER_FRAME_MARK()`; frames before `engine_ready_` return without reading dvars.

`discovery_.scan()` and `drivers_.reconcile(devices_)` refresh device state, while `engine::publish_present(dvars_, drivers_.size() != 0)` updates engine presence.

`engine::read(dvars_.enabled, true)` disables processing when false or when `drivers_.size() == 0`; `keys_.release_all()`, `view_.idle()`, `active_ = no_device`, `had_device_ = false`, `lit_device_ = no_device`, and `lit_colour_ = 0` clear held state when a device was active.

`drivers_.for_each()` polls every bound driver through `advance()`, but `candidate` follows exactly one device: a new reading wins unless `active_` also reports, preserving the current active device during simultaneous reports.

`latest_.sequence > last_published_` is asserted before updating `last_published_`, enforcing monotonic published-frame ordering.

`keys_.release_all()` runs when `active_ != latest_.device` before `keys_.dispatch(latest_.state)`, preventing held-button latching across device takeover.

`view_.observe(latest_.state)` latches stick state for the later movement hook; `keys_.dispatch(latest_.state)` still ticks held-button repeats when `had_device_` is true but no fresh sample arrives.

## Light-Bar Contract

`engine::read(dvars_.light_bar, true)` gates output; disabled light bars reset `lit_device_` and `lit_colour_` without overwriting OS or Steam state.

`light_bar_r`, `light_bar_g`, and `light_bar_b` default to `196`, `151`, and `54`; the local `clamp8(int v)` clamps each channel to `[0, 255]`.

`colour` packs RGB as `(r << 16) | (g << 8) | b`; `drivers_.submit(active_, driver::light_bar_request{r, g, b})` runs only when `active_ != lit_device_` or `colour != lit_colour_`.

**exception.cpp does Windows crash interception, minidump generation, and fatal-error termination for Project: Consolation.**

## Public symbols

- `exception::component final : component_interface` registers exception handling.
- `exception::component::post_load() override -> void` installs `exception_filter` via `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`.
- `REGISTER_COMPONENT(exception::component)` activates the component loader registration.

## Crash workflow

- `exception_filter(LPEXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> LONG` continues harmless exceptions; otherwise calls `write_minidump`, stores thread-local `exception_data`, redirects `ContextRecord->Eip` to `get_reset_state_stub()`, and returns `EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION`.
- `is_harmless_error(LPEXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> bool` allows `STATUS_INTEGER_OVERFLOW`, `STATUS_FLOAT_OVERFLOW`, and `STATUS_SINGLE_STEP` to continue execution.
- `write_minidump(LPEXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> void` serializes `create_minidump(exceptioninfo)` to `minidumps/consolation-crash-%s.dmp`, substituting `utils::string::get_timestamp()`.
- `get_reset_state_stub() -> size_t` lazily assembles x86 instructions `sub esp, 0x10`, `or esp, 0x8`, and jump to `reset_state`.
- `reset_state() -> void` delegates to `display_error_dialog()` after exception-context redirection.

## Fatal dialog and state

- `exception_data` is thread-local `{ DWORD code = 0; PVOID address = nullptr; }`, carrying the exception code and fault address.
- `display_error_dialog() -> void` formats `Fatal error (0x%08X) at 0x%p.\nA minidump has been written.\n\n`, appends the graphics-driver/OS-update guidance, suspends other threads, shows the cursor, displays `"Project: Consolation ERROR"`, then calls `TerminateProcess(..., exception_data.code)`.
- `generate_crash_info(LPEXCEPTION_POINTERS) -> std::string` emits CRLF lines for timestamp, exception code, fault address, and `OS Version: %u.%u`; it is currently unused.
- `show_mouse_cursor() -> void` repeatedly calls `ShowCursor(TRUE)` until the cursor becomes visible.

## Integration constraints

- `utils::hook`, `utils::io`, `utils::string`, `utils::thread`, and `exception/minidump.hpp` supply assembly hooks, file output, formatting/timestamps, thread suspension, and dump creation.
- `ContextRecord->Eip`, `esp`, and `TerminateProcess` imply a 32-bit Windows runtime; `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter` establishes process-wide handling.

entries.response:
**component_loader.cpp does lifecycle dispatch, filtering, import resolution, and teardown for registered `component_interface` instances.**

## Interface

- `component_loader::register_component(std::unique_ptr<component_interface>&&)` transfers ownership into the global component registry.
- `component_loader::post_start() -> bool` invokes `component_interface::post_start()` once; returns `false` on `premature_shutdown_trigger`, otherwise `true`.
- `component_loader::post_load() -> bool` calls `clean()`, then invokes `component_interface::post_load()` once with the same shutdown/error contract.
- `component_loader::pre_destroy() -> void` invokes `component_interface::pre_destroy()` once for every retained component.
- `component_loader::clean() -> void` removes unsupported components after calling `component_interface::pre_destroy()`.
- `component_loader::load_import(const std::string&, const std::string&) -> void*` queries every component and returns the last non-null import pointer.
- `component_loader::trigger_premature_shutdown() -> void` throws `premature_shutdown_trigger`.
- `component_loader::get_components() -> std::vector<std::unique_ptr<component_interface>>&` exposes the process-wide registry.

## Behavior and coupling

`get_components()` uses a function-local static `std::unique_ptr` with `std::function` deleter; destruction calls `pre_destroy()` before deleting the vector. `post_start()` and `post_load()` use static `handled` sentinels, so repeated calls return immediately. `post_start()` and `post_load()` wrap `std::exception`, `const char*`, and unknown exceptions as `std::runtime_error` using `post_start failed in {}: {}` or `post_load failed in {}: {}`; `premature_shutdown_trigger` propagates to the outer handler. `log_component_event()` emits `[component_loader] {} {}\n` through `OutputDebugStringA`, `std::printf`, and `std::fflush(stdout)`. `typeid(*component_).name()` identifies components at runtime; registry iteration follows a Registry plus Chain-of-Responsibility dispatch pattern.

**gametypes.cpp hooks rawfile lookup and rebuilds the UI gametype caches.**

## Role and integration

`gametypes::component` integrates custom gametype discovery into the game loader through `REGISTER_COMPONENT(gametypes::component)`.

`db_find_xasset_header_internal_hook` detours `game::DB_FindXAssetHeader_Internal` to prioritize patch-zone assets, then filesystem overrides, then fastfile assets.

`filesystem::read_file`, `filesystem::get_search_paths`, `game::DB_EnumXAssetEntries`, `game::game_offset`, `utils::memory::allocate`, `utils::io`, `utils::hook`, `utils::string`, `console`, and `command` form the primary coupling surface.

## Exported interface

`void gametypes::refresh_ui_gametype_list()` rebuilds the UI cache only when `ui_gametype_list_refreshed` is `false`.

`void gametypes::force_refresh_ui_gametype_list()` unconditionally invokes `rebuild_ui_gametype_cache()`.

`void gametypes::dump_debug_state()` serializes primary and secondary UI entries, feeder patch addresses, and raw instruction bytes to `consolation/gametypes_dump/debug_state.txt`.

## Asset lookup behavior

`normalize_gametype_path(const char*) -> std::string` converts `\` to `/` and maps null names to an empty string.

`is_gametype_rawfile(game::XAssetType, const char*) -> bool` matches `game::ASSET_TYPE_RAWFILE` names beginning case-insensitively with `maps/mp/gametypes/`.

`is_scaleform_rawfile(game::XAssetType, const char*) -> bool` matches `game::ASSET_TYPE_RAWFILE` names beginning with `scaleform/` and ending with `.gfx`.

`db_find_xasset_header_internal_stub(const game::XAssetType, const char*, const int) -> game::XAssetHeader` applies the lookup order patch zone → disk override → original database lookup for gametype rawfiles, while Scaleform lookup uses patch zone → disk override → original lookup.

`find_patch_gametype_rawfile(const std::string&) -> game::RawFile*` enumerates `game::ASSET_TYPE_RAWFILE`, filters populated names and `patch_` zones, and prefers zone `patch_consolation`.

`find_patch_scaleform_rawfile(const std::string&) -> game::RawFile*` duplicates the patch-zone selection logic for `.gfx` assets and prefers `patch_consolation`.

`load_custom_gametype_rawfile(const char*) -> game::RawFile*` caches normalized filesystem-loaded gametype files in `loaded_gametype_rawfiles` and logs `gametypes: loaded raw fallback %s from %s\n`.

`load_custom_scaleform_rawfile(const char*) -> game::RawFile*` caches binary `.gfx` overrides in `loaded_scaleform_rawfiles`, trying `ui_mp/<normalized_name>` before `<normalized_name>`, and logs `scaleform: loaded raw override %s from %s\n`.

`make_rawfile(const std::string&, const std::string&) -> game::RawFile*` allocates a null-terminated `game::RawFile` with `len = data.size() + 1`.

`make_binary_rawfile(const std::string&, const std::string&) -> game::RawFile*` allocates a non-null-terminated binary `game::RawFile` with `len = data.size()`.

`rawfile_has_data(const game::RawFile*) -> bool` requires non-null `buffer` and `len > 0`.

`get_rawfile_buffer(const game::RawFile*) -> std::string` strips one trailing `'\0'` when `rawfile->buffer[rawfile->len - 1] == '\0'`.

`read_gametype_rawfile(const std::string&) -> std::string` calls `game::DB_FindXAssetHeader_Internal(game::ASSET_TYPE_RAWFILE, name.c_str(), 1)` and extracts its buffer.

## Gametype enumeration and parsing

`GAMETYPES_LIST` is exactly `"maps/mp/gametypes/_gametypes.txt"`.

`GAMETYPE_PREFIX` is exactly `"maps/mp/gametypes/"`.

`UI_GAMETYPE_MAX` is `0x20`, limiting parsed, merged, and written gametype entries to 32.

`parse_gametype_ids(const std::string&) -> std::vector<std::string>` reads line-by-line, removes text beginning at the first `//`, trims `" \t\r\n"`, and stops after `UI_GAMETYPE_MAX` non-empty IDs.

`trim(std::string) -> std::string` removes leading and trailing spaces, tabs, carriage returns, and newlines.

`is_hidden_gametype_id(const std::string&) -> bool` hides only the case-insensitive ID `"menu"`.

`append_unique_gametype_id(std::vector<std::string>&, std::unordered_set<std::string>&, const std::string&) -> void` trims, rejects empty IDs, `"menu"`, and full lists, lowercases accepted IDs with `std::tolower`, and deduplicates through `known_ids`.

`get_gametype_id_from_display_path(const std::string&) -> std::string` extracts the basename without `.txt` from paths containing `maps/mp/gametypes/`, excluding `GAMETYPES_LIST`.

`append_patch_gametype_ids(std::vector<std::string>&, std::unordered_set<std::string>&) -> void` discovers `.txt` display assets from populated `patch_` zones through `game::DB_EnumXAssetEntries`.

`append_disk_gametype_ids(std::vector<std::string>&, std::unordered_set<std::string>&) -> void` scans every `filesystem::get_search_paths()` directory at `maps/mp/gametypes` and merges discovered file IDs.

`get_visible_gametype_ids(const std::string&) -> std::vector<std::string>` merges IDs in this order: `_gametypes.txt` entries, patch-zone display files, then disk files.

`parse_gametype_display_name(const std::string&, const std::string&) -> std::string` trims input, removes `//` comments, removes one surrounding quote pair, and falls back to the gametype ID for empty content.

## UI cache layout

`GAMETYPE_ENTRY_SIZE` is `0x2C` bytes per UI entry.

`UI_GAMETYPE_COUNT` is `0x113D1684`; `UI_GAMETYPE_ENTRIES` is `0x113D1688`.

`UI_GAMETYPE_ALT_COUNT` is `0x113D31EC`; `UI_GAMETYPE_ALT_ENTRIES` is `0x113D31F0`.

`copy_ui_gametype_string(char*, std::size_t, const std::string&) -> void` uses `strncpy_s(..., _TRUNCATE)` and safely ignores null destinations or zero-sized buffers.

`rebuild_ui_gametype_cache() -> void` reads `GAMETYPES_LIST`, merges IDs, clears both `UI_GAMETYPE_MAX` entry arrays, writes each ID into the first 12 bytes and display text into the remaining `GAMETYPE_ENTRY_SIZE - 0x0C` bytes, then updates both count locations.

`rebuild_ui_gametype_cache()` writes display-backed entries first and stores unavailable display files afterward with the ID as both identifier and display string.

`rebuild_ui_gametype_cache()` logs `gametypes: cannot refresh UI list because %s was empty or unavailable\n`, `gametypes: cannot refresh UI list because %s parsed no entries\n`, and `gametypes: refreshed UI gametype lists with %i visible entries, %i total entries\n`.

`dump_loaded_gametypes_rawfile() -> void` reads `GAMETYPES_LIST` from disk or fastfile, then writes it to `consolation/gametypes_dump/_gametypes.txt`.

`dump_loaded_gametypes_rawfile()` logs `dumpGametypes: %s was empty or unavailable\n`, `dumpGametypes: dumped %s from %s to %s\n`, and `dumpGametypes: failed to write %s\n`.

`dump_parsed_ui_gametypes() -> void` clamps `UI_GAMETYPE_COUNT` to `[0, UI_GAMETYPE_MAX]` and emits entries using the exact format `"{} \"{}\"\r\n"` to `consolation/gametypes_dump/parsed_ui_gametypes.txt`.

`bounded_string(const char*, std::size_t) -> std::string` reads at most the requested length, replaces bytes outside ASCII `[32, 126]` with `'.'`, and prevents unbounded debug reads.

`safe_read_byte(const std::uintptr_t, unsigned char*) -> bool` uses `ReadProcessMemory(GetCurrentProcess(), ...)` and requires exactly one byte read.

`append_bytes(std::string&, const char*, std::uintptr_t, std::size_t) -> void` formats bytes as `"  {} @ {:08X}: "` followed by `"{:02X} "` or `"?? "` and terminates each row with `"\r\n"`.

`dump_debug_state()` writes `primary count: {} @ {:08X}\r\n`, `primary entries: {:08X}\r\n`, `secondary count: {} @ {:08X}\r\n`, and `secondary entries: {:08X}\r\n` records.

`dump_debug_state()` records feeder addresses `0x102DEA4A`, `0x102DE2EF`, `0x102DE2F5`, and `0x102DC430`, plus 3 bytes at `0x102DEA4A`, 3 bytes at `0x102DE2F5`, and 10 bytes at `0x102D4A12`.

`dump_debug_state()` explicitly excludes `game::ASSET_TYPE_MENU`, documenting that `ASSET_TYPE_MENU` represents IW `.menu` assets rather than Scaleform `.gfx`.

`write_file_noexcept(const std::string&, const std::string&, DWORD*) -> bool` resolves relative paths against the executable directory, creates parent directories, writes at most `MAXDWORD` bytes with `CreateFileA(..., CREATE_ALWAYS, ...)`, and returns `GetLastError()` through the optional error pointer.

`create_directory_tree(const std::string&, DWORD*) -> bool` creates each path component with `CreateDirectoryA`, treats `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS` as success, and skips empty components and drive roots.

`resolve_game_path(const std::string&) -> std::string` preserves drive-qualified paths and otherwise prefixes `get_exe_directory()` plus `"\\"`.

`get_exe_directory() -> std::string` uses `GetModuleFileNameA(nullptr, ..., MAX_PATH)` and returns the executable’s parent directory.

## Commands and lifecycle

`register_commands() -> void` registers `dumpGametypes` with `command::add`; the handler calls `dump_loaded_gametypes_rawfile()` and `dump_parsed_ui_gametypes()`.

`register_commands()` is defined but not invoked by `component::post_load()` in this file.

`component::post_load() -> void` installs `db_find_xasset_header_internal_hook`, NOPs the stock hide-last feeder subtraction at `0x102DEA4A` and `0x102DE2F5`, and NOPs the Scaleform fixed-window limit at `0x102D4A12` for 10 bytes.

`component::pre_destroy() -> void` clears `db_find_xasset_header_internal_hook`, `loaded_gametype_rawfiles`, `loaded_scaleform_rawfiles`, and `ui_gametype_list_refreshed`.

`loaded_gametype_rawfiles` and `loaded_scaleform_rawfiles` retain allocated `game::RawFile` objects until `component::pre_destroy()` clears the maps; clearing the maps does not visibly free the allocations created by `utils::memory::allocate`.

## Behavioral constraints

`db_find_xasset_header_internal_stub()` must preserve original lookup through `db_find_xasset_header_internal_hook.invoke<game::XAssetHeader>(...)` when no valid patch or disk override exists.

`append_unique_gametype_id()` lowercases IDs for deduplication and UI output, so case distinctions are intentionally discarded.

`UI_GAMETYPE_MAX == 0x20` bounds all list parsing and cache writes; count values in `dump_parsed_ui_gametypes()` and `dump_debug_state()` are clamped to the same maximum.

`component::post_load()` assumes fixed game offsets and instruction layouts, making `0x10AB8188`, `0x113D1684`, `0x113D1688`, `0x113D31EC`, `0x113D31F0`, `0x102DEA4A`, `0x102DE2F5`, and `0x102D4A12` version-sensitive integration points.

**concurrency.hpp does synchronized access to a default-constructed `T`.**

## API

`container<T, MutexType = std::mutex>` stores `T` with mutable `MutexType`.

`access<R = void>(F&&)` locks via `std::lock_guard`, invokes `F`, returns `R`; const/non-const overloads.

`access_with_lock<R = void>(F&&)` uses `std::unique_lock`, passes lock to `F`; const/non-const overloads.

`get_raw()` returns `T&` or `const T&`, bypassing synchronization.

entries.response:
**hook.hpp does x86 runtime patching, detouring, instruction assembly, and memory access under `utils::hook`.**

## Dependencies

`nt.hpp`, `asmjit::x86::Assembler`, `asmjit::JitRuntime`, `VirtualProtect`, `FlushInstructionCache`, and `GetCurrentProcess` support executable-memory modification and JIT assembly.

## Public API

`assembler` subclasses `Assembler`, re-exports constructors, `call`, and `jmp`, and overloads `call(void*)`/`jmp(void*)` with `asmjit::Error` returns.

`detour` exposes `detour()`, `detour(void*, void*)`, `detour(size_t, void*)`, `~detour()`, move construction/assignment, `enable()`, `disable()`, `create(void*, void*)`, `create(size_t, void*)`, `clear()`, `get_original() -> void*`, `get<T>() -> T*`, and `invoke<T, Args...>(Args...) -> T`; copy operations are deleted.

`nop(void*, size_t)` and `nop(size_t, size_t)` replace bytes with NOPs; `call(...)` and `jump(...)` patch relative or absolute targets across pointer/`size_t` overloads.

`is_relatively_far(const void*, const void*, int offset = 5) -> bool` checks relative-address reachability; `assemble(const std::function<void(assembler&)>&) -> void*` emits assembled code.

`set<T>(void*, T)` and `set<T>(size_t, T)` temporarily apply `PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE`, write `sizeof(T)`, restore protection, and flush the instruction cache.

`invoke<T, Args...>(size_t, Args...)`/`invoke<T, Args...>(void*, Args...)` cast and call function addresses; `get<T>(void*)`/`get<T>(DWORD)` dereference typed memory.

## Lifecycle

`detour::place_` and `detour::original_` track patch and trampoline addresses; move operations null the source, while `enable()`, `disable()`, `create()`, and `clear()` govern patch state.

**hook.cpp implements Windows x86-64 code patching, MinHook detours, IAT replacement, and AsmJit runtime assembly in `utils::hook`.**

## Integration & Lifecycle

`MinHook` initializes via anonymous RAII class `_` at static startup; `MH_Initialize()` failure throws `"Failed to initialize MinHook"`, while `_::~_()` calls `MH_Uninitialize()`.

## Exported Symbols

- `assembler::call(void* target)` and `assembler::jmp(void* target)` forward pointer targets to `asmjit::Assembler`, returning `asmjit::Error`.
- `detour::detour(size_t place, void* target)` and `detour::detour(void* place, void* target)` create and immediately enable hooks.
- `detour::~detour()` calls `clear()`; `detour::enable() const` and `detour::disable() const` call MinHook state transitions.
- `detour::create(void* place, void* target)` and `detour::create(size_t place, void* target)` replace existing hooks, capture `original_`, and throw `"Unable to create hook"` on `MH_CreateHook` failure.
- `detour::clear()` removes `place_` when non-null, then resets `place_` and `original_` to `nullptr`; `detour::get_original() const` returns `void*`.
- `iat(nt::library module, const std::string& target_module, const std::string& process, void* stub)` patches a valid IAT entry and returns `bool`.
- `nop(void* place, size_t length)` and `nop(size_t place, size_t length)` write `0x90` bytes after `VirtualProtect`, restore protection, and flush the instruction cache.
- `is_relatively_far(const void* pointer, const void* data, int offset)` returns whether the signed address delta exceeds `int32_t`.
- `call(...)` emits opcode `0xE8`; `jump(...)` emits opcode `0xE9`; both support pointer/`size_t` overloads and throw `"Too far away to create 32bit relative branch"`.
- `assemble(const std::function<void(assembler&)>& asm_function)` builds code with static `asmjit::JitRuntime` and returns allocated executable `void*`.

## Behavioral Constraints

`call` and `jump` encode 5-byte 32-bit relative branches; `iat` and `nop` depend on Windows `VirtualProtect`, `FlushInstructionCache`, `GetCurrentProcess`, and writable executable memory.

**io.cpp implements Windows file, directory, and PE-string I/O utilities.**

## Public API

- `remove_file(const std::string& file) -> bool` calls `DeleteFileA`; returns `true` only when deletion succeeds.
- `file_exists(const std::string& file) -> bool` tests readability via `std::ifstream(file).good()`.
- `write_file(const std::string& file, const std::string& data, bool append) -> bool` creates parent directories, writes binary data, and appends when `append` is `true`.
- `read_file(const std::string& file) -> std::string` returns file contents or an empty string on failure.
- `read_file(const std::string& file, std::string* data) -> bool` clears `*data`, reads binary contents, and rejects null output pointers.
- `read_pe_string_rva(const std::string& file, std::uint32_t rva, std::size_t max_length) -> std::optional<std::string>` extracts a null-terminated string from a PE section.
- `file_size(const std::string& file) -> size_t` returns byte length or sentinel `0`.
- `create_directory(const std::string& directory) -> bool` delegates recursive creation to `std::filesystem::create_directories`.
- `directory_exists(const std::string& directory) -> bool` delegates to `std::filesystem::is_directory`.
- `directory_is_empty(const std::string& directory) -> bool` delegates to `std::filesystem::is_empty`.
- `list_files(const std::string& directory) -> std::vector<std::string>` returns immediate entries as `generic_string()` paths, or an empty vector on invalid directories/iteration errors.

## PE Parsing Contract

`read_pe_string_rva` validates `IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE`, positive `e_lfanew`, `IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE`, and `sizeof(IMAGE_DOS_HEADER)`/`sizeof(IMAGE_NT_HEADERS)` bounds before mapping `rva` through `IMAGE_FIRST_SECTION`. `read_pe_string_rva` accepts RVAs within `[VirtualAddress, VirtualAddress + max(Misc.VirtualSize, SizeOfRawData))`, reads at most `max_length`, stops at `'\0'`, and returns `std::nullopt` for malformed files, unmapped RVAs, invalid raw offsets, empty strings, or read failures.

## Integration and Caveats

`write_file` depends on `create_directory`; `read_file`, `file_size`, and `read_pe_string_rva` depend on `file_exists`. `remove_file` requires Windows `DeleteFileA`; all stream operations use binary mode. `read_file` resizes using `uint32_t`, so files exceeding 32-bit size may truncate allocation metadata.
