    dnf|yum)
      cmd="sudo $pm install -y"
      pkgs="wine python3 msitools ca-certificates samba-winbind git curl gcc gcc-c++ make"
      ;;
    apt)
      cmd="sudo apt install -y"
      pkgs="wine python3 msitools ca-certificates winbind git curl build-essential"
      ;;
    pacman)
      cmd="sudo pacman -S --noconfirm"
      pkgs="wine python msitools ca-certificates samba git curl base-devel"
      ;;
  esac

  diag "info: installing system dependencies"

  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  run $cmd $pkgs
}

wine_setup ()
{
  diag "info: setting up wine environment"

  export WINEPREFIX="$wn_dir"
  export WINEDLLOVERRIDES="mscoree,mshtml="

  if ! test -d "$wn_dir"; then
    diag "info: initializing wine prefix at $wn_dir/"
    run wineboot --init
  fi

  mmsi="wine-mono-$mn_ver-x86.msi"
  murl="$mn_url/$mn_ver/$mmsi"

  if ! test -f "/tmp/$mmsi"; then
    diag "info: downloading wine-mono $mn_ver"
    download "$murl" "/tmp/$mmsi"
  else
    diag "info: using cached wine-mono installer"
  fi

  diag "info: installing wine-mono"
  run msiexec /i "/tmp/$mmsi" /quiet
}

msvc_setup ()
{
  diag "info: setting up msvc toolchain"

  if ! test -d "msvc-wine"; then
    run git clone "$mw_url" msvc-wine
  else
    # shellcheck disable=SC2164
    run cd msvc-wine
    run git pull
    # shellcheck disable=SC2164
    run cd "$owd"
  fi

  # shellcheck disable=SC2164
  run cd msvc-wine

  if ! test -d "$mi_dir"; then
    diag "info: downloading msvc toolchain to $ca_dir/"
    run mkdir -p "$ca_dir"
    run python3 ./vsdownload.py --accept-license --cache "$ca_dir" --dest "$mi_dir"
  else
    diag "info: msvc toolchain already present at $mi_dir/"
  fi

  diag "info: installing msvc into wine prefix"
  run ./install.sh "$mi_dir"

  # shellcheck disable=SC2164
  run cd "$owd"
}

gen_vscode ()
{
  diag "info: generating vscode configuration"

  run mkdir -p .vscode

  mv="14.44.35207"
  sv="10.0.26100.0"

  if test -d "$mi_dir/vc/tools/msvc"; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC2012
    v="$(ls "$mi_dir/vc/tools/msvc" | sort -V | tail -n 1)"
    if test -n "$v"; then mv="$v"; fi
  fi

  if test -d "$mi_dir/kits/10/Include"; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC2010,SC2012
    v="$(ls "$mi_dir/kits/10/Include" | grep -E '^10\.' | sort -V | tail -n 1)"
    if test -n "$v"; then sv="$v"; fi
  fi

  cat > .vscode/c_cpp_properties.json << EOF
{
  "configurations": [
    {
      "name": "Linux",
      "includePath": [
        "\${default}",
        "$mi_dir/vc/tools/msvc/$mv/atlmfc/include",
        "$mi_dir/vc/tools/msvc/$mv/include",
        "$mi_dir/kits/10/Include/$sv/shared",
        "$mi_dir/kits/10/Include/$sv/ucrt",
        "$mi_dir/kits/10/Include/$sv/um",
        "$mi_dir/kits/10/Include/$sv/winrt",
        "\${workspaceFolder}/**"
      ],
      "defines": [],
      "cStandard": "c17",
      "cppStandard": "c++20",
      "intelliSenseMode": "windows-msvc-x86",
      "forcedInclude": [
        "$owd/src/std_include.hpp"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "version": 4
}
EOF
}

gen_bbuild ()
{
  diag "info: generating build files"

  if ! test -f "tools/premake5.exe"; then
    error "premake5 executable not found in tools/ directory"
  fi

  run wine tools/premake5.exe generate-buildinfo

  sed '/^[[:space:]]*prebuildcommands/,/^[[:space:]]*}/d; /^[[:space:]]*postbuildcommands/,/^[[:space:]]*}/d' premake5.lua > premake5-linux.lua

  run wine tools/premake5.exe --file=premake5-linux.lua "--target-dir=%{wks.location}/bin/%{cfg.buildcfg}" vs2022
  run rm -f premake5-linux.lua
}

compile ()
{
  diag "info: building consolation-client ($cfg)"

  sln="build/consolation-client.sln"
  if ! test -f "$sln"; then
    error "solution file $sln not found"
  fi

  args="/p:Configuration=$cfg /p:Platform=Win32"
  if test "$verb" = true; then
    args="$args /verbosity:detailed"
  fi

  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  run "$mi_dir/bin/x86/msbuild.exe" "$sln" $args
}

sync_submodules ()
{
  if test -z "$submods"; then
    return
  fi

  diag "info: updating git submodules"
  run git submodule sync --recursive
  run git submodule update --init --recursive
}

print_summary ()
{
  diag
  diag "-------------------------------------------------------------------------"
  diag
  diag "Build configuration: $cfg"
  diag "Solution:            $owd/build/consolation-client.sln"
  diag "Output directory:    $owd/build/bin/$cfg/"
  diag
}

build ()
{
  diag
  diag "-------------------------------------------------------------------------"
  diag
  diag "About to perform fast path build of Consolation Client."
  diag
  diag "Build configuration: $cfg"
  diag "Wine prefix:         $wn_dir/"
  diag "MSVC install dir:    $mi_dir/"
  diag
  diag "To perform a from-scratch bootstrap, specify the --force option."
  diag
  prompt

  sync_submodules
  gen_vscode
  gen_bbuild
  compile
  print_summary
}

bootstrap ()
{
  diag
  diag "-------------------------------------------------------------------------"
  diag
  diag "About to bootstrap Consolation Client build environment and compile."
  diag
  diag "Build configuration: $cfg"
  diag "Wine prefix:         $wn_dir/"
  diag "MSVC install dir:    $mi_dir/"
  diag
  if test "$clean" = true; then
    diag "WARNING: --clean option will remove existing wine and msvc installations."
    diag
  fi
  prompt

  if test "$clean" = true; then
    diag "info: cleaning build environment"
    run rm -rf build/ msvc-wine/ "$wn_dir" "$mi_dir" /tmp/wine-mono-*.msi
  fi

  sys_deps

  check_cmd wine "install wine package for your distribution"
  check_cmd git "install git package for your distribution"
  check_cmd curl "install curl package for your distribution"
  check_cmd python3 "install python3 package for your distribution"
  check_cmd msiexec "wine installation may be incomplete"

  wine_setup
  msvc_setup

  sync_submodules
  gen_vscode
  gen_bbuild
  compile
  print_summary

  diag "To rebuild, change to $owd/ and run:"
  diag
  diag "  sh $prog $(echo "$cfg" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
  diag
}

main ()
{
  if check_env; then
    build
  else
    bootstrap
  fi
}

**generate-linux.sh bootstraps and builds the Consolation Client with Wine, MSVC-Wine, Premake, and x86 MSBuild.**

## Interface

- `usage` stores `Usage: $0 [-h|--help] [<options>] [<config>]`; `mn_ver`, `mn_url`, `mw_url`, `ca_dir`, `mi_dir`, `wn_dir`, `cfg`, `to`, and `cto` define toolchain versions, URLs, directories, build configuration, and network timeouts.
- `fail()` restores `owd` with `cd "$owd" || true` and exits status `1`; `diag()` writes blank or variadic diagnostic text to stderr.
- `error()` prefixes diagnostics with `error:` and invokes `fail()`; `run()` logs `+ $*`, executes `"$@"`, and exits through `fail()` on any nonzero status.
- `check_cmd()` validates an executable via `command -v`, emits an optional installation hint, and terminates through `fail()` when missing.
- `prompt()` loops until `yes` is `true`, accepting `y`, `Y`, or empty input; `n`/`N` invokes `fail()`, while other input retries.
- `download(url, output?)` invokes `curl -fL --connect-timeout "$cto" --max-time "$to" --progress-bar` with `-o "$2"` or `-O`.
- `check_env()` returns `1` when `force=true`, `$wn_dir` or `$mi_dir` is absent, or `$mi_dir/bin/x86/msbuild.exe` is absent; otherwise returns `0`.
- `sys_deps()` detects `dnf`, `yum`, `apt`, or `pacman`, then installs Wine, Python, MSITools, certificates, Git, Curl, compiler tools, and platform-specific Winbind packages through `sudo`.
- `wine_setup()` exports `WINEPREFIX="$wn_dir"` and `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="mscoree,mshtml="`, initializes `$wn_dir` with `wineboot --init`, downloads `/tmp/wine-mono-11.0.0-x86.msi`, and installs it through `msiexec /i ... /quiet`.

- `gen_vscode()` creates `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json` with MSVC/Windows SDK include paths, `cStandard: "c17"`, `cppStandard: "c++20"`, `intelliSenseMode: "windows-msvc-x86"`, and forced include `$owd/src/std_include.hpp`.

- `compile()` requires `build/consolation-client.sln`, invokes `$mi_dir/bin/x86/msbuild.exe` with `/p:Configuration=$cfg /p:Platform=Win32`, and adds `/verbosity:detailed` when `verb=true`.
- `sync_submodules()` runs `git submodule sync --recursive` and `git submodule update --init --recursive` unless `submods` is empty.
- `print_summary()` reports `$cfg`, `$owd/build/consolation-client.sln`, and `$owd/build/bin/$cfg/`.

- `bootstrap()` optionally removes `build/`, `msvc-wine/`, `$wn_dir`, `$mi_dir`, and `/tmp/wine-mono-*.msi`, installs dependencies, validates commands, runs setup/generation/build stages, and prints the rebuild command.

## CLI Contract

- `--yes`, `--clean`, `--no-deps`, `--no-submodules`, `--force`, and `--verbose` set `yes`, `clean`, `deps`, `submods`, `force`, and `verb`.
- `--cache-dir <dir>`, `--msvc-dir <dir>`, `--wine-dir <dir>`, and `--timeout <sec>` override `ca_dir`, `mi_dir`, `wn_dir`, and `to`; missing values produce `error`.

- `-h|--help` exits `0`; unknown options emit `error: unknown option '$1'`; invalid configurations emit `error: invalid build configuration '$bcfg' (expected debug or release)`.
- `verb=true` enables shell tracing with `set -x`; `to=300` and `cto=30` control Curl total and connect timeouts.

- `clean=true` triggers destructive `run rm -rf`; `prompt()` gates both `build()` and `bootstrap()` unless `--yes` is supplied.

-- Quote the given string input as a C string
function cstrquote(value)
	if value == nil then
		return "\"\""
	end
	result = value:gsub("\\", "\\\\")
	result = result:gsub("\"", "\\\"")
	result = result:gsub("\n", "\\n")
	result = result:gsub("\t", "\\t")
	result = result:gsub("\r", "\\r")
	result = result:gsub("\a", "\\a")
	result = result:gsub("\b", "\\b")

-- Converts tags in "vX.X.X" format and given revision number Y to an array of numbers {X,X,X,Y}.
-- In the case where the format does not work fall back to padding with zeroes and just ending with the revision number.
-- partscount can be either 3 or 4.
function vertonumarr(value, vernumber, partscount)
	vernum = {}
	for num in string.gmatch(value or "", "%d+") do
		if #vernum < 3 then
			table.insert(vernum, tonumber(num))
		end
	end
	while #vernum < 3 do

**premake5.lua defines Premake build configuration, Git-derived version generation, dependency loading, and Windows DLL projects.**

## Public symbols

- `gitVersioningCommand = "git describe --tags --dirty --always"` and `gitCurrentBranchCommand = "git symbolic-ref -q --short HEAD"` store Git command strings; only `gitVersioningCommand` is used.
- `cstrquote(value) -> string` escapes `\`, `"`, newline, tab, carriage return, bell, and backspace, returns quoted C-string text, and maps `nil` to `""`.
- `vertonumarr(value, vernumber, partscount) -> table<number>` extracts at most three numeric components, pads missing components with `0`, and appends `tonumber(vernumber)` until length reaches `partscount` (normally `3` or `4`).
- `getbaseversion(tagName) -> string` converts `[vV]?major.minor.patch` tags to `major.minor.patch`, defaulting invalid, empty, or `nil` input to `"0.0.1"`.
- `readbuildcounter(path) -> number` reads and whitespace-strips a counter file, returning numeric content or `0` for missing/invalid files.
- `dependencies = { basePath = "./deps" }` models dependency modules discovered from `./deps/premake/*.lua`.
- `dependencies.load() -> nil` requires each discovered dependency Lua file.
- `dependencies.imports() -> nil` invokes numeric dependency entries’ `import()` methods.
- `dependencies.projects() -> nil` invokes numeric dependency entries’ `project()` methods.

## Premake actions and options

- `newoption("copy-to")` accepts `PATH` and enables post-build DLL copying for `d3d9` and `xlive`.
- `newoption("target-dir")` accepts `PATH` and overrides Premake’s workspace target directory.
- `newaction("version")` runs `git rev-list --count HEAD`, prints the revision count, then calls `os.exit(0)`.
- `newaction("generate-buildinfo")` scans `src/version.h`, runs Git metadata commands, increments `src/build_counter.txt`, writes `version.txt`, and regenerates `src/version.h` plus `src/version.hpp` when generated values change.

## Version-generation contract

`generate-buildinfo` uses `git describe --tags --dirty --always`, `git describe --tags --abbrev=0`, `git rev-list --count HEAD`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain`, and `git branch --show-current`; detached-HEAD fallback parses `git show -s --pretty=%d HEAD`, then defaults `GIT_BRANCH` to `"develop"`.

`generate-buildinfo` recognizes existing definitions with exact patterns `#define GIT_DESCRIBE (.+)%s*$`, `#define VERSION_PRODUCT \"([^\"]*)\"%s*$`, and `#define VERSION_BUILD \"([^\"]*)\"%s*$`.

`src/version.h` receives `GIT_DESCRIBE`, `GIT_DIRTY` (`0`/`1`), `GIT_HASH`, `GIT_TAG`, `GIT_BRANCH`, `VERSION_PRODUCT_RC`, `VERSION_PRODUCT`, `VERSION_BUILD`, `VERSION_FILE_RC`, `VERSION_FILE`, `VERSION`, and `SHORTVERSION`; `src/version.hpp` includes `".\\version.h"`.

`VERSION_PRODUCT_RC` uses `vertonumarr(baseVersion, revNumber, 3)`, while `VERSION_FILE_RC` and `VERSION_FILE` use `vertonumarr(baseVersion, buildNumber, 4)`; missing Git tags resolve through `getbaseversion` to `"0.0.1"`.

`buildCounter` increments `src/build_counter.txt` only when `GIT_DESCRIBE`, `VERSION_PRODUCT`, or `VERSION_BUILD` differs from the existing header; `version.txt` stores the raw `gitCommitHash`.

## Workspace and projects

`workspace "consolation-client"` selects `startproject "consolation-client"`, emits files under `./build`, uses `targetdir(_OPTIONS["target-dir"] or "%{wks.location}/bin/%{cfg.buildcfg}")`, and logs to `%{wks.location}/obj/%{cfg.architecture}/%{cfg.buildcfg}/%{prj.name}/%{prj.name}.log`.

`workspace "consolation-client"` targets C++20, `x86`/`Win32`, `v143`, `systemversion "latest"`, static runtime, ASCII charset, symbols, extra warnings, `/std:c++latest`, `/FS`, `_SILENCE_ALL_CXX17_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS`, and flags `NoIncrementalLink`, `NoMinimalRebuild`, `MultiProcessorCompile`, `No64BitChecks`.

`d3d9` is a `SharedLib` hooking the game, links `hid` and `setupapi`, compiles `src/**.h`, `src/**.hpp`, `src/**.cpp`, and `src/**.rc`, uses `std_include.hpp` PCH from `src/std_include.cpp`, and runs `tools\\premake5 generate-buildinfo` as a prebuild command.

`xlive` is a `SharedLib` with target name `"xlive"`, links `ws2_32` and `shell32`, compiles `src_xlive/**.cpp`, `src_xlive/**.hpp`, `src_xlive/**.h`, and `src_xlive/**.def`, includes the Microsoft Games for Windows - LIVE SDK path, and links `../src_xlive/xlive.def` via `/DEF`.

`d3d9` and `xlive` conditionally execute `copy /y "$(TargetPath)" "<copy-to>"`; `dependencies.imports()` attaches dependency imports to `d3d9`, while `dependencies.projects()` adds dependency projects under group `"Dependencies"`.

## Configuration behavior

`Debug` enables `DEBUG` and `_DEBUG` with debug optimization; `Release` enables `NDEBUG`, `/Os`, full optimization, `FatalCompileWarnings`, and `LinkTimeOptimization`.

`filter "platforms:Win*"` defines `_WINDOWS` and `WIN32`; `architecture "x86"`, `platforms { "Win32" }`, and `toolset "v143"` make the configuration Windows-specific.

**bots.cpp does server-side bot movement, targeting, combat, cover seeking, health synchronization, and engine-hook lifecycle integration for up to 18 clients.**

## Role and integration

`bots::component` integrates custom bot behavior into the game through `component_interface`, `REGISTER_COMPONENT(bots::component)`, `post_load()`, and `pre_destroy()`.

`game::game_offset()` resolves hard-coded engine addresses; `game::SV_ClientThink` supplies the original client-think function; `game::SV_BotUserMove` supplies the bot movement hook target; `utils::hook::call()` installs `client_enter_world_hook`; `utils::hook::jump()` replaces the native bot movement routine.

`component::post_load()` stores `SV_ClientThink.get()` in `s_client_think_real_addr`, hooks engine address `0x10414440` with `client_enter_world_hook`, jumps `SV_BotUserMove.get()` to `sv_bot_user_move_hook`, initializes `s_tracked_target` to `-1`, and registers shutdown cleanup through `scheduler::on_shutdown()`.

`component::pre_destroy()` restores the five original bytes at `game_offset(0x10414440)` as `E8 2B 5E D9 FF` and restores the first five bytes at `SV_BotUserMove.get()` as `83 EC 30 83 BE`.

`game::entity_t`, `game::playerState_t`, `game::clientState_t`, `game::usercmd_t`, `game::usercmd_buttons`, and `game::dvar_s` are accessed through direct memory layouts and engine globals, making this code version-sensitive to the target executable.

`dvars::bot_maxHealth` controls bot health; `sv_maxclients_dvar()` controls client iteration bounds; `sv_bots_press_attack_dvar()` gates ranged bot firing.

## Public symbol

`bots::component final : public component_interface` exposes:

- `void post_load() override` — resolves the original think address, installs enter-world and bot-movement hooks, initializes target state, and registers shutdown state reset.
- `void pre_destroy() override` — restores overwritten engine instruction bytes before component unload.

`REGISTER_COMPONENT(bots::component)` registers the component with the loader.

## Engine memory contracts

`CLIENT_STRIDE = 688916` bytes separates client records; `CLIENT_ENTITYPTR_OFF = 0x2128C` locates the client entity pointer; `CLIENT_LAST_USERCMD_OFF = 0x20E9C` locates the last `game::usercmd_t`; `CLIENT_USERINFO_OFF = 1604` locates the backslash-delimited user-info string.

`PS_ORIGIN_OFFSET = 0x20` locates player-state origin; `PS_MAXHEALTH_OFFSET = 0x32C4` locates player-state maximum health; the player-state health field is read at offset `0x1CC`.

`SNAPINFO_STRIDE = 13504` and `SNAPINFO_DEAD_OFF = 0x3228` locate per-client dead-state data in `g_snapshot_info()`; null `g_snapshot_info()` conservatively makes `client_is_dead()` return `true`.

`g_entities()` reads entity storage from `game_offset(0x11961F80)`; `g_clients()` dereferences the client-base pointer at `game_offset(0x11CA5D8C)`; `g_snapshot_info()` dereferences snapshot info at `game_offset(0x11A34458)`.

## Team and target selection

`parse_team_value(const std::string& value) -> game::bot_team` lowercases input with `utils::string::to_lower()` and recognizes:

- `axis`, `1`, or substrings `axis`, `cell`, `enemy` → `game::bot_team::axis`
- `allies`, `2`, or substrings `allies`, `mi6`, `friendly` → `game::bot_team::allies`
- `spectator`, `3` → `game::bot_team::spectator`
- `free`, `0`, `none` → `game::bot_team::free`
- all other values, including empty values → `game::bot_team::unknown`

`client_team(int idx) -> game::bot_team` reads `teamNum` first from `client_userinfo(idx)` and falls back to `team` only when `teamNum` parses as `unknown`.

`should_target_client(int bot_idx, int target_idx) -> bool` rejects self-targeting, inactive clients (`game::CS_ACTIVE` mismatch), dead clients, null entities, and entities with `health <= 0`; unknown-vs-unknown teams are rejected, unknown/free bot teams target every non-spectator target, and known teams reject spectators and same-team clients.

`client_state(int idx) -> game::clientState_t` copies the client-state structure from `client_at(idx)`; `client_is_real_player(int idx) -> bool` tests the integer flag at client offset `0x20`; `client_is_dead(int idx) -> bool` reads snapshot dead state; `client_userinfo(int idx) -> const char*` returns the user-info buffer; `client_last_usercmd(int idx) -> game::usercmd_t*` returns the last command pointer.

`client_recently_fired(int idx, int command_time) -> bool` requires `BUTTON_ATTACK`, computes `age = command_time - cmd->serverTime`, and accepts ages in `[0, 1200]`; structured exception handling converts invalid command memory into `false`.

## Persistent bot state

`MAX_CLIENTS = 18` sizes all per-client arrays; `bot_state_index(int client_idx) -> int` maps valid indices `[0, MAX_CLIENTS)` to themselves and invalid indices to `-1`.

`s_attack_phase[MAX_CLIENTS]` tracks attack-phase state; `s_tracked_target[MAX_CLIENTS]` stores target indices and uses `-1` as the no-target sentinel; `s_last_visible_time[MAX_CLIENTS]` stores the last target visibility timestamp; `s_last_seen_origin[MAX_CLIENTS][3]` stores the latest remembered target eye position.

`s_last_cmd_yaw[MAX_CLIENTS]` and `s_last_cmd_pitch[MAX_CLIENTS]` support aim-settling checks; `s_search_yaw[MAX_CLIENTS]` and `s_next_search_time[MAX_CLIENTS]` drive idle search movement; `s_last_progress_time[MAX_CLIENTS]` and `s_last_progress_origin[MAX_CLIENTS][3]` detect stuck bots; `s_last_applied_bot_max_health` prevents redundant health synchronization.

`clear_bot_target_state(int client_idx) -> void` resets attack, target, visibility, aim, search-progress, and remembered-origin state for one valid client while preserving invalid indices.

`component::post_load()` shutdown cleanup zeroes every state array, refills `s_tracked_target` with `-1`, and resets `s_last_applied_bot_max_health` to `0`.

## Geometry, visibility, and cover

`IW_RAD_TO_ANGLE = 10430.378f` converts radians to engine angle units; `normalize_angle_units(int angle) -> int` wraps values into approximately `[-32768, 32768]`.

`get_eye_position(const game::playerState_t* ps, float eye_height, float* out) -> void` copies player origin and adds `eye_height` to Z; `BOT_EYE_HEIGHT = 56.0f`, `TARGET_EYE_HEIGHT = 48.0f`, and `TARGET_TORSO_HEIGHT = 26.0f`.

`distance_squared_3d(const float* a, const float* b) -> float` computes squared Euclidean distance; `copy_vec3(float* out, const float* in) -> void` copies three coordinates; `set_vec3(float* out, float x, float y, float z) -> void` writes three coordinates.

`vector_length_2d(float x, float y) -> float` and `vector_length_3d(float x, float y, float z) -> float` use square-root Euclidean norms; `vector_to_yaw_units(float x, float y) -> int` applies `atan2f(y, x) * IW_RAD_TO_ANGLE`.

`yaw_units_to_forward_right(int yaw_units, float* forward, float* right) -> void` converts engine yaw units into normalized horizontal forward/right vectors using `sinf()` and `cosf()`.

`build_target_sample_points(const float* bot_eye, const game::playerState_t* target_ps, float samples[5][3]) -> void` creates five visibility samples: target eye center, eye ± lateral offsets, torso, and low body; `TARGET_SAMPLE_WIDTH = 10.0f`.

`sample_target_visibility(const float* bot_eye, int bot_idx, const game::playerState_t* target_ps) -> float` traces all five samples and returns visible-sample fraction in `{0.0f, 0.2f, 0.4f, 0.6f, 0.8f, 1.0f}`.

`find_cover_goal(const float* bot_eye, int bot_idx, const float* enemy_eye, int enemy_idx, float* out_goal) -> bool` evaluates five lateral/backward/diagonal candidates, requires bot-to-candidate visibility, rejects enemy-to-candidate visibility, and chooses the nearest valid candidate by squared distance.

`COVER_OFFSET_SIDE = 96.0f`, `COVER_OFFSET_BACK = 128.0f`, and `COVER_OFFSET_DIAGONAL = 72.0f` define cover candidates; `COVER_COMMIT_RANGE = 80.0f` prevents unnecessary movement once near cover.

## Movement and stuck recovery

`set_move_toward(game::usercmd_t& cmd, int view_yaw, int move_yaw, std::int8_t forward_speed, std::int8_t side_speed) -> void` converts yaw delta into movement: delta within `4096` uses full forward, delta at least `24576` uses half reverse, and intermediate deltas use half forward plus signed strafing.

`apply_search_movement(game::usercmd_t& cmd, int bot_idx, int command_time) -> void` updates search yaw every `SEARCH_UPDATE_MS = 900`, computes `degrees = ((phase * 45) + bot_idx * 35) % 360`, writes yaw/pitch/roll as search yaw/`0`/`0`, moves forward at `127`, and adds `game::BUTTON_SPRINT`.

`bot_is_stuck(int bot_idx, const game::playerState_t* bot_ps) -> bool` records progress origin and command time, treats movement greater than `STUCK_DIST_EPSILON = 24.0f` as progress, and reports stuck after `STUCK_REPATH_MS = 1400` without sufficient displacement.

`bot_user_move_impl()` applies alternating yaw perturbations of `±8192` and alternating forward/right/up movement when `bot_is_stuck()` is true; grounded bots receive `upmove = 127`, and stuck recovery adds `BUTTON_SPRINT`.

## Health management

`get_bot_max_health() -> int` returns positive `dvars::bot_maxHealth->current.integer`, otherwise `100`.

`sanitize_bot_health(int client_idx, bool force_full_health, bool assume_bot = false) -> void` skips real players unless `assume_bot` is true, writes player-state max health, forcefully sets entity/player health to max when requested, clamps invalid live health values, and caps dead health values without reviving dead clients.

`sync_bot_health_from_dvar() -> void` compares `get_bot_max_health()` against `s_last_applied_bot_max_health`, iterates clients below `game::CS_CONNECTED`, skips real players, calls `sanitize_bot_health(i, true)`, and records the applied max health.

`client_enter_world_hook()` sets `s_last_applied_bot_max_health` to the current dvar value and calls `sanitize_bot_health(client_idx, true)` after the native enter-world routine.

## `bot_user_move_impl()` behavior

`bot_user_move_impl(std::uintptr_t client) -> void` exits when `g_clients()` is null, synchronizes health, derives `bot_idx = (client - clients_base) / CLIENT_STRIDE`, sanitizes bot health, and initializes a zeroed `game::usercmd_t`.

`bot_user_move_impl()` copies weapon state from `g_archived_snap_base()[bot_idx * g_archived_snap_stride() + 0xF0]` when archived snapshots are valid; the default max-client fallback is `12` when `sv_maxclients_dvar()` is unavailable.

`bot_user_move_impl()` scans valid target clients, computes target-eye squared distance and five-point visibility, scores visible targets as `(visibility * 600000.0f) - d2` plus `60000.0f` for the tracked target, and scores hidden targets as `-d2` plus `50000.0f` for the tracked target and `85000.0f` for recently firing targets.

`TARGET_MEMORY_MS = 5000` allows a bot to pursue the last tracked target and last seen eye position for five seconds after visibility is lost; visible targets refresh `s_tracked_target`, `s_last_visible_time`, and `s_last_seen_origin`.

`bot_user_move_impl()` selects visible targets before hidden targets, retains valid tracked targets within `TARGET_MEMORY_MS`, calls `clear_bot_target_state()` when no target remains, and falls back to `apply_search_movement()` when no target or player state exists.

`bot_user_move_impl()` aims at target yaw and torso pitch, clamps pitch to `[-1400, 1400]`, stores the latest aim units, and defines `aim_settled` as yaw/pitch deltas each within `AIM_SETTLE_THRESHOLD = 1400`.

`bot_user_move_impl()` seeks cover when the target is visible, visibility is at least `0.4f`, distance is at most `FIRE_RANGE = 1400.0f`, and bot health is at most `max(35, max_health / 2)`.

`bot_user_move_impl()` uses full forward speed `96` and side speed `48` against visible targets, or forward `127` and side `32` while searching/approaching hidden targets; sprint is added beyond `SPRINT_RANGE = 700.0f` or whenever the target is hidden.

`bot_user_move_impl()` applies periodic strafing `±24` for visible targets in `(192.0f, FIRE_RANGE)`, periodic crouch within `CROUCH_RANGE = 384.0f` and beyond `160.0f`, and melee attack plus `BUTTON_MELEE_BREATH` within `MELEE_RANGE * 1.5f = 144.0f`.

`bot_user_move_impl()` adds `BUTTON_ADS` for visible targets with visibility at least `0.4f` and distance greater than `256.0f`.

`bot_user_move_impl()` adds `BUTTON_ATTACK` only when `sv_bots_press_attack_dvar()->current.enabled`, target visibility is positive, distance is at most `FIRE_RANGE`, and aim alignment satisfies `aim_settled` or yaw/pitch delta within `FIRE_ALIGNMENT_THRESHOLD * 2 = 2400`.

`bot_user_move_impl()` increases forward movement to at least `48` and alternates side movement `±32` for ranged attacks beyond `224.0f`; otherwise `s_attack_phase[state_idx]` is cleared.

`bot_user_move_impl()` decrements the client command counter through `*(int*)(client + 0x08) = *(int*)(client + 0x10) - 1`, invokes `call_sv_client_think_real(client, &cmd)`, and sanitizes bot health again after native processing.

## Observable constants and assumptions

`CONTENTS_SOLID_SHOT = 41969713`, `ENTITYNUM_NONE = 1023`, `MAX_CLIENTS = 18`, `TARGET_MEMORY_MS = 5000`, `SEARCH_UPDATE_MS = 900`, `STUCK_REPATH_MS = 1400`, `AIM_SETTLE_THRESHOLD = 1400`, `FIRE_VISIBILITY_THRESHOLD = 3`, `FIRE_ALIGNMENT_THRESHOLD = 1200`, `MELEE_RANGE = 96.0f`, `CROUCH_RANGE = 384.0f`, `SPRINT_RANGE = 700.0f`, `FIRE_RANGE = 1400.0f`, and `STUCK_DIST_EPSILON = 24.0f` define gameplay thresholds and must remain synchronized with engine units.

`FIRE_VISIBILITY_THRESHOLD` is declared as `3` but ranged-fire logic compares `best_visibility` directly against `0.0f` and `0.4f`; changing this unused constant alone does not alter firing behavior.

`__asm`, `__try`, `__except`, absolute game offsets, client strides, and raw structure offsets require the original 32-bit Windows-compatible compiler/runtime and matching game binary layout.

- `ItemKeyHandler` forms a linked list with `key`, `action`, and `next`; `columnInfo_s` stores `pos`, `width`, `maxChars`, and `alignment`.
- `operationEnum` encodes UI expression operators from `OP_NOOP=0x0` through `OP_STATRANGEBITSSET=0x49`, with `OP_RIGHTPAREN=0x1`, arithmetic/comparison/logical/bitwise operators, `OP_SIN=0x17`, `OP_FIRSTFUNCTIONCALL=0x17`, `OP_COS=0x18`, `OP_MIN=0x19`, `OP_MAX=0x1A`, dvar/localvar/stat/UI/game queries, conversions, and `NUM_OPERATORS=0x4A`.

- `editFieldDef_s` stores value bounds/default/range and character/paint limits; `listBoxDef_s` stores four-element scroll bounds, element dimensions/style, `columnInfo[16]`, double-click action, selection flags/colors, and `selectIcon`.
- `multiDef_s` stores 32-entry `dvarList`, `dvarStr`, and `dvarValue` arrays plus `count` and `strDef`; `itemDefData_t` selects list-box, edit-field, multi, enum-dvar, or generic `data`.

- `menuDef_t` embeds `windowDef_t`, font/fullscreen/item/cursor/fade/blur state, lifecycle callbacks `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onESC`, keyboard handlers, visibility/rectangle expressions, binding/sound/image data, colors, and `items: itemDef_s**`; `sizeof(menuDef_t)==308`.
- `MenuList` stores `name`, `menuCount`, and `menus: menuDef_t**`.

- `RawFile` stores `name`, byte `len`, and mutable `buffer`; `sizeof(RawFile)==12`.

- `XAsset` pairs `type: XAssetType` with `header: XAssetHeader`; `XZoneInfo` stores `name`, `allocFlags`, and `freeFlags` with size 12; `XZone` stores `name[64]` and `flags` with size 68.
- `XAssetEntry` combines `XAsset`, `zoneIndex`, `inuse`, `nextHash`, `nextOverride`, and `usageFrame`; `XAssetEntryPoolEntry` uses a union Strategy to represent either `entry` or intrusive `next`.
- `CmdArgs` stores eight-level command nesting, local-client/controller indices, `argc`, and `argv`; `cmd_function_s` forms a command linked list with autocomplete metadata and `void(__cdecl* function)()`.
- `scrMemTreePub_t` stores `mt_buffer`; `ScreenPlacement` stores virtual/real scaling and viewport bounds as nine `float[2]` arrays.

## Dvars and scripting ABI

- `DvarType : uint8_t` maps `DVAR_TYPE_BOOL=0x0`, `DVAR_TYPE_FLOAT=0x1`, `DVAR_TYPE_FLOAT_2=0x2`, `DVAR_TYPE_FLOAT_3=0x3`, `DVAR_TYPE_FLOAT_4=0x4`, `DVAR_TYPE_INT=0x5`, `DVAR_TYPE_ENUM=0x6`, `DVAR_TYPE_STRING=0x7`, `DVAR_TYPE_COLOR=0x8`, and `DVAR_TYPE_COUNT=0x9`.

- `VariableType` defines script sentinels and values: `VAR_UNDEFINED=0x0`, `VAR_BEGIN_REF=0x1`, `VAR_POINTER=0x1`, `VAR_STRING=0x2`, `VAR_ISTRING=0x3`, `VAR_VECTOR=0x4`, `VAR_END_REF=0x5`, `VAR_FLOAT=0x5`, `VAR_INTEGER=0x6`, `VAR_CODEPOS=0x7`, `VAR_PRECODEPOS=0x8`, `VAR_FUNCTION=0x9`, `VAR_BUILTIN_FUNCTION=0xA`, `VAR_BUILTIN_METHOD=0xB`, `VAR_STACK=0xC`, `VAR_ANIMATION=0xD`, `VAR_DEVELOPER_CODEPOS=0xE`, `VAR_INCLUDE_CODEPOS=0xF`, `VAR_THREAD_LIST=0x10`, `VAR_THREAD=0x11`, `VAR_NOTIFY_THREAD=0x12`, `VAR_TIME_THREAD=0x13`, `VAR_CHILD_THREAD=0x14`, `VAR_OBJECT=0x15`, `VAR_DEAD_ENTITY=0x16`, `VAR_ENTITY=0x17`, `VAR_ARRAY=0x18`, `VAR_DEAD_THREAD=0x19`, `VAR_COUNT=0x1A`, `VAR_FREE=0x1A`, and `VAR_ENDON_LIST=0x1B`.

## Input and gameplay ABI

- `keyNum_t` preserves engine key codes: gamepad ranges `K_BUTTON_A`–`K_BUTTON_Y`, shoulder/start/back/stick/trigger buttons, `K_DPAD_UP`–`K_DPAD_RIGHT`, `K_APAD_UP`–`K_APAD_RIGHT`, keyboard controls through `K_BACKSPACE`, extended ASCII `K_ASCII_FIRST`–`K_END_ASCII_CHARS`, system/function/keypad codes through `K_KP_EQUALS`, mouse/aux codes `K_MOUSE1`–`K_AUX16`, and `K_LAST_KEY=0xDF`; aliases include `K_NONE`, `K_TAB`, `K_ENTER`, `K_ESCAPE`, `K_SPACE`, `K_GRAVE`, and `K_TILDE`.
- `KeyState` stores `down`, `repeats`, and `binding`; `PlayerKeyState` stores `overstrikeMode`, `anyKeyDown`, and `keys[256]`; `field_t` stores cursor/scroll/drawing metrics and `buffer[256]`.
- `usercmd_buttons` defines `BUTTON_ATTACK=0x1`, `BUTTON_SPRINT=0x2`, `BUTTON_MELEE_BREATH=0x4`, `BUTTON_USE=0x8`, `BUTTON_RELOAD=0x20`, `BUTTON_PRONE=0x80`, `BUTTON_CROUCH=0x100`, `BUTTON_ADS=0x200`, and `BUTTON_HOLDBREATH=0x800`.
- `usercmd_t` is a 44-byte per-frame command with `serverTime`, button mask, `weapon`, offhand/flags, unknown word, `angles[3]`, signed `forwardmove`/`rightmove`, `upmove`, and `unk_20[3]`; `sizeof(usercmd_t)==0x2C`, angle units use `0x8000==360°`, and movement bounds are `-127..127`.
- `clientState_t` defines `CS_FREE=0`, `CS_ZOMBIE=1`, `CS_CONNECTED=2`, `CS_CLIENTLOADING=3`, and `CS_ACTIVE=4`; `bot_team : uint8_t` defines `unknown`, `free`, `axis`, `allies`, and `spectator`.
- `playerState_t` is a partial offset-preserving layout with confirmed `commandTime`, `pm_type`, `pm_flags`, `origin[3]`, `gravity`, `health`, `maxHealth`, `viewHeightTarget`, `viewangles[3]`, and `serverTime_copy`; gaps are byte arrays, `groundEntityNum==1023` means `ENTITYNUM_NONE`, and total size is at least `0x34B4`.
- `entity_t` has stride `0x290`, `ps: playerState_t*` at `+0x184`, mirrored `health` at `+0x1CC`, and `sizeof(entity_t)==0x290`; client entities occupy indices `0..sv_maxclients-1`.
- `client_t` begins with `state: clientState_t` at `+0x00000`, `isRealPlayer` at `+0x20`, and a large unreversed remainder; runtime stride is `688916 (0xA8314)` bytes, with deep fields accessed by byte offsets `+0x20E9C` (`usercmd_t`), `+0x2128C` (`entity_t*`), and `+0x213A4` (`last_svtime`).

## Coupling and maintenance constraints

- `Material`, `windowDef_t`, `menuDef_t`, `XAssetHeader`, `dvar_s`, `usercmd_t`, `playerState_t`, `entity_t`, and `client_t` are binary-layout contracts, so changing field order, packing, pointer width, enum underlying types, or padding can break engine interoperability.
- `std::uint8_t`, `std::uint16_t`, `std::int8_t`, `uint8_t`, and `uint16_t` require standard integer headers elsewhere; `__int16`, `__int64`, `__cdecl`, and `__stdcall` require the project’s MSVC-compatible ABI.
- `XAssetHeader`, `DvarValue`, `DvarLimits`, `VariableUnion`, `itemDefData_t`, `GfxDrawSurf`, and `GfxStateBits` require tag/context discipline because the active union member is selected externally.
- `playerState_t`, `entity_t`, and `client_t` intentionally contain unreversed regions; consumers must use documented offsets and must not infer absent members from padding.

**xlive_shim.cpp emulates the Windows LIVE/XLive API with Winsock forwarding, offline identity, local profile settings, title storage, and synchronous overlapped-operation stubs.**

## Role and architecture

`xlive_shim.cpp` implements an `extern "C"`/`WINAPI` compatibility layer for a game DLL, forwarding socket calls to Winsock while replacing Xbox LIVE services with deterministic offline behavior.

`qos_module()`, `qos_address<T>()`, and `find_dvar()` optionally inspect `jb_mp_s.dll` using fixed IDA addresses `qos_base = 0x10000000`, `dvar_hash_table_addr = 0x1149FCE0`, and `generate_hash_value_addr = 0x10275260`.

`offline_name()` resolves the identity from the in-process `name` dvar (`type == 7`), command-line `name`, `+name`, `-name`, `-set name value`, or `-seta name value`, falling back to `"Player"`.

`offline_xuid()` applies 64-bit FNV-1a hashing with offset basis `1469598103934665603ull` and prime `1099511628211ull`, then returns `0x1100001000000000ull | (hash & 0x0000FFFFFFFFFFFFull)`.

`storage_root()` stores state beside the executable in `storage`, falling back to `current_path()/storage` when `GetModuleFileNameW` fails or truncates its 32768-character buffer.

`offline_profile_root()` resolves to `storage/profiles/<16-digit-uppercase-hex-XUID>`; `profile_setting_path()` resolves to `settings/<8-digit-title-ID>/<8-digit-setting-ID>.bin`, substituting `qos_title_id = 0x41560829` when `title_id == 0`.

`title_storage_path()` strips case-insensitive `offline://`, splits the first `/` into facility and item, defaults facility to `"3"`, and maps files beneath `title_storage/<sanitized-facility>/<sanitized-item>`.

`sanitize_storage_name()` replaces control characters and `<>:"/\\|?*` with `_`, and changes empty, `"."`, or `".."` names to `"unnamed"`.

`read_file()` and `write_file()` implement binary local persistence; `write_file()` creates parent directories and truncates existing files.

`import_legacy_qos_profile()` performs a one-time scan of `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Xlive\Content` for `41560829.gpd`, validates little-endian `FBDX`/XDBF tables, and imports namespace-3 setting payloads only when destination files do not exist.

`complete_overlapped()` writes `internal_low`, `internal_high`, and `extended_error`, signals `event`, and invokes `completion_routine`; `finish_operation()` returns `ERROR_IO_PENDING` when an `xoverlapped*` exists, otherwise the supplied error.

`inert_success()` and `inert_not_found()` complete optional `xoverlapped` structures with `ERROR_SUCCESS` or `ERROR_NOT_FOUND`.

## Internal ABI structures and constants

`XUID` aliases `unsigned long long`; `xoverlapped`, `xsession_info`, `xstorage_download_results`, `xuser_data`, `xuser_profile_setting`, `xuser_read_profile_setting_result`, and `xuser_signin_info` mirror expected XLive memory layouts.

`xuser_data` uses type tags `1` int32, `2` int64, `3` double, `4` Unicode, `5` float, `6` binary, `7` FILETIME, and `0xFF` null.

`xuser_profile_setting` uses `xsource_no_value = 0` and `xsource_title = 2`; `xuser_read_profile_setting_result` stores an inline array of settings followed by variable-sized Unicode/binary payloads.

`xstorage_download_results` returns `bytes_total`, `xuid_owner`, and current `FILETIME created`.

`xuser_signin_info` uses `signed_in_to_live = 2`, `info_flags = 1`, and a 16-byte `user_name`.

`xonline_e_storage_file_not_found = 0x8015C004`, `xonline_e_storage_file_is_too_big = 0x8015C003`, `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER`, `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`, `ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES`, `ERROR_NOT_FOUND`, and `ERROR_WRITE_FAULT` are observable result codes.

## Exported Winsock bridge

- `int WINAPI xlive_XWSAStartup(WORD version, WSADATA* data)` forwards to `WSAStartup`.
- `SOCKET WINAPI xlive_XSocketCreate(int af, int type, int protocol)` forwards to `socket`.
- `int WINAPI xlive_XSocketClose(SOCKET socket_handle)` forwards to `closesocket`.
- `int WINAPI xlive_XSocketIOCTLSocket(SOCKET socket_handle, long cmd, u_long* argp)` forwards to `ioctlsocket`.
- `int WINAPI xlive_XSocketSetSockOpt(SOCKET socket_handle, int level, int optname, const char* optval, int optlen)` forwards to `setsockopt`.
- `int WINAPI xlive_XSocketBind(SOCKET socket_handle, const sockaddr* name, int namelen)` forwards to `bind`.
- `int WINAPI xlive_XSocketRecvFrom(SOCKET socket_handle, char* buffer, int len, int flags, sockaddr* from, int* fromlen)` forwards to `recvfrom`.
- `int WINAPI xlive_XSocketSendTo(SOCKET socket_handle, const char* buffer, int len, int flags, const sockaddr* to, int tolen)` forwards to `sendto`.
- `unsigned long WINAPI xlive_XSocketInet_Addr(const char* cp)` forwards to `inet_addr`.
- `int WINAPI xlive_XWSAGetLastError()` returns `WSAGetLastError`.
- `unsigned short WINAPI xlive_XSocketHTONS(unsigned short hostshort)` forwards to `htons`.

## Exported networking and notification stubs

- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetStartup(void*)` returns `ERROR_SUCCESS`.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetXnAddrToInAddr(const void*, const void*, IN_ADDR* in_addr)` writes loopback `INADDR_LOOPBACK` when `in_addr` is non-null.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetInAddrToXnAddr(IN_ADDR in_addr, void* xn_addr, void*)` copies at most 36 bytes into `xn_addr`.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetConnect(const void*)` returns success.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetGetConnectStatus(const void*)` returns `1`.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetQosListen(const void*, const void*, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD)` returns success.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetQosLookup(DWORD, const void*, const void*, const void*, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, void**)` returns success without allocating results.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetQosServiceLookup(DWORD, DWORD, void**)` returns success without allocating results.
- `void WINAPI xlive_XNetQosRelease(void*)` performs no action.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetGetTitleXnAddr(void* addr)` zeroes 36 bytes when `addr` is non-null.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetGetEthernetLinkStatus()` returns `1`.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNetSetSystemLinkPort(WORD)` returns success.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNotifyGetNext(HANDLE, DWORD, DWORD*, ULONG_PTR*)` returns `0`, indicating no notification.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XNotifyPositionUI(DWORD)` returns success.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XGetOverlappedExtendedError(xoverlapped* overlapped)` returns `extended_error`, or success for null.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XGetOverlappedResult(xoverlapped* overlapped, DWORD* result, BOOL wait)` optionally waits on `event`, writes `internal_high` to `result`, and returns `extended_error`.
- `HANDLE WINAPI xlive_XNotifyCreateListener(ULONGLONG, DWORD)` creates an auto-reset, initially nonsignaled event.

## Exported rendering, protected-data, and UI stubs

- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XLiveInput(void*)`, `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XLiveRender()`, `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XLiveOnCreateDevice(void*, void*)`, `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XLiveOnDestroyDevice()`, and `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XLiveOnResetDevice(void*)` return success.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XHVCreateEngine(void*, void*, void*)` returns success without creating an engine.
- `BOOL WINAPI xlive_XLivePreTranslateMessage(const MSG*)` always returns `FALSE`.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XLiveCreateProtectedDataContext(void*, HANDLE* handle)` writes sentinel handle `reinterpret_cast<HANDLE>(1)` when `handle` is non-null.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XLiveQueryProtectedDataInformation(HANDLE, void*)` and `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XLiveCloseProtectedDataContext(HANDLE)` return success.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XShowGuideUI(DWORD)`, `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XShowGamerCardUI(DWORD, XUID, DWORD)`, `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XShowSigninUI(DWORD, DWORD)`, and `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XShowFriendsUI(DWORD)` return success.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XCancelOverlapped(xoverlapped* overlapped)` completes `overlapped` successfully and returns success.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XEnumerate(HANDLE, void*, DWORD, DWORD* returned, xoverlapped* overlapped)` writes zero to `returned`, completes successfully, and returns `ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES`.

## Exported user, stats, and profile APIs

- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserGetXUID(DWORD user_index, XUID* xuid)` accepts only user index `0` and non-null `xuid`, then returns `offline_xuid()`.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserGetSigninState(DWORD user_index)` returns `signed_in_to_live` for user `0`, otherwise `0`.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserGetName(DWORD user_index, char* user_name, DWORD user_name_chars)` validates index, buffer, and nonzero capacity, then truncating-copies `offline_name()`.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserAreUsersFriends(DWORD, const XUID*, DWORD, void*, xoverlapped* overlapped)` completes with `ERROR_NOT_FOUND`.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserCheckPrivilege(DWORD, DWORD, BOOL* allowed)` writes `TRUE` when `allowed` is non-null and returns success.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserGetSigninInfo(DWORD user_index, DWORD, xuser_signin_info* info)` validates user `0`, zeroes `info`, and fills XUID, flags, sign-in state, and truncated name.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserSetProperty(DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, const void*)` and `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserSetContext(DWORD, DWORD, DWORD)` return success without storing state.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserWriteAchievements(DWORD, void*, xoverlapped* overlapped)` completes successfully.
- `DWORD WINAPI xlive_XUserReadStats(DWORD, XUID*, DWORD, DWORD, void*, DWORD, void*, xoverlapped* overlapped)` completes with `ERROR_NOT_FOUND`.
- `HANDLE WINAPI xlive_XUserCreateStatsEnumeratorByRank(DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD*)` sets last error to `ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES` and returns `INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE`.
- `HANDLE WINAPI xlive_XUserCreateStatsEnumeratorByXuid(XUID, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD, DWORD*)` has the same empty-enumerator behavior.

# aim

`gamepad::unstable::controller::aim` groups deterministic gamepad aiming primitives, including `aim_processor`, `aim_calibration`, `aim_graph`, `turn_integrator`, `low_pass`, deadzone transforms, response curves, and dimension-safe aim types.

## Contents

### Processing

- [assist.cpp](./assist.cpp) implements `aim_processor::process`, `slowdown_scale`, `scale_dominant_axis`, and `lock_on`.
- [assist.hpp](./assist.hpp) declares `aim_processor`, `aim_frame_input`, `aim_frame_output`, `aim_profile`, `lock_on_target`, and `lock_on_params`.
- [integrator.cpp](./integrator.cpp) implements `turn_integrator::advance`.
- [integrator.hpp](./integrator.hpp) declares acceleration/deceleration limits, `advance`, `current`, and `reset`.
- [filter.cpp](./filter.cpp) implements frame-time-independent `low_pass` smoothing.
- [filter.hpp](./filter.hpp) declares `low_pass`, `apply`, `reset`, and `value`.

### Calibration and shaping

- [calibration.cpp](./calibration.cpp) implements `fov_scale`, validated `aim_calibration::make`, and `processor_config`.
- [calibration.hpp](./calibration.hpp) declares `aim_settings`, `aim_calibration`, and FOV-aware calibration ownership.
- [curve.cpp](./curve.cpp) implements `to_string`, `validate`, and `evaluate` for response curves.
- [curve.hpp](./curve.hpp) declares `curve_kind` and `response_curve`.
- [deadzone.cpp](./deadzone.cpp) implements radial `validate` and `apply` for stick deadzones.
- [deadzone.hpp](./deadzone.hpp) declares `deadzone_params`, deadzone validation, and radial transformation.
- [graph.cpp](./graph.cpp) implements validated piecewise-linear `aim_graph::make` and `aim_graph::evaluate`.
- [graph.hpp](./graph.hpp) declares `knot`, `max_graph_knots`, and allocation-free `aim_graph`.

### Domain types

- [types.cpp](./types.cpp) implements stream formatting for `degrees` and `deg_per_s`.
- [types.hpp](./types.hpp) declares `degrees`, `radians`, `deg_per_s`, `deg_per_s2`, `axis_input`, `magnitude`, `screen_vector`, `world_vector`, `dot`, and unit conversions.

## Architecture / Data Flow

`aim_calibration::make` validates `aim_settings`, optionally constructs `aim_graph`, and returns `aim_calibration`; `aim_calibration::processor_config` supplies `aim_processor::config`.

`aim_processor::process` clamps `ads_lerp`, interpolates `aim_profile` values, applies `deadzone_params`, evaluates `response_curve` or `aim_graph`, scales by FOV/sensitivity/slowdown, advances `turn_integrator`, enforces optional limits, and applies pitch inversion.

`low_pass` smooths scalar input independently of frame rate, while `lock_on` converts projected relative velocity into yaw and pitch corrections.

## Behavioral Contracts

- `curve::validate` requires power `exponent` to be finite and greater than `0.0f`; `curve::evaluate` clamps input to `[0.0f, 1.0f]`.
- `deadzone::validate` requires `inner.value`, `outer.value`, and `anti.value` in `[0, 1)`, plus `inner.value < 1.0f - outer.value`.
- `aim_graph::make` accepts 2–`max_graph_knots` knots, with `max_graph_knots == 16`, finite values, inputs in `[0, 1]`, and strictly increasing inputs.
- `aim_processor::process` uses `cfg_.ads.curve` when `t >= 0.5f`, integrates non-negative target speeds before restoring signs, and negates final pitch when `invert_pitch` is true.
- `slowdown_scale` returns `1.0f` without a target and otherwise interpolates hip/ADS scales using clamped `ads_lerp`.
- `scale_dominant_axis` preserves the dominant stick axis and attenuates the subordinate axis by the absolute-magnitude difference.
- `lock_on` returns `{}` when `target.distance <= 0.0f`; otherwise it uses `arc = target.distance * pi`.
- `low_pass::apply` bypasses smoothing when `tau_ <= 0`, adopts the first target exactly, and otherwise uses `alpha = clamp(1 - exp(-dt/tau), 0, 1)`.
- `turn_integrator::advance` returns `degrees{0.0f}` for `dt <= 0` and integrates rate with `0.5f * (prev + cur) * dt`.
- `fov_scale` returns `1.0f` when the reference tangent is non-positive or `f` is non-finite.
- `aim_calibration::make` emits `"hip deadzone: "`, `"ADS deadzone: "`, `"hip curve: "`, `"ADS curve: "`, and `"aim graph: "` diagnostics.

## File Relationships

`assist.cpp` consumes `deadzone.cpp`, `curve.cpp`, `graph.cpp`, and `integrator.cpp` through `assist.hpp`, while `calibration.cpp` assembles `curve`, `deadzone`, and `graph` validation into `aim_processor::config`.

`types.hpp` supplies unit-safe values for `assist.hpp`, `calibration.hpp`, `filter.hpp`, and `integrator.hpp`; `clock.hpp`, `support/types.hpp`, `support/utility.hpp`, and `sample/axis.hpp` supply shared timing and controller primitives.

`aim_calibration::graph_` must outlive processors created from `processor_config()`, and `lock_on_target::view_yaw_axis` must use RIGHT (`+yaw`) coordinates.

`device_notifier`, `hid_device`, `windows_hid_device`, and `xinput_module` form the Windows controller-transport layer for HID discovery, asynchronous reports, device-change notifications, and dynamically loaded XInput APIs.

## Contents

### HID transport

- [hid.hpp](./hid.hpp) defines `hid_device`, `hid_enumeration_entry`, `hid_attributes`, `classify_link`, `enumerate`, and `open`.
- [hid.cpp](./hid.cpp) implements `windows_hid_device`, HID enumeration, capability validation, overlapped I/O, feature reports, and read-only fallback.

### Device notification

- [device-notify.hpp](./device-notify.hpp) defines non-copyable `device_notifier`, `consume`, `run`, `pending_`, and `window_`.
- [device-notify.cpp](./device-notify.cpp) implements the `WM_DEVICECHANGE` message-only window, HID registration, worker-thread message pumping, and polling fallback.

### XInput transport

- [xinput-module.hpp](./xinput-module.hpp) defines non-copyable `xinput_module`, runtime status queries, and safe forwarding for `get_state`, `get_capabilities`, and `set_state`.
- [xinput-module.cpp](./xinput-module.cpp) implements ordered XInput DLL probing, function-pointer resolution, guide-button detection, reporting, and teardown.

## Architecture / Data Flow

`enumerate` discovers present HID interfaces, `classify_link` validates report framing, and `open` creates a `windows_hid_device` after re-querying `HidD_GetAttributes` and `query_caps`.

`device_notifier::run` converts `WM_DEVICECHANGE` events into the atomic `pending_` flag, while `device_notifier::consume` lets discovery reconcile devices or use polling.

`windows_hid_device::issue_read` starts overlapped `ReadFile` operations, `windows_hid_device::read` consumes completed reports, and `windows_hid_device::write`, `get_feature`, and `set_feature` submit output or feature transfers.

`xinput_module::load` probes `variants`, resolves mandatory entry points, optionally resolves ordinal `100`, and forwards controller calls through `get_state_`, `get_state_ex_`, `get_capabilities_`, and `set_state_`.

## API Surface

`hid_device::read` returns `optional<size_t>`, with `size_t(0)` for an in-flight read and `nullopt` for invalid or failed transport state.

`hid_device::write` and `hid_device::set_feature` require writable access, while `hid_device::get_feature` remains available when `feature_report_length()` is satisfied.

`classify_link` maps `64` to `connection::usb`, `78` to `connection::bluetooth`, and all other lengths to `connection::unknown`.

`xinput_module::loaded`, `xinput_module::dll_name`, and `xinput_module::has_guide_button` expose runtime-loading state without exposing `HMODULE` ownership.

## Behavioral Contracts

- `max_report_size` equals `128`, bounding `windows_hid_device::buf_`, `input_length_`, and `feature_length_`.
- `usb_input_report_length` equals `64`; `bluetooth_input_report_length` equals `78`.
- `window_class` equals `L"gamepad_controller_devnotify"`.
- `device_notifier::window_proc` handles `WM_DEVICECHANGE`, `WM_CLOSE`, and `WM_DESTROY`.
- `DBT_DEVICEARRIVAL` and `DBT_DEVICEREMOVECOMPLETE` set `pending_` with `std::memory_order_release`.

- `variants` probes `"xinput1_4.dll"`, `"xinput1_3.dll"`, and `"xinput9_1_0.dll"` in that order.
- `get_state_ex_` resolves ordinal `100`; missing `get_state_ex_` disables guide-button decoding without rejecting the DLL.
- `ERROR_DEVICE_NOT_CONNECTED` is returned by unavailable `get_state`, `get_capabilities`, and `set_state` entry points.

## Failure Contracts

`device_notifier::run` reports `"device-change window class registration failed; discovery will poll"`, `"device-change window creation failed; discovery will poll"`, and `"HID device-change registration failed; discovery will poll"` through `ctx.report`.

`open` reports `"unable to open a HID device interface"`, `"opened HID device does not answer its capabilities"`, and `"opened HID device is not a controller we can decode"` for activation failures.

`xinput_module::load` reports `"no XInput runtime could be loaded; XInput controllers will not be available"` when all `variants` fail.

`hid.cpp` implements the abstract `hid_device` contract from `hid.hpp`, while `types.hpp`, `utility.hpp`, `context.hpp`, `id.hpp`, and `identity.hpp` supply transport-facing types.

`device-notify.cpp` implements lifecycle and Windows callbacks declared by `device-notify.hpp`, with `pending_` connecting the notifier thread to discovery polling.

`xinput-module.cpp` implements the ABI and ownership contract declared by `xinput-module.hpp`, with `context`, `severity`, `facility`, and `errc` controlling diagnostics.

`connection::usb` and `connection::bluetooth` describe report framing and layout; `classify_link` does not guarantee the physical bus.

## Report Framing

- `resolve_frame(span<const byte> r, connection link, size_t& common) noexcept -> bool` accepts USB reports only when `r.size() >= ds_size_usb`, `rd_u8(r, 0) == ds_report_usb`, with `ds_report_usb = 0x01`, `ds_size_usb = 64`, and `ds_common_usb = 1`.
- `resolve_frame` accepts Bluetooth reports only when `r.size() >= ds_size_bt`, `rd_u8(r, 0) == ds_report_bt`, and `verify_ps_crc32(ps_input_crc_seed, r.first(ds_size_bt - 4), rd_le32(r, ds_size_bt - 4))` succeeds, with `ds_report_bt = 0x31`, `ds_size_bt = 78`, and `ds_common_bt = 2`.
- `connection` values other than `connection::usb` and `connection::bluetooth` cause `resolve_frame` and `decode_dualsense` to return `false`.
- `read_and_decode` allocates `array<byte, ds_size_bt>` and treats zero-length or failed `hid_.read()` results as poll termination.

## Input Mapping

- `decode_dualsense` reads sticks at `b + 0..3`, assigns `raw.sticks`, and fills `canonical.sticks` with raw coordinates plus `normalize_ps_stick()` values.
- `decode_dualsense` reads analog L2/R2 values at `b + 4` and `b + 5`, stores `raw.triggers`, and normalizes canonical trigger values as `value / 255.0f`.
- `decode_dualsense` reads button bytes at `b + 7..10`; `b0` maps face buttons and hat input, `b1` maps `l1`, `r1`, `l2`, `r2`, `back`, `start`, `l3`, and `r3`, and `b2` maps `guide`, `touchpad`, and `mute`.
- `decode_dualsense` invokes `apply_hat(btns, static_cast<uint8_t>(b0 & 0x0Fu))`, maps face bits `0x10`, `0x20`, `0x40`, `0x80` to west/south/east/north, and preserves packed `b0..b3` in `raw.buttons`.
- `decode_dualsense` maps Edge-only `b2` bits `0x10`, `0x20`, `0x40`, `0x80` to `edge_fn_left`, `edge_fn_right`, `edge_paddle_left`, and `edge_paddle_right` only when `edge == true`.
- `decode_dualsense` reads signed little-endian gyro values at `b + 15`, `b + 17`, `b + 19`, acceleration values at `b + 21`, `b + 23`, `b + 25`, and a 32-bit device timestamp at `b + 27`.
- `decode_dualsense` decodes two four-byte touch contacts at `b + 32` and `b + 36` through `decode_touch_point`, assigning `canonical.touch` and `raw.touch`.
- `decode_dualsense` interprets battery `st0 = rd_u8(r, b + 52)`, with `capacity = st0 & 0x0F` and `charging = (st0 >> 4) & 0x0F`; charging codes `0x0` and `0x1` yield discharging/charging with `min(capacity * 10 + 5, 100)`, `0x2` yields full/100%, and other codes yield unknown status without usable capacity.
- `decode_dualsense` resets `canonical.motion` because calibrated physical-unit motion is assigned by a later calibration stage.

## Capabilities and Output

- `decode_dualsense` assigns `capabilities` for `gyroscope`, `accelerometer`, `touchpad`, `battery`, `rumble`, `haptics`, `adaptive_triggers`, `light_bar`, `player_leds`, and `microphone_button`; `edge == true` additionally adds `back_buttons`.
- `dualsense_driver::submit` uses `array<byte, ds_output_bt_size>` and `bt_output_sequence_` with `encode_dualsense_output(request, link_, bt_output_sequence_, buf)`.
- `dualsense_driver::submit` reports `errc::output_rejected` with `"DualSense driver ignores an output request it cannot encode (adaptive triggers are not yet enabled)"` when encoding returns `nullopt`.
- `dualsense_driver::submit` reports `errc::output_rejected` with `"DualSense output report write failed"` when `hid_.write()` fails.
- `encode_dualsense_output` supports verified-layout rumble, light-bar, and player-LED output while rejecting adaptive-trigger effects.

## Diagnostics and Dependencies

- `read_and_decode` drops malformed reports and reports `severity::warning`, `facility::decode`, `errc::report_malformed`, and `"DualSense report failed framing or CRC validation and was dropped"`.
- `read_and_decode` recognizes `minimal_bluetooth_report(r, link_)`, logs `severity::info`, `facility::decode`, `errc::none`, and `"DualSense is still sending minimal Bluetooth reports and produces no input; the controller did not switch to its extended report"` once via `minimal_reported_`.
- `decode_dualsense` depends on `decode.hpp` for `rd_u8`, `rd_le16s`, `rd_le32`, `normalize_ps_stick`, `decode_touch_point`, `apply_hat`, and `minimal_bluetooth_report`.
- `resolve_frame` depends on `playstation.hpp` for `connection`, `ps_input_crc_seed`, and `verify_ps_crc32`; `submit` depends on `output-report.hpp` for `output_request`, `ds_output_bt_size`, and `encode_dualsense_output`.

`decode_dualsense` selects report framing from `connection`; Bluetooth CRC-32 is checked before field access. `edge` decodes rear-button bits `buttons[2]` bits `4..7` and records back-button capability; standard DualSense leaves those bits uninterpreted.

**Purpose:** dualshock4.cpp decodes DualShock 4 HID input reports and submits USB/Bluetooth output reports.

**dualshock4.cpp decodes DualShock 4 HID input reports and submits USB/Bluetooth output reports.**

## Public Interface

## Report Framing

`resolve_frame(span<const byte> r, connection link, size_t& common, size_t& max_touch) noexcept` rejects unknown `connection` values, short reports, incorrect report IDs, and invalid Bluetooth CRC-32 values before decoding.

- `ds4_report_usb = 0x01`, `ds4_size_usb = 64`, `ds4_common_usb = 1`, and `ds4_max_touch_usb = 3` define USB framing.
- `ds4_report_bt = 0x11`, `ds4_size_bt = 78`, `ds4_common_bt = 3`, and `ds4_max_touch_bt = 4` define Bluetooth framing.
- Bluetooth `resolve_frame` reads the little-endian CRC at `ds4_size_bt - 4` and verifies `verify_ps_crc32(ps_input_crc_seed, r.first(ds4_size_bt - 4), crc)`.
- `array<byte, ds4_size_bt> buf` accommodates the largest input report; Bluetooth reports include a trailing four-byte CRC.

## Input Mapping

`decode_dualshock4` interprets the common block relative to `b`:

- `b + 0..3` contains `lx`, `ly`, `rx`, and `ry`; `normalize_ps_stick` converts both raw stick pairs into canonical normalized values while `raw.sticks` preserves device bytes.
- `b + 4` contains the four face-button bits (`0x10`, `0x20`, `0x40`, `0x80`) and the low-nibble hat value; `apply_hat` maps the hat to canonical directional buttons.
- `b + 5` maps bits `0x01..0x80` to `button::l1`, `button::r1`, `button::l2`, `button::r2`, `button::back`, `button::start`, `button::l3`, and `button::r3`.
- `b + 6` maps `0x01` to `button::guide`/PS and `0x02` to `button::touchpad`; the complete three-byte button state is preserved in `raw.buttons` as `b0 | (b1 << 8) | (b2 << 16)`.
- `b + 7` and `b + 8` populate left/right `trigger_side` values, with canonical trigger magnitudes normalized by division through `255.0f`.
- `b + 9` supplies `motion.device_timestamp`; signed little-endian values at `b + 12`, `b + 14`, `b + 16` populate `motion.gyro.angular_velocity`, while `b + 18`, `b + 20`, `b + 22` populate `motion.accel.acceleration`.
- `raw.motion` retains raw device counts; `canonical.motion.reset()` delegates physical-unit conversion to the calibration stage and device calibration feature report.
- `b + 29` supplies battery `cap = st0 & 0x0F` and cable state `st0 & 0x10`; `ds4_battery_full = 11` plus cable attachment yields `battery_state::status::full` and `100`, otherwise `cap * 10` is clamped to `100` with charging/discharging status.
- `b + 32` supplies `num_touch`; values `1..max_touch` decode points from `b + 34` and `b + 38` through `decode_touch_point(r.subspan(off, 4))`, while other values clear `canonical.touch`.
- `canonical.caps` always advertises `capability::gyroscope | capability::accelerometer | capability::touchpad | capability::battery | capability::rumble | capability::light_bar`.

## Polling and Error Contracts

`dualshock4_driver::poll` treats valid reports as newest-state updates, bounded by `max_reports_per_poll`; zero-length or unavailable `hid_.read` results terminate draining.

`minimal_bluetooth_report(r, link_)` identifies non-malformed minimal Bluetooth reports, which are discarded because they lack extended motion/touch data; `minimal_reported_` suppresses repeated informational diagnostics.

`ctx_.report` emits `facility::decode` with `errc::none` for the first minimal-report notice and `errc::report_malformed` with `"DualShock 4 report failed framing or CRC validation and was dropped"` for rejected reports.

## Output and Integration

`dualshock4_driver::submit` allocates `array<byte, ds4_output_bt_size> buf` and calls `encode_dualshock4_output(request, link_, buf)`; absent length produces `facility::driver`, `errc::output_rejected`, and `"DualShock 4 driver ignores an output request it cannot encode for this connection"`.

`hid_.write(span<const byte>(buf.data(), *n))` sends encoded output; write failure reports `facility::driver`, `errc::output_rejected`, and `"DualShock 4 output report write failed"`.

`decode.hpp` supplies `rd_u8`, `rd_le16`, `rd_le16s`, `rd_le32`, and `decode_touch_point`; `output-report.hpp` supplies `ds4_output_bt_size` and `encode_dualshock4_output`; `playstation.hpp` supplies `normalize_ps_stick`, `verify_ps_crc32`, and `ps_input_crc_seed`; `std_include.hpp` supplies project aliases such as `span`, `array`, `optional`, `byte`, and `uint8_t`.

**Purpose:** output-report.cpp encodes DualShock 4 and DualSense rumble/LED requests into USB or Bluetooth HID output reports.

**output-report.cpp encodes DualShock 4 and DualSense rumble/LED requests into USB or Bluetooth HID output reports.**

## Public Interface

- `optional<size_t> encode_dualshock4_output(const output_request& r, connection link, span<byte> out) noexcept` validates `link` and buffer capacity, emits USB (`0x05`) or Bluetooth (`0x11`) framing, encodes `rumble_request` or `light_bar_request`, seals Bluetooth reports with CRC-32, and returns encoded size or `nullopt`.
- `optional<size_t> encode_dualsense_output(const output_request& r, connection link, uint8_t& bt_sequence, span<byte> out) noexcept` validates framing inputs, encodes `rumble_request`, `light_bar_request`, or `player_led_request`, advances the Bluetooth sequence nibble, seals Bluetooth reports, and returns encoded size or `nullopt`.

## Encoding Contracts

- `encode_dualshock4_output` selects `ds4_output_usb_size`/`ds4_output_bt_size`, uses common-field bases `1`/`3`, and zero-fills the complete report before writing fields.
- `encode_dualshock4_output` maps `rumble_request.high_frequency` to `motor_right` at `base + 3`, `rumble_request.low_frequency` to `motor_left` at `base + 4`, and `light_bar_request.{red,green,blue}` to `base + 5..7`.
- `encode_dualsense_output` selects `ds_output_usb_size`/`ds_output_bt_size`, uses bases `1`/`3`, and zero-fills output before encoding.
- `encode_dualsense_output` maps rumble to `base + 2/+3`, light-bar RGB to `base + 44..46`, and `player_led_request.mask & 0x1F` to `base + 43`.
- `to_byte(float v) noexcept` clamps normalized magnitudes to `[0,1]` and rounds `v * 255.0f` via `+ 0.5f`; `put(span<byte>, size_t, uint8_t)` asserts bounds before byte assignment.
- `encode_dualshock4_output` rejects non-`usb`/non-`bluetooth` links, undersized buffers, `player_led_request`, and adaptive-trigger variants.
- `encode_dualsense_output` rejects non-`usb`/non-`bluetooth` links, undersized buffers, and unsupported adaptive-trigger variants.

## Bluetooth Integrity and State

- `seal_bt_crc(span<byte> b) noexcept` computes CRC-32 over the report prefix using `ps_output_crc_seed` (`0xA2`), initializes with `0xFFFFFFFFu`, complements the result, and writes little-endian CRC bytes into the final four positions.
- `encode_dualshock4_output` writes Bluetooth report ID `0x11`, hardware-control flags `ds4_hwctl_hid | ds4_hwctl_crc32` (`0x80 | 0x40`).
- `encode_dualsense_output` writes Bluetooth report ID `0x31`, stores `(bt_sequence & 0x0F) << 4` in byte `1`, writes `ds_output_tag` (`0x10`) in byte `2`, then updates `bt_sequence = (bt_sequence + 1) & 0x0F`.
- `ds4_flag0_motor` (`0x01`), `ds4_flag0_led` (`0x02`), `ds_flag0_compatible_vibration` (`0x01`), `ds_flag0_haptics_select` (`0x02`), `ds_flag1_lightbar_enable` (`0x04`), and `ds_flag1_player_leds_enable` (`0x10`) control device interpretation.

## Dependencies and Design

- `output_request`, `rumble_request`, `light_bar_request`, `player_led_request`, `connection`, `byte`, `span`, `optional`, `crc32_le`, and report-size constants come from `output-report.hpp`/`decode.hpp` and shared project headers.
- `std::variant` visitation through `std::get_if` implements a type-dispatch strategy; `std::clamp`, `std::fill_n`, and `assert` enforce normalization, deterministic zeroed layouts, and programmer-error bounds checks.
- `noexcept` encoders return `nullopt` for validation or capability failures; unsupported layouts are intentionally not guessed.

## Interface

- `set::set (const context& ctx, const transport::xinput_module& x)` stores non-owning `ctx_` and `xinput_` references.

- `void set::reconcile (const registry& r)` synchronizes active `entries_` with registry membership.

- `set::bind` maps `family::xbox` to `xinput_driver`, requiring `std::get_if<xinput_binding>(&d.binding)` and passing `ctx_`, `xinput_`, `d.id`, and `b->index`.

- `set::bind` requires non-null `hid` for PlayStation families and asserts `hid->link() == connection::usb || hid->link() == connection::bluetooth`.

- `set::reconcile` caches `registry::generation()` in `generation_` and skips work when `reconciled_ && g == generation_`.
- `set::reconcile` snapshots `registry` via `r.for_each` before slow HID operations or lock reacquisition.
- `std::erase_if(entries_)` retires entries whose `device.id` is absent; `entry` owns the borrowed `hid` lifetime alongside `drv`.
- `transport::open (ctx_, b->path)` opens `hid_binding` paths; null handles skip binding after transport-side error reporting.
- `set::reconcile` reports `errc::none` for release/bind events and `errc::unsupported_device` with `severity::warning` when `bind` returns null.

- `set.cpp` includes `set.hpp`, `xinput.hpp`, `dualshock4.hpp`, `dualsense.hpp`, `dualsense-edge.hpp`, and `playstation.hpp`.

**set.hpp manages live gamepad drivers and their HID/XInput resources.**

## Interface

- `set(const context&, const transport::xinput_module&)` initializes non-owning runtime dependencies; `~set()` destroys bound entries.
- `set` is non-copyable via deleted `set(const set&)` and `operator=(const set&)`.

- `for_each(function_ref<void(driver&, const device_connection&)>) -> void` visits each bound driver/device pair.

## Design

`entry` stores `device_connection device`, optional `unique_ptr<transport::hid_device> hid`, and `unique_ptr<driver> drv`; `drv` may reference `hid`, requiring destruction order `drv` then `hid` and prohibiting entry copying. `bind(const device_connection&, unique_ptr<transport::hid_device>&) -> unique_ptr<driver>` selects family-specific drivers: Xbox-class uses XInput, PlayStation families use dedicated drivers, and unknown/unlinked devices remain unbound without fallback decoding.

## Role and Integration

`gamepad::unstable::controller::engine::key_dispatcher` consumes `canonical_sample`, applies stick deadzones, tracks button/axis transitions, and emits engine key events through `emit_key`. - `void key_dispatcher::dispatch_buttons (const canonical_sample& sample, unsigned time) noexcept` compares current buttons against `buttons_`, emitting transitions and held repeats for D-pad and triggers.

- `void key_dispatcher::reset_scroll (engine_key key, bool down, unsigned time) noexcept` initializes or clears scroll-hold tracking and schedules the first repeat.
- `void key_dispatcher::menu_key_event (engine_key key, bool down)` translates `engine_key` to menu keycodes using the current millisecond timestamp.
- `bool key_dispatcher::scoreboard_key_event (engine_key) noexcept` always returns `false`.

## Mapping and Fallback Contracts

`button_keys[]` maps `face_west→button_x`, `face_south→button_a`, `face_east→button_b`, `face_north→button_y`, `l2→button_ltrig`, `r2→button_rtrig`, `l1→button_lshldr`, `r1→button_rshldr`, `start→button_start`, `back→button_back`, `l3→button_lstick`, `r3→button_rstick`, and all four D-pad directions to matching `engine_key` values.

`menu_key` maps `button_a`/`button_start` to `K_ENTER`, `button_b`/`button_back` to `K_ESCAPE`, and D-pad/apad/rstick directions to `K_UPARROW`, `K_DOWNARROW`, `K_LEFTARROW`, or `K_RIGHTARROW`; unsupported keys return `0`.

`fallback_command` maps gameplay keys to `"+gostand"`, `"+stance"`, `"+usereload"`, `"weapnext"`, `"+speed_throw"`, `"+attack"`, `"+smoke"`, `"+frag"`, `"togglemenu"`, `"+scores"`, `"+breath_sprint"`, `"+melee"`, and D-pad `"+actionslot 1"` through `"+actionslot 4"`.

`engine_binding` reads the game binding table at `game::game_offset (0x11263624 + keynum * 12)` for key values `[0,255]`; invalid values return `nullptr`.

`queue_fallback` formats held commands as `"%s %d %u\n"` and released `+commands` as `"-%s %d %u\n"`; one-shot commands format as `"%s\n"` only on press, then call `game::Cbuf_AddText (0, text)`.

## Timing, Thresholds, and State

`scroll_delay_first`, `scroll_delay_rest`, `scroll_delay_min`, `scroll_accel_time`, and `controller_use_hold_time` equal `420`, `210`, `50`, `1500`, and `250` milliseconds respectively. `dispatch` reads default stick deadzone values `0.2f` and `0.01f`, button deadzone `0.13f`, pressed threshold `0.4f`, and hysteresis `0.1f`. `ignore_repeat` accelerates D-pad repeats linearly from `210` toward `50` over `1500` ms while preserving a first-repeat delay of `420` ms.

`dispatch` reports `"invalid stick deadzone; using defaults"` once per dispatcher via `reported_deadzone_`; `release_all` is the lifecycle reset boundary for buttons, axis hysteresis, and scroll state.

`dispatch(const canonical_sample&) noexcept` performs sample-to-sample edge detection, emits button and stick-direction events, updates controller ownership, and applies menu/scoreboard/UI/binding routing.

## Event and state model

`key_event` distinguishes `pressed`, `repeated`, and `released`; `repeated` drives held d-pad/menu scrolling while non-menu keys generally repeat only on their initial press.

`buttons_` stores the previous `button_set`; `deflected_` and `was_deflected_` track negative/positive stick states across `axis_count == 4` axes ordered right-x, right-y, left-x, left-y.

`dispatch_apad(unsigned time) noexcept` synthesizes `APAD_*` and `RSTICK_*` direction keys from latched deflection, including sticks already held when a menu opens.

`dispatch_buttons(const canonical_sample&, unsigned time) noexcept` converts canonical button state into engine keys; `emit_button(mapping::engine_key, key_event, unsigned time) noexcept` marks controller usage and refreshes menu scrolling before `emit(mapping::engine_key, key_event, unsigned time) noexcept` performs common event routing.

`ignore_repeat(mapping::engine_key, int repeats, unsigned time) noexcept` filters repeats; `reset_scroll(mapping::engine_key, bool down, unsigned time) noexcept` manages repeat timing; `menu_key_event(mapping::engine_key, bool down) noexcept` and `scoreboard_key_event(mapping::engine_key) noexcept` forward catcher-specific events.

`next_scroll_`, `scroll_hold_start_`, and `scroll_hold_key_` schedule accelerating held d-pad/trigger repeats in engine milliseconds.

## Runtime contracts

`apply_use_hold_time() noexcept` synchronizes `g_useholdtime` with controller ownership: combined `+usereload` reloads on tap and uses on hold only when hold time is positive, while the engine default `0` otherwise causes immediate use.

`use_hold_time_` is a lazily resolved `dvar_t*`; `reported_deadzone_` suppresses duplicate invalid-deadzone reports because stick deadzone dvars are validated on every read.

`set_in_use(bool) noexcept` maintains input-source transitions, and `dispatch(const canonical_sample&) noexcept` must receive every device sample; callers must invoke `release_all() noexcept` when the device disappears.

## Aim Processor Lifecycle

- `tuning_signature(const dvars& d)` hashes yaw/pitch turn rates, deadzones, acceleration, and `accel_enabled` using `result = result * 31u + std::hash<float>{}(value)`.
- `make_profile(const dvars& d, float yaw, float pitch)` creates linear `aim_profile` values with `deg_per_s` rates, `deadzone_params`, and `response_curve{curve_kind::linear, 1.0f}`.
- `ensure_processor()` uses hip defaults `260.0f/90.0f`, ADS defaults `90.0f/55.0f`, deadzone defaults `0.2f/0.01f`, acceleration default `1200.0f`, and disables acceleration when `accel_enabled` is false.
- `ensure_processor()` clamps `view_sensitivity` to `[0.01f, 30.0f]`, `sensitivity_level` to `[1, 10]`, and scales level by `/ 5.0f`.
- `ensure_processor()` deliberately clears `settings.graph_knots` and sets `settings.graph_monotonic = false` because QoS stores dvar pointers at `0x1149E108`; invalid calibration reports `severity::warning`, `facility::aim`, `errc::graph_invalid`, and `"aim configuration rejected (" + reason + ")"`.

## Movement and View Behavior

- `clamp_move(int value) noexcept` clamps command axes to `[-128, 127]`; `move_scale` is `127.0f`.
- `apply_move()` adds rounded `axes_.forward` and `axes_.side` contributions to `cmd.forwardmove` and `cmd.rightmove`, then exits when `view_active(client)` or `ensure_processor()` fails.
- `apply_move()` clamps `frame_time` to `[0.0f, 0.05f]`, optionally applies `scale_dominant_axis`, and constructs `aim_frame_input` with `adsLerp`, `sensitivity_scale`, `invert_pitch`, and `seconds{frame_time}`.
- `apply_move()` enables slowdown only when aim assist, initialized globals, `slowdown_enabled`, and `best_target()` all succeed; slowdown uses `slowdown_scale(true, 0.4f, 0.5f, globals.adsLerp)`.
- `best_target()` rejects `screenTargetCount` outside `[0, 64]`, requires finite positive `distSqr`, checks range `8192.0f * max(range_scale, 0.0f)`, and tests `clipMins`/`clipMaxs` with `in_region()`.
- `apply_move()` enables lock-on only when `lockon_enabled` is true and `hypot(look.x, look.y) <= lockon_deflection` (default `0.05f`); strengths default to yaw `0.6f` and pitch `0.0f`.
- `apply_move()` accepts only finite `lock_on()` corrections and processor deltas, subtracts deltas from `view_yaw()`/`view_pitch()`, and clamps pitch to `[-85.0f, 85.0f]`.

## Integration and Safety

- `view_driver` couples `context`, `dvars`, `canonical_sample`, `usercmd_s`, `aim_globals`, `AimAssistGlobals`, `aim_calibration`, `turn_integrator`, `mapping`, `slowdown_scale`, and `lock_on`.
- `reported_invalid_` suppresses repeated invalid-configuration warnings; `processor_` and `calibration_` are reset before failed rebuilds.
- `observe()` and `apply_move()` use finite-value guards; `apply_move()` is synchronous and `noexcept` at its command-processing boundary.

## Role

`view_driver` owns latched analog-stick state, persistent aim integration, stick-layout resolution, and controller contributions to `usercmd_s`; `observe()` and `idle()` cover frame sampling, while `apply_move()` and `apply_remote_move()` consume latched state later in command construction.

## Public interface

- `view_driver(const context&, const dvars&)` binds runtime `context` and tuning `dvars`.
- `void observe(const canonical_sample&) noexcept` maps the calibrated sample through `mapping::resolved_axes` and latches virtual movement/view axes.
- `void idle() noexcept` clears `axes_` and resets aim integrators when no controller drives the frame.
- `void apply_move(int client, usercmd_s& cmd, float frame_time) noexcept` adds movement to `forwardmove`/`rightmove`, advances view angles after native `CL_MouseMove`, and accounts for left-handed attack/throw mapping.
- `void apply_remote_move(int client, usercmd_s& cmd) noexcept` folds controller movement into remote-control commands.

## State and algorithms

`axes_` stores the most recent shaped stick vectors, decoupling runtime sampling from later command construction. `calibration_` owns the validated aim response graph referenced by `processor_`; both `optional` values remain empty until a successful build, with invalid tuning falling back to unshaped stick input. `tuning_signature_`, `have_signature_`, and `reported_invalid_` implement cached dvar-change detection and invalid-configuration reporting.

`ensure_processor()` rebuilds the aim processor when tuning changes and returns availability; `view_active(int client) const noexcept` gates view motion while menus, console/chat input, or player freeze are active.

## Integration and contracts

`view_driver` depends on `support/types.hpp`, `support/utility.hpp`, `engine/import.hpp`, `context.hpp`, `dvar.hpp`, `aim/assist.hpp`, `aim/calibration.hpp`, `mapping/stick-layout.hpp`, and `sample/sample.hpp`. `gpad_sticksConfig` selects left/right stick roles, while engine aim-assist globals apply slowdown and lock-on. `apply_move()` and `apply_remote_move()` are explicitly `noexcept`; `apply_move()` receives `frame_time` in seconds.
