# engine

`bind_bridge`, `key_dispatcher`, `view_driver`, `dvars`, and `install` form the IW4 gamepad engine boundary, translating controller samples into engine bindings, key events, movement, view angles, dvars, console commands, and hook callbacks.

## Contents

- [bind.cpp](./bind.cpp) — `bind_bridge` queues named controller layouts, applies `mapping::binding_table`, migrates legacy commands, and tracks `"custom"` manual layouts.
- [bind.hpp](./bind.hpp) — `bind_bridge` and `controller_command_for` define layout application, binding lookup, and controller-command migration contracts.
- [command.cpp](./command.cpp) — `register_commands` registers `controller_status`, `bindgpbuttonsconfigs`, and `bindgpsticksconfigs`.
- [command.hpp](./command.hpp) — `register_commands` declares fixed-order console-command registration through `runtime`.
- [dvar.cpp](./dvar.cpp) — `register_dvars` registers controller configuration dvars, while `publish_present` updates `gpad_present`.
- [dvar.hpp](./dvar.hpp) — `dvars`, `register_dvars`, `publish_present`, and typed `read` overloads define the engine dvar registry.
- [hook.cpp](./hook.cpp) — `install`, `controller_key_name`, `controller_key_from_name`, and `mouse_move_body` install key conversion and mouse-move detours.
- [hook.hpp](./hook.hpp) — `install(runtime&)` declares engine hook installation.
- [import.cpp](./import.cpp) — `Dvar_Register*`, `Dvar_Set*`, `emit_key`, `aim_globals`, `view_pitch`, `view_yaw`, and `frame_seconds` adapt engine calls and memory-backed state.
- [import.hpp](./import.hpp) — `dvar_t`, `usercmd_s`, dvar flags, key constants, `AimScreenTarget`, and `AimAssistGlobals` define the imported engine ABI.
- [key.cpp](./key.cpp) — `key_dispatcher` translates `canonical_sample` buttons and axes into engine events, menu input, fallback commands, and controller ownership.
- [key.hpp](./key.hpp) — `key_dispatcher` declares sample dispatch, repeat handling, ownership state, and `release_all`.
- [netmove.cpp](./netmove.cpp) — `move_changed`, `pack_move`, and `unpack_move` implement XOR-packed movement deltas.
- [netmove.hpp](./netmove.hpp) — `move_delta` and the movement codec define the pure network movement API.
- [view.cpp](./view.cpp) — `view_driver` shapes movement, rebuilds aim calibration, applies slowdown and lock-on, and mutates `usercmd_s`.
- [view.hpp](./view.hpp) — `view_driver` declares sampling, idle state, local movement, and remote movement integration.

## Architecture / Data Flow

`canonical_sample` enters `key_dispatcher::dispatch` and `view_driver::observe`; `key_dispatcher` emits `emit_key` transitions or `game::Cbuf_AddText` fallback commands, while `view_driver::apply_move` mutates `usercmd_s` after native mouse processing.

`register_dvars` creates `dvars`; `key_dispatcher`, `bind_bridge`, and `view_driver` consume those handles through `read`, `publish_present`, and engine registration helpers.

`install` connects `controller_key_name`, `controller_key_from_name`, `mouse_move_body`, `runtime::view`, and `patches::enforce_ads_sprint_interrupt` to engine callsites.

## Patterns

`dvars` uses a typed-handle registry with null-safe `read` overloads and change-filtered `publish_present`.

`key_dispatcher` uses edge detection through `buttons_`, axis hysteresis through `deflected_` and `was_deflected_`, and lifecycle cleanup through `release_all`.

`view_driver` uses `tuning_signature_`, `have_signature_`, `calibration_`, and `processor_` to cache aim processing and rebuild state only after dvar changes.

`bind_bridge` treats the engine bind table as authoritative and isolates engine keynum lookup inside `command_keys`.

## API Surface

`register_commands(const context&, runtime&)`, `register_dvars(const context&)`, `install(runtime&)`, `move_changed`, `pack_move`, `unpack_move`, `controller_command_for`, and the `bind_bridge`, `key_dispatcher`, and `view_driver` classes define the directory API.

`AimAssistGlobals` uses `#pragma pack(1)` with `screenTargets == 0xFC`, `screenTargetCount == 0xDFC`, and `sizeof == 0xE34`.

## Behavioral Contracts

`controller_command_for` maps `+activate` and `+reload` to `+usereload`, and `+melee_breath` to `+holdbreath`.

`custom_layout` equals `"custom"`; `apply_configured_layout` skips `"custom"`, while `note_manual_rebind` writes `"custom"` through `Dvar_SetString`.

`command_keys` initializes both output keys to `-1`, returns at most two matches, and restricts lookup to the active half of the 256-key space.

`queue_fallback` formats held commands as `"%s %d %u\n"`, released plus-commands as `"-%s %d %u\n"`, and one-shot commands as `"%s\n"`.

`pack_move` stores `forward` in the low byte and `right` in the high byte, XORs with `key`, and masks `0xFFFF`; `unpack_move` reverses the operation using `int8_t`.

`key_dispatcher` uses `scroll_delay_first == 420`, `scroll_delay_rest == 210`, `scroll_delay_min == 50`, `scroll_accel_time == 1500`, and `controller_use_hold_time == 250`.

`view_driver` clamps movement to `[-128, 127]`, frame time to `[0.0f, 0.05f]`, pitch to `[-85.0f, 85.0f]`, and target counts to `[0, 64]`.

`best_target` uses `8192.0f * max(range_scale, 0.0f)` as the aim-assist range bound and requires finite positive `distSqr`.

`frame_seconds` clamps `0x11255D70` milliseconds to `[0, 200]` before multiplying by `0.001f`.

## File Relationships

`bind.cpp` consumes `mapping::binding_table` and `apply_button_layout`; `key.cpp` consumes `mapping::engine_key`, `mapping::to_engine_key`, `mapping::axis_deflected`, and `mapping::all_engine_keys`.

`view.cpp` consumes `aim::validate`, `aim::apply`, `mapping::stick_layout_from_name`, `mapping::resolve`, `slowdown_scale`, and `lock_on`.

`import.cpp` exposes `game::game_offset(0x1149D290)`, `game::game_offset(0x11A9FEC0)`, and `game::game_offset(0x11A9FEC4)` for aim globals, pitch, and yaw.

`hook.cpp` patches `game::game_offset(0x102FFBFE)` and invokes native `CL_MouseMove` at `game::game_offset(0x102FC4D0)`.

`release_all` is the lifecycle boundary that clears `buttons_`, `deflected_`, `was_deflected_`, and scroll ownership after controller removal.

- `CL_ParseServerMessage_huffman_guard(int a1, std::uint32_t* a2) -> unsigned int` delegates null `a2` to the original detoured function, rejects `a2[5] < a2[7]`, and rejects compressed lengths above `k_huffman_max_compressed_bytes`.
- `CL_ParseServerMessage_huffman_guard(...)` reports underflow through `game::Com_Error(".\\cl_parse_mp.cpp", 1243, 1, "Huffman compressed msg cursor underflow detected\n")`.
- `CL_ParseServerMessage_huffman_guard(...)` reports oversized Huffman data through `"Huffman compressed msg exceeded safe decode limit (%u > %u)\n"` and returns `0` after either rejection.
- `UI_ReplaceDirective_guard(int ArgList, char* a2, int a3, unsigned __int8 a4) -> char*` bounds-checks both `ArgList` reinterpreted as `const char*` and `a2` with `bounded_length(..., k_ui_replace_directive_max_len + 1)`.
- `UI_ReplaceDirective_guard(...)` rejects inputs exceeding `0x100` bytes, logs `"UI_ReplaceDirective: rejected oversized directive input\n"`, returns `a2`, and otherwise invokes the original detour.
- `PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin_guard(char a1, std::uint32_t* a2, int a3, __int64 a4, int a5, std::uint32_t* a6) -> int` delegates null `a2` or `a6`, rejects `a6[5] < a6[7]`, and rejects unread messages above `0x4000` bytes.
- `PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin_guard(...)` logs malformed cursor input as `"PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin: rejected malformed message cursor\n"` and oversized input as `"PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin: rejected oversized message (%zu bytes)\n"`.
- `PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin_self_test() -> bool` constructs a cursor with `packet_cursor[5] = 0` and `packet_cursor[7] = 1`, verifies the guard returns `0`, and logs pass/fail.
- `UI_ReplaceDirective_self_test() -> bool` uses a `0x110`-byte non-NUL oversized input, `0xDEADBEEF`/`0xCAFEBABE` canaries, and a `0x110`-byte output to verify rejection, return-pointer preservation, canary integrity, and NUL termination.
- `register_security_guard_self_test() -> void` registers the `securityGuardSelfTest` console command, runs both self-tests, and prints `"securityGuardSelfTest: party=%s ui=%s\n"`.

## Dvar handling

- `dvar_enabled(const char* name) -> bool` converts boolean, integer, float, string, and enumeration dvars into enabled state; strings treat empty, `"0"`, case-insensitive `"false"`, and case-insensitive `"off"` as disabled.
- `dvar_int_value(const char* name, int fallback = 0) -> int` converts boolean, integer, float, string, and enumeration dvars to integers, returning `fallback` when absent or when a string value is null.
- `make_dvar_saved_and_writable(const char* name) -> void` clears `read_only`, `write_protected`, and `latched`, then sets `saved`.
- `make_dvar_debug_writable(const char* name) -> void` additionally clears `cheat_protected` before setting `saved`.
- `find_dvar(std::unordered_map<std::string, T>& map, const std::string& name) -> T*` implements map lookup for dvar override tables.
- `find_dvar(std::unordered_set<std::string>& set, const std::string& name) -> bool` implements membership lookup for dvar name sets.
- `Dvar_RegisterNew_Stub(const char* dvarName, game::DvarType type, unsigned short flags, char* desc, int unk, game::DvarValue value, game::DvarLimits domain) -> game::dvar_s*` intercepts registration and applies typed overrides from `dvars::overrides::register_bool_overrides`, `register_int_overrides`, `register_float_overrides`, and `register_string_overrides`.
- `Dvar_RegisterNew_Stub(...)` special-cases `DVAR_TYPE_FLOAT_2`/`"cg_debugInfoCornerOffset"` to zero both vector components and makes `DVAR_TYPE_ENUM`/`"cg_drawFPS"` saved and writable.
- `BG_GetPlayerJumpHeight_stub(int a1) -> float` returns `jump_height->current.value` when available and otherwise invokes `BG_GetPlayerJumpHeight_hook`.
- `BG_GetPlayerSpeed_stub(int a1) -> int` returns `g_speed->current.integer` when available and otherwise invokes `BG_GetPlayerSpeed_hook`.
- `r_lodScale_stub(float value) -> void` suppresses renderer reapplication when `r_lodScale->modified` is true and otherwise invokes `r_lodScale_hook`.
- `post_load()` forces `sv_cheats`, `vid_xpos`, and `vid_ypos` to saved/writable state during startup and every `250ms`; `DEBUG` builds additionally repair `r_fullbright` through `make_dvar_debug_writable`.

## Movement patches

- `Jump_GetLandFactor(DWORD* ps) -> float` returns `1.0` when `jump_slowdownEnable` is disabled, otherwise scales landing slowdown from `ps + 24` below `1700` and caps the factor at `2.5`.
- `Jump_Start_stub(int unused, int unused2, DWORD* pml_t) -> int` reads the engine `pmove_t` through inline x86 assembly, computes jump velocity from `jump_height` and gravity, applies `Jump_GetLandFactor`, resets movement timing/origin state, sets `groundEntityNum` to `1023`, and accumulates `jump_spreadAdd` into player state.
- `Jump_Start_stub(...)` clamps the spread accumulator at `255.0`, writes jump velocity using `sqrt(calculatedGravity)`, sets the movement flag `0x4000`, and returns the current `jump_spreadAdd` value.
- `Jump_Start_stub(...)` assumes valid engine pointers and dvars after hook installation; unlike the security guards, it does not null-check `jump_height`, `jump_slowdownEnable`, or `jump_spreadAdd`.

## Installed patches and lifecycle

- `post_load()` uses `utils::hook::set(game::game_offset(0x1047627C), create_window_ex_stub)` to intercept window creation.
- `post_load()` NOPs five-byte calls at `0x1000230F` and `0x102E1284` to suppress Scaleform and unknown UI-script `Com_Printf` diagnostics.
- `post_load()` NOPs five-byte instructions at `0x103F9E53`, `0x1027D3C4`, and `0x103BE16D` to preserve the registered version dvar, avoid an intentional debugger break, and prevent forced `r_fullscreen = 1`.
- `post_load()` creates detours at `0x101E6900` (`BG_GetPlayerJumpHeight_hook`), `0x101E6930` (`BG_GetPlayerSpeed_hook`), `0x10279010` (`r_lodScale_hook`), and `0x101DB390` (`Jump_Start_hook`).
- `post_load()` registers `sv_cheats = 1`, `version`, `shortversion`, `gamename = "Project: Consolation"`, and `gamedate` through `dvars::overrides`.
- `post_load()` installs `dvar_registernew_hook` on `game::Dvar_RegisterNew`, then schedules startup work on `scheduler::main` using `scheduler::once`.
- `scheduler::once` replaces engine dvars at fixed call sites with `dvars::make_float`, `dvars::make_int`, and `dvars::make_bool`: `r_lodScale`, `cg_fovScale`, `cg_fov`, `input_viewSensitivity`, `jump_height`, `developer`, `com_maxfps`, and `r_fullscreen`.
- `r_lodScale` defaults to `0.0f` with domain `[0.0f, 3.0f]`; `cg_fovScale` defaults to `1.0f` with `[0.0f, 2.0f]`; `cg_fov` defaults to `65.0f` with `[0.0f, 160.0f]`.
- `input_viewSensitivity` defaults to `1.0f` with `[0.01f, 30.0f]`; `jump_height` defaults to `41.0f` with `[0.0f, 1000.0f]`; `developer` defaults to `0` with `[0, 2]`; `com_maxfps` defaults to `85` with `[0, 1000]`.
- `r_fullscreen` defaults to `true` and uses `saved | latched`; all replacement dvars except `developer` use `saved`.
- `DEBUG` startup logic NOPs `0x101AB211` and `0x10245A2A`, registers `sv_cheats` through `dvars::Dvar_RegisterBool`, updates pointers at `0x11A343C0` and `0x1149FCD8`, and makes `r_fullbright` debug-writable.
- `post_load()` creates `cl_parse_server_message_huffman_hook` at `0x1030D960`, `ui_replace_directive_hook` at `0x102BB870`, and `party_atomic_host_handle_member_join_hook` at `0x103087B0`.
- `post_load()` registers `securityGuardSelfTest` after installing the three security detours, so the command must run only after component initialization.
- `game::game_offset(...)` encodes build-specific x86 engine addresses; changing target game versions requires revalidating every hard-coded offset and calling convention.

### profile_patches.cpp
**Purpose:** profile_patches.cpp does profile-config migration, decryption, deduplication, synchronization, and lifecycle integrat...

**profile_patches.cpp does profile-config migration, decryption, deduplication, synchronization, and lifecycle integration for Quantum of Solace multiplayer profiles.**

## Role and Integration

`profile_patches::component` implements `component_interface` and registers through `REGISTER_COMPONENT(profile_patches::component)`; `post_load()` installs commands, scheduler callbacks, and shutdown synchronization.

`game::game_offset`, `game::dvar_s`, and `game::Com_Printf` couple profile handling to engine memory, dvars, and console output; `utils::io::read_file`, `write_file`, and `file_exists` handle filesystem access; `SHGetFolderPathA` resolves `%APPDATA%`; `command::add` exposes console commands; `scheduler::once`, `scheduler::loop`, and `scheduler::on_shutdown` control lifecycle execution.

## Public Interface

`profile_patches::component::post_load() override` schedules initialization on `scheduler::main`, polls profile changes every `250ms`, and exports stock configuration back to the custom file during shutdown.

`REGISTER_COMPONENT(profile_patches::component)` makes `profile_patches::component` discoverable by the component loader.

## Paths, Dvars, and Constants

`default_profile_config_name` is `"config_mp.cfg"`; `custom_profile_config_name` is `"consolation_mp.cfg"`; `decrypted_profile_config_name` is `"consolation_mp_decrypted.cfg"`.

`get_dvar_string(std::size_t dvar_ptr_address)` reads a `game::dvar_s*` through `game::game_offset`; offsets `0x114E7068` and `0x10806824` represent the players-root dvar and profile-name dvar.

`get_players_directory()` prefers the configured players-root dvar, otherwise resolves `CSIDL_APPDATA` and appends `"Activision\\Quantum of Solace\\players"`; `get_profile_name()` returns the configured profile string or `""`.

`join_path(const std::string& base, const std::string& leaf)` preserves existing trailing `\\` or `/`, returns `leaf` for an empty base, and otherwise inserts `\\`.

`build_profile_file_path(const char* filename)` returns `<players-directory>\\<profile-name>\\<filename>` or `{}` when either directory or profile name is unavailable.

`build_profile_config_path()` targets `"config_mp.cfg"`; `build_custom_profile_config_path()` targets `"consolation_mp.cfg"`; `build_legacy_shared_config_path()` targets the custom filename directly under the players directory.

`build_runtime_config_path()` aliases the profile-scoped custom config; `build_decrypted_output_path()` targets the profile-scoped decrypted filename, falling back to the players directory when necessary.

## Config Recognition and Normalization

`looks_like_plaintext_config(const std::string& data)` rejects empty data and data with fewer than `85%` printable characters, then requires `"seta "`, `"set "`, or `"unbindall"`.

`to_lower(std::string value)` lowercases keys using unsigned-character-safe `std::tolower`; `trim_copy(const std::string& value)` removes leading and trailing spaces, tabs, carriage returns, and newlines.

`find_canonical_dvar_name(const std::string& key)` canonicalizes case-insensitive spellings for `con_outputHeightScale`, `cg_fovScale`, `input_viewSensitivity`, `ui_smallFont`, `ui_bigFont`, `ui_extraBigFont`, `r_lodScale`, `m_rawInput`, `bot_maxHealth`, `g_debugVelocity`, and `g_debugLocalization`.

`try_parse_dvar_assignment(std::string& line, std::string* key)` recognizes only lines beginning with exact prefixes `"seta "` or `"set "`, extracts and lowercases the dvar key, and rewrites recognized names to canonical casing.

`should_strip_runtime_only_dvar(const std::string& key)` removes `r_aspectratiocustom`, `r_aspectratiocustomenable`, `r_custommode`, and `r_ultrawidecustommode`.

`dedupe_config_text(const std::string& data)` preserves non-assignment lines, normalizes recognized assignments, removes runtime-only dvars, and retains only the last assignment for each lowercased key; output uses `"\r\n"` when input contains CRLF, otherwise `"\n"`.

`dedupe_custom_profile_config()` operates only when `should_use_custom_profile_config()` detects an existing plaintext-like custom config, rewriting it only when deduplication changes content.

## Decryption and Conversion

`decrypt_in_place(std::string& data)` invokes the engine `__stdcall` transform at `game::game_offset(0x103ECCA0)` with the mutable data pointer and `int` byte length.

`try_decode_config_to_plaintext(std::string& data)` accepts recognized plaintext unchanged, otherwise decrypts in place and validates with `looks_like_plaintext_config`.

`convert_config_to_path(const std::string& source_path, const std::string& fallback_path, const std::string& output_path, const char* command_name)` loads `source_path` first, falls back to `fallback_path`, decrypts non-plaintext input, validates the result, writes `output_path`, and emits diagnostic messages through `print_profile_message`; empty output paths, missing sources, invalid decrypted data, and write failures return `false`.

`migrate_config()` converts the profile-scoped stock config, or runtime custom config as fallback, into `consolation_mp_decrypted.cfg`.

`convert_config()` converts legacy shared custom config, or stock profile config as fallback, into the profile-scoped custom config.

`import_custom_profile_config_into_stock()` reads the profile-scoped custom config or legacy shared config, decodes and deduplicates plaintext, writes custom plaintext, re-encrypts a copy with `decrypt_in_place`, and writes encrypted stock config.

`export_stock_profile_config_to_custom()` reads and decodes stock config, deduplicates plaintext, and writes the custom profile config.

## Console Commands

`profile_decrypt_config` invokes `migrate_config()`.

`profile_convert_config` invokes `convert_config()`, `dedupe_custom_profile_config()`, `import_custom_profile_config_into_stock()`, and `print_runtime_config_path()`.

`profile_sync_config` invokes `import_custom_profile_config_into_stock()` and reports `^3profile:config synced %s into %s\n` or `^1profile:config failed to sync plaintext config into stock profile config\n`.

`profile_show_config_path` invokes `print_runtime_config_path()`.

`profile_dedupe_config` invokes `dedupe_custom_profile_config()` and then prints the runtime path.

`print_profile_message(const char* fmt, ...)` formats into a fixed `1024`-byte buffer via `vsnprintf` and sends channel `16` output through `game::Com_Printf`.

`print_runtime_config_path()` emits `^3profile:config runtime config path is unavailable\n` for unavailable paths or `^3profile:config %s\n` for resolved paths.

## Lifecycle Behavior

`post_load()` uses `scheduler::once(..., scheduler::main)` to register commands and perform initial deduplication.

`post_load()` uses `scheduler::loop(..., scheduler::main, 250ms)` with static `imported_profile` and `missing_profile` sentinels to avoid repeated work; profile changes trigger `import_custom_profile_config_into_stock()`, while missing sources suppress retries until the profile name changes.

`post_load()` uses `scheduler::on_shutdown(...)` to call `export_stock_profile_config_to_custom()` followed by `dedupe_custom_profile_config()`.

`post_load()` deliberately leaves the game’s active config filename and save path unchanged, so automatic engine-path patching remains disabled while signed-in startup-freeze behavior is investigated.
### xlive.cpp
**Purpose:** xlive.cpp disables debugger detection in `xlive.dll`, hooks anti-debugging NT APIs, and continuously clears process d...

**xlive.cpp disables debugger detection in `xlive.dll`, hooks anti-debugging NT APIs, and continuously clears process debug state.**

## Public Interface

- `void apply_early()` clears PEB debug flags, installs NTDLL detours, patches `xlive.dll`, and starts `peb_cleaner_thread`.
- `class component final : public component_interface` overrides `void post_load()` to repeat `clear_peb_debug_flags()` and `patch_xlive()` after component loading.
- `component::post_load()` is defined, but `REGISTER_COMPONENT(xlive::component)` remains disabled under `DEBUG`.

## Anti-Debugging Hooks

- `nt_query_information_process_stub(HANDLE, UINT, PVOID, ULONG, PULONG) -> LONG` spoofs `process_debug_port = 7u` as zero with `status_success = 0x00000000L`, spoofs `process_debug_object_handle = 0x1Eu` as null with `status_port_not_set = 0xC0000353L`, and reports `process_debug_flags = 0x1Fu` as `1`; other classes delegate through `nt_query_information_process_hook`.
- `nt_set_information_thread_stub(HANDLE, UINT, PVOID, ULONG) -> LONG` returns `status_success` for `thread_hide_from_debugger = 0x11u`, otherwise invokes `nt_set_information_thread_hook`.
- `nt_set_information_process_stub(HANDLE, UINT, PVOID, ULONG) -> LONG` accepts `process_debug_flags` changes without effect and delegates all other classes through `nt_set_information_process_hook`.
- `nt_query_system_information_stub(UINT, PVOID, ULONG, PULONG) -> LONG` delegates through `nt_query_system_information_hook`, then rewrites `system_kernel_debugger_information = 0x23u` output bytes to `KernelDebuggerEnabled = FALSE` and `KernelDebuggerNotPresent = TRUE` when `status_success` and `info_len >= 2`.
- `nt_get_context_thread_stub(HANDLE, PCONTEXT) -> LONG` delegates through `nt_get_context_thread_hook` and zeros `CONTEXT_DEBUG_REGISTERS` fields `Dr0`, `Dr1`, `Dr2`, `Dr3`, `Dr6`, and `Dr7` on successful queries.
- `nt_set_context_thread_stub(HANDLE, const CONTEXT*) -> LONG` copies debug-register contexts, zeros `Dr0`–`Dr3`, `Dr6`, and `Dr7`, then invokes `nt_set_context_thread_hook` with the sanitized copy.
- `nt_set_debug_filter_state_stub(ULONG, ULONG, BOOLEAN) -> LONG` always returns `status_success`.
- `nt_yield_execution_stub() -> LONG` delegates to `nt_yield_execution_hook`.
- `is_debugger_present_stub() -> BOOL` always returns `FALSE`; `check_remote_debugger_present_stub(HANDLE, PBOOL) -> BOOL` writes `FALSE` when `present != nullptr` and returns `TRUE`.
- `output_debug_string_a_stub(LPCSTR)` and `output_debug_string_w_stub(LPCWSTR)` discard debug output.

## Patching and PE/Import Handling

- `mem_write(void*, const void*, size_t) -> bool` temporarily changes protection to `PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE`, copies bytes with `memcpy`, calls `FlushInstructionCache`, restores protection, and reports `VirtualProtect` failure.
- `scan(uint8_t*, size_t, const uint8_t*, size_t) -> uint8_t*` performs an exact byte-pattern search and returns `nullptr` for empty patterns, undersized images, or missing signatures.
- `get_module_range(const char*, uint8_t*&, size_t&) -> bool` resolves a module with `GetModuleHandleA`, validates `IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE` and `IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE`, and returns `IMAGE_NT_HEADERS::OptionalHeader.SizeOfImage`.
- `patch_xlive_imports(uint8_t*, size_t)` scans `IMAGE_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR` entries for case-insensitive `"kernel32.dll"` or `"kernel32"` and replaces `IsDebuggerPresent`, `CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent`, `OutputDebugStringA`, and `OutputDebugStringW` IAT entries via `mem_write`; malformed access is suppressed by `__try/__except (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER)`.
- `patch_peverifyhash(uint8_t*, size_t)` searches the 22-byte `prologue` signature, falls back to `peverifyhash_rva = 0x000F36B3u`, and overwrites the target with `ret_success = { 0x31, 0xC0, 0xC2, 0x0C, 0x00 }`, making `PEVerifyHash` return success with `ret 0x0C`.
- `patch_peverifyhash()` skips absent signatures, already-patched `ret_success`, or unexpected bytes; `dbg()` records `"PEVerifyHash patch skipped: signature missing"`, `"PEVerifyHash patch already applied"`, `"PEVerifyHash patch skipped: unexpected bytes at +0x%X"`, and `"PEVerifyHash patch applied at +0x%X"` in `DEBUG`.

## Lifecycle and Coupling

- `hook_ntdll()` installs `utils::hook::detour` instances for `NtQueryInformationProcess`, `NtSetInformationThread`, `NtSetInformationProcess`, `NtQuerySystemInformation`, `NtGetContextThread`, `NtSetContextThread`, `NtSetDebugFilterState`, and `NtYieldExecution` using `GetProcAddress`.
- `clear_peb_debug_flags()` uses x86 FS offsets `0x18` and `0x30`, clears PEB byte offset `0x02` (`BeingDebugged`) and DWORD offset `0x68` (`NtGlobalFlag`), and safely returns when the PEB is null.
- `peb_cleaner_thread(LPVOID) -> DWORD` runs indefinitely, calling `clear_peb_debug_flags()` followed by `Sleep(16)`, so `apply_early()` intentionally creates a persistent thread and immediately closes its handle.
- `patch_xlive()` targets only the loaded `"xlive.dll"` module and applies `patch_peverifyhash()` plus `patch_xlive_imports()`.
- `dbg(const char*, ...)` formats into a 512-byte buffer and emits `[xlive] ` through `OutputDebugStringA` in `DEBUG`; the release implementation is a no-op.
- `std_include.hpp`, `utils/hook.hpp`, `loader/component_loader.hpp`, and `xlive.hpp` supply Windows types, detour machinery, component integration, and xlive declarations.

## Contents

- [integrator.cpp](./integrator.cpp) implements `turn_integrator::advance`.
- [integrator.hpp](./integrator.hpp) declares acceleration/deceleration limits, `advance`, `current`, and `reset`.
- [filter.cpp](./filter.cpp) implements frame-time-independent `low_pass` smoothing.
- [filter.hpp](./filter.hpp) declares `low_pass`, `apply`, `reset`, and `value`.

### Calibration and shaping

- [calibration.cpp](./calibration.cpp) implements `fov_scale`, validated `aim_calibration::make`, and `processor_config`.
- [calibration.hpp](./calibration.hpp) declares `aim_settings`, `aim_calibration`, and FOV-aware calibration ownership.
- [curve.cpp](./curve.cpp) implements `to_string`, `validate`, and `evaluate` for response curves.
- [curve.hpp](./curve.hpp) declares `curve_kind` and `response_curve`.
- [deadzone.cpp](./deadzone.cpp) implements radial `validate` and `apply` for stick deadzones.
- [deadzone.hpp](./deadzone.hpp) declares `deadzone_params`, deadzone validation, and radial transformation.
- [graph.cpp](./graph.cpp) implements validated piecewise-linear `aim_graph::make` and `aim_graph::evaluate`.
- [graph.hpp](./graph.hpp) declares `knot`, `max_graph_knots`, and allocation-free `aim_graph`.

### Domain types

- [types.cpp](./types.cpp) implements stream formatting for `degrees` and `deg_per_s`.
- [types.hpp](./types.hpp) declares `degrees`, `radians`, `deg_per_s`, `deg_per_s2`, `axis_input`, `magnitude`, `screen_vector`, `world_vector`, `dot`, and unit conversions.

## Architecture / Data Flow

`aim_calibration::make` validates `aim_settings`, optionally constructs `aim_graph`, and returns `aim_calibration`; `aim_calibration::processor_config` supplies `aim_processor::config`.

`aim_processor::process` clamps `ads_lerp`, interpolates `aim_profile` values, applies `deadzone_params`, evaluates `response_curve` or `aim_graph`, scales by FOV/sensitivity/slowdown, advances `turn_integrator`, enforces optional limits, and applies pitch inversion.

`low_pass` smooths scalar input independently of frame rate, while `lock_on` converts projected relative velocity into yaw and pitch corrections.

## Behavioral Contracts

- `curve::validate` requires power `exponent` to be finite and greater than `0.0f`; `curve::evaluate` clamps input to `[0.0f, 1.0f]`.
- `deadzone::validate` requires `inner.value`, `outer.value`, and `anti.value` in `[0, 1)`, plus `inner.value < 1.0f - outer.value`.
- `aim_graph::make` accepts 2–`max_graph_knots` knots, with `max_graph_knots == 16`, finite values, inputs in `[0, 1]`, and strictly increasing inputs.
- `aim_processor::process` uses `cfg_.ads.curve` when `t >= 0.5f`, integrates non-negative target speeds before restoring signs, and negates final pitch when `invert_pitch` is true.
- `slowdown_scale` returns `1.0f` without a target and otherwise interpolates hip/ADS scales using clamped `ads_lerp`.
- `scale_dominant_axis` preserves the dominant stick axis and attenuates the subordinate axis by the absolute-magnitude difference.
- `lock_on` returns `{}` when `target.distance <= 0.0f`; otherwise it uses `arc = target.distance * pi`.
- `low_pass::apply` bypasses smoothing when `tau_ <= 0`, adopts the first target exactly, and otherwise uses `alpha = clamp(1 - exp(-dt/tau), 0, 1)`.
- `turn_integrator::advance` returns `degrees{0.0f}` for `dt <= 0` and integrates rate with `0.5f * (prev + cur) * dt`.
- `fov_scale` returns `1.0f` when the reference tangent is non-positive or `f` is non-finite.
- `aim_calibration::make` emits `"hip deadzone: "`, `"ADS deadzone: "`, `"hip curve: "`, `"ADS curve: "`, and `"aim graph: "` diagnostics.

## File Relationships

`assist.cpp` consumes `deadzone.cpp`, `curve.cpp`, `graph.cpp`, and `integrator.cpp` through `assist.hpp`, while `calibration.cpp` assembles `curve`, `deadzone`, and `graph` validation into `aim_processor::config`.

`aim_calibration::graph_` must outlive processors created from `processor_config()`, and `lock_on_target::view_yaw_axis` must use RIGHT (`+yaw`) coordinates.

`discovery::scan()` consumes `notifier_` state and clock values, invokes `scan_now()` when required, and reconciles `registry` membership.

`discovery::scan_now()` collects `transport_binding` values, scans XInput first, conditionally scans HID, and passes unseen bindings to `retire_unseen()`.

`device_identity` selects `family`, `capabilities_for()` records factual hardware support, and drivers outside `device` decode reports and emit samples.

## Behavioral Contracts

- `operator<<(ostream&, capabilities)` emits `{}` or ordered names: `gyroscope`, `accelerometer`, `touchpad`, `battery`, `microphone-button`, `back-buttons`, `rumble`, `haptics`, `adaptive-triggers`, `light-bar`, `player-leds`.

- `scan_hid()` requires `e.link != connection::unknown`; `scan_xinput()` records `connection::unknown`.

`capabilities_for(family::dualshock4)` returns gyroscope, accelerometer, touchpad, battery, rumble, and light-bar capabilities.

`capabilities_for(family::dualsense)` returns `dualsense_capabilities`; `family::dualsense_edge` adds `capability::back_buttons`.

`enumerate` discovers present HID interfaces, `classify_link` validates report framing, and `open` creates a `windows_hid_device` after re-querying `HidD_GetAttributes` and `query_caps`.

- [calibration/](./calibration/) contains profile measurement, normalization, validation, and persistence.
- [device/](./device/) contains device identity, capability classification, discovery, registry, and transport bindings.
- [driver/](./driver/) contains XInput and PlayStation polling, report decoding, output encoding, and driver reconciliation.
- [engine/](./engine/) contains dvars, commands, key dispatch, bindings, view movement, imports, and hooks.
- [mapping/](./mapping/) contains physical-to-engine key translation, logical commands, glyphs, bindings, and stick layouts.
- [sample/](./sample/) contains raw and canonical samples, buttons, axes, triggers, motion, touch, frames, and SPSC rings.
- [support/](./support/) contains shared controller type aliases and non-owning `function_ref`.
- [transport/](./transport/) contains HID I/O, device notifications, and dynamically loaded XInput APIs.

## Architecture / Data Flow

`runtime::frame()` invokes `discovery::scan()`, `driver::set::reconcile()`, `runtime::advance()`, `engine::key_dispatcher::dispatch()`, `engine::view_driver::observe()`, and `runtime::apply_light_bar()`.

`driver::driver::poll()` writes `sample::raw_sample`, `calibration::apply()` writes `sample::canonical_sample`, and `runtime::advance()` publishes `sample::input_frame` with `clock::timestamp`, `clock::latency_span`, `device_id`, and monotonic `sequence`.

`context` shares `diagnostic_sink`, `developer`, `errc`, and device identity values across `device`, `driver`, `sample`, `aim`, and `engine` layers without owning subsystem state.

`runtime::engine_ready()` registers engine dvars and commands, applies `binds_`, performs eager discovery, and gates subsequent `runtime::frame()` execution through `engine_ready_`.

`runtime::active_` selects one device for singular key and view state, while `runtime::latest_`, `sequence_`, `last_published_`, and `had_device_` preserve publication and takeover invariants.

## API Surface

`runtime::runtime`, `runtime::engine_ready`, `runtime::frame`, `runtime::active`, `runtime::latest`, `runtime::keys`, `runtime::binds`, `runtime::view`, `runtime::driving`, `runtime::dvars`, and `runtime::device_count` define the process-level controller boundary.

`context::make_context`, `context::diagnostics`, `context::developer`, and both `context::report` overloads define the borrowed service boundary.

`clock::now`, `clock::since_epoch`, `latency_span::latency`, `to_string(facility)`, `to_string(severity)`, `to_string(errc)`, `operator<<(ostream&, errc)`, and `report` define shared timing and diagnostic utilities.

## Behavioral Contracts

`clock::base` must satisfy `base::is_steady`, and `clock::since_epoch()` uses a first-call-fixed epoch.

`latency_span::latency()` computes `consumed - acquired` without validation and assumes `consumed >= acquired`.

`to_string(facility)` recognizes `runtime`, `discovery`, `transport`, `driver`, `decode`, `sample`, `calibration`, `mapping`, `aim`, `steam`, `engine`, and `debug`, with unknown values returning `"runtime"`.

`to_string(severity)` maps `info`, `warning`, and `error`, with unknown values returning `"info"`.

`logging_sink::consume` emits `controller: <facility>: <message> [<code>] device=<id>\n`; `[<code>]` is omitted for `errc::none`, and `device=<id>` is omitted for empty devices.

`errc` string tokens remain stable: `"none"`, `"device-unavailable"`, `"ambiguous-identity"`, `"unsupported-device"`, `"transport-failure"`, `"report-malformed"`, `"report-truncated"`, `"checksum-mismatch"`, `"output-rejected"`, `"calibration-invalid"`, `"calibration-version"`, `"graph-invalid"`, `"binding-invalid"`, `"steam-unavailable"`, `"steam-unsuitable"`, `"hook-failed"`, and `"dvar-registration"`.

`runtime::engine_ready()` is idempotent through `engine_ready_`, and `runtime::frame()` must not throw across the engine ABI or allocate on per-frame acquisition.

`runtime::profile_for()` indexes `profiles_` by `controller::family`, with `profiles_` sized for five families and a `static_assert` covering `controller::family::dualsense_edge == 4`.

`runtime::advance()` aborts publication when `driver::driver::poll()` returns `false`, increments `sequence_`, and preserves monotonic `last_published_`.

`runtime::frame()` releases held keys when `active_ != latest_.device`, while `engine::key_dispatcher::dispatch()` continues held-button repeats when `had_device_` is true.

`runtime::apply_light_bar()` clamps RGB channels to `[0, 255]`, packs `colour` as `(r << 16) | (g << 8) | b`, and submits output only when `lit_device_` or `lit_colour_` changes.

`light_bar_r`, `light_bar_g`, and `light_bar_b` default to `196`, `151`, and `54`; light-bar output requires `capability::light_bar`.

`LIBIW4X_CONTROLLER_TRACE` defaults to `0`, while `CONTROLLER_ZONE(name)` and `CONTROLLER_FRAME_MARK()` expand to `do {} while (false)` when tracing is disabled.

## Role and Architecture

`command::component` integrates command registration with the component lifecycle through `component_interface`, `REGISTER_COMPONENT(command::component)`, and `scheduler::once(..., scheduler::main)`.

`cmd_allocator` owns `game::cmd_function_s` allocations and is released by `component::pre_destroy()`.

`main_handler()` lowercases `params[0]`, looks up `handlers`, and invokes the matching callback; unknown commands are ignored.

## Exported Interface

`command::params::params()` captures the current engine command nesting index from `*game::command_id`.

`int command::params::size() const` returns `game::cmd_argc[nesting_]`.

`const char* command::params::get(int index) const` returns `game::cmd_argv[nesting_][index]`, or `""` when `index >= size()`; negative indices are not explicitly rejected.

`std::string command::params::join(int index) const` joins arguments from `index` through `size() - 1` with literal spaces.

`void command::add(const char* name, const std::function<void()>& callback)` adapts a no-argument callback to `std::function<void(const params&)>`.

## Runtime Constants and Engine Memory Contracts

`CLIENT_REAL_PLAYER_OFFSET` is `0x20`; `is_bot_client(int index)` treats a client as a bot when its connection state is at least `game::CS_CONNECTED` and the integer at `client + 0x20` equals `0`.

`CLIENT_USERINFO_OFFSET` is `1604`; `rename_new_bot_client()` reads and rewrites userinfo at `get_client(i) + 1604`.

`CLIENT_USERINFO_SIZE` is `1024`; `rename_new_bot_client()` zeroes 1024 bytes and copies at most `CLIENT_USERINFO_SIZE - 1` bytes before calling `game::SV_ClientUserinfoChanged(i)`.

`CLAN_DIRTY_FLAGS` is `0x1149E6BC`; `update_clan_name_state()` resolves it and ORs the pointed `std::uint32_t` with `2u`.

`GAMETYPES_RAWFILE` is `"maps/mp/gametypes/_gametypes.txt"`; `dumpGametypes` passes it to `dump_rawfile()`.

## Parsing, Paths, and File I/O

`parse_integer(const char* value, std::uintptr_t* result)` rejects null, empty, or invalid strings; it uses base `10`, switches to base `16` for `0x`/`0X` prefixes or any hexadecimal letters `a-fA-F`, and requires `std::strtoull()` to consume the entire input.

`resolve_address(std::uintptr_t parsed)` treats values in `[0x10000000, 0x20000000)` as IDA/game addresses and maps them with `game::game_offset()`; other values remain runtime pointers.

`append_format(std::string& output, const char* format, ...)` formats into a 256-byte buffer with `vsnprintf_s(..., _TRUNCATE, ...)`, so formatted lines are truncated at 255 bytes.

`get_exe_directory()` obtains the executable path through `GetModuleFileNameA(nullptr, path, sizeof(path))`, rejects zero or oversized results, and removes the final `/` or `\` component.

`resolve_game_path(const std::string& path)` preserves paths with a drive prefix at `path[1] == ':'`; other paths receive the executable directory plus `"\\"`.

`create_directory_tree(const std::string& path, DWORD* error)` creates each slash-delimited parent using `CreateDirectoryA`, accepts `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS`, and stores `GetLastError()` through `error` on failure.

`write_file_noexcept(const std::string& path, const std::string& data, DWORD* error)` resolves the path, creates parents, writes with `CreateFileA(..., GENERIC_WRITE, FILE_SHARE_READ, ..., CREATE_ALWAYS, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, ...)`, caps the write size at `MAXDWORD`, requires `WriteFile()` and exact byte count, and closes the handle.

`is_readable_memory(const void* address, std::size_t length)` uses `VirtualQuery()` and accepts committed regions with `PAGE_READONLY`, `PAGE_READWRITE`, `PAGE_WRITECOPY`, `PAGE_EXECUTE_READ`, `PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE`, or `PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY`; it requires `start + length <= region_end`.

`safe_read_byte(std::uintptr_t address, unsigned char* value)` reads one byte with `ReadProcessMemory(GetCurrentProcess(), ...)` and requires exactly `sizeof(*value)` bytes.

`dump_memory(const char* address_text, const char* length_text, const char* output_name)` implements `dumpMemory <address> [length] [output]`; default length is `0x100`, accepted length is clamped to `[1, 0x4000]`, and only the first byte is validated with `is_readable_memory()`.

`dump_memory()` emits hexadecimal rows using exact formats `"%08X  "` and `"%02X "`, substitutes `"?? "` and `'?'` for failed byte reads, renders printable ASCII for bytes `32 <= byte < 127`, and terminates rows with `"\r\n"`.

`dump_memory()` defaults output to `"consolation/memory_dump/%08X.txt"`; explicit output names are appended to `"consolation/memory_dump/"`, then written by `write_file_noexcept()`.

`dump_rawfile()` prints `"dumpRawFile <rawfile> [output]: dump a rawfile asset to consolation/rawfile_dump\n"` without an asset name and warns with `"dumpRawFile: rawfile '%s' was empty or unavailable\n"` for unavailable data.

`dump_rawfile_binary(const game::RawFile* rawfile, const char* output_prefix)` writes binary data to `output_prefix + make_dump_safe_path(rawfile->name)` through `write_file_noexcept()`.

`dump_swf_by_name(const char* swf_name)` enumerates loaded `game::ASSET_TYPE_RAWFILE` assets via `fastfiles::enum_assets(..., true)`, compares lowercased basenames against the requested name, and accepts `.swf` to `.gfx` fallback conversion.

## Exported Interface

- `print(const int type, const char* fmt, ...)` formats variadic text with `format`, then routes it through `dispatch_message(type, result)` for console output, game-console storage, color selection, and logging.
- `match_compare(const std::string& input, const std::string& text, const bool exact) -> bool` returns `true` when `exact` requires `text == input`, or when non-exact mode finds `input` as a substring of `text`.
- `showDevConsole() -> void` sleeps for `500ms`, calls `game::Sys_ShowConsole()`, then pumps `GetMessageA`, `TranslateMessage`, and `DispatchMessageA` until the message loop ends.
- `console::component final : component_interface` allocates/configures the Windows console in its constructor, installs hooks in `post_load()`, and tears down hooks/thread/handles in `pre_destroy()`.
- `REGISTER_COMPONENT(console::component)` registers `console::component` with the loader component system.

## Console Lifecycle

- `component::component()` calls `AllocConsole()`, `AttachConsole(GetCurrentProcessId())`, redirects `stdin` to `CONIN$`, redirects `stdout`/`stderr` to `CONOUT$`, and initially hides `GetConsoleWindow()` with `SW_HIDE`.
- `component::post_load()` creates `printf_hook` over `printf` and `com_printf_hook` over `game::game_offset(0x103F6400)`, shows the console, sets a versioned title, creates `con.kill_event`, and starts the named `"Console"` thread through `utils::thread::create_named_thread`.
- `component::pre_destroy()` clears `printf_hook` and `com_printf_hook`, sets `con.kill`, signals `con.kill_event`, posts `WM_QUIT` to `con.thread_id`, cancels synchronous I/O, joins `con.thread`, hides/frees the console, closes `con.kill_event`, and resets `con.thread_id`.
- `con.thread` waits on `STD_INPUT_HANDLE`, `con.kill_event`, and queued window messages through `MsgWaitForMultipleObjects(..., 100, QS_ALLINPUT)`.
- `game_window_closed()` ignores missing windows before first observation, then treats a missing `*game::main_window` lasting more than `3s` as shutdown.
- `con.thread` handles `WM_QUIT`, `WM_CLOSE`, and `WM_DESTROY` by enqueueing `game::Cbuf_AddText(0, "quit\n")`; other messages pass through `TranslateMessage` and `DispatchMessageA`.

## Input State and Rendering

- `con` stores `kill`, `thread`, `kill_event`, `thread_id`, a fixed `char buffer[512]`, `cursor`, `history_index`, and a `std::deque<std::string> history`.
- `handle_input(INPUT_RECORD record)` handles resize events, key-down events, cursor movement, editing, command submission, and history navigation under `print_mutex`.
- `VK_UP` and `VK_DOWN` navigate `con.history`, clamp `con.history_index` to `[-1, history.size()-1]`, copy selected entries into `con.buffer`, and refresh through `clear()`/`update()`.
- `VK_LEFT` and `VK_RIGHT` clamp `con.cursor` to the current `strlen(con.buffer)` range; `VK_BACK` removes one byte with `std::memmove`; `VK_ESCAPE` clears the input buffer.
- `VK_RETURN` removes a duplicated selected history entry, pushes non-empty input to the front, caps `con.history` at `10` entries, submits `utils::string::va("%s\n", con.buffer)` through `game::Cbuf_AddText(0, ...)`, logs `"]%s\n"`, prints `"]%s\r\n"`, and clears `con.buffer`.
- `get_max_input_length() -> size_t` derives the input limit from the console window width and `sizeof(con.buffer)`; insertion is rejected when `strlen(con.buffer) + 1 >= get_max_input_length()`.
- `update()` hides the cursor, rewrites `con.buffer` at position `0`, restores `con.cursor`, and shows the cursor; `clear_output()` overwrites the displayed input with spaces based on `strlen(con.buffer)`.
- `handle_resize()` calls `clear()` followed by `update()`; `clear()` resets `con.buffer`, `con.cursor`, and the console cursor position.
- `set_cursor_pos(int x)` and `show_cursor(bool show)` manipulate `CONSOLE_SCREEN_BUFFER_INFO` and `CONSOLE_CURSOR_INFO` on `OUTPUT_HANDLE`.
- `get_attribute(int type) -> uint8_t` maps `con_type_info` to `7` (white), `con_type_warning` to `6` (yellow), `con_type_error` to `4` (red), and `con_type_debug` to `3` (cyan), defaulting to `7`.

## Output Hooks and Classification

- `printf_stub(const char* fmt, ...) -> int` formats through `format`, calls `write_log`, appends to `game_console::append_output`, forwards to `game::CL_ConsolePrint(0, 6, result.c_str(), 0, 0, 0)`, and returns the original `printf` status through `invoke_printf("%s", result.data())`.
- `com_printf_stub(int channel, const char* fmt, ...) -> void` formats/logs game output, forwards the formatted string to the original `com_printf_hook`, classifies color prefixes and keyword substrings, applies suppression rules, and dispatches colored output.
- `format(va_list* ap, const char* message) -> std::string` uses thread-local `char buffer[0x1000]` and `vsnprintf_s(buffer, _TRUNCATE, message, *ap)`; negative results return `{}` and successful results preserve the reported byte count.
- `dispatch_message(int type, const std::string& message) -> int` logs unless `skip_dispatch_log`, appends through `game_console::append_output`, clears the input line, sets `get_attribute(type)`, prints `message`, restores info color, adds `"\n"` when needed, refreshes input, and returns the original print result.
- `dispatch_split_debug_message(const std::string& message) -> int` logs `"debug:" + message`, appends only `message`, prints `"debug:"` in `con_type_error` color and the body in `con_type_warning` color, then restores `con_type_info`.
- `com_printf_stub` recognizes `^1` as `con_type_error`, `^3` as `con_type_warning`, and `^5` as `con_type_debug`, stripping the two-byte prefix for display.
- `error_substrings` forces `con_type_error` for `"Unable to"`, `"Couldn't reset"`, and `"nat type is Strict"`.
- `warning_substrings` forces `con_type_warning` for `"Unable to"`, `"Missing asset"`, `"Couldn't find"`, `"Unknown command"`, `"is read only"`, `"is not a valid value"`, `"is write protected"`, `"already defined"`, `"Adding channel:"`, `"Hiding channel:"`, `"will use the shock"`, `"WARNING:"`, and `"nat type is Moderate"`.
- `debug_substrings` forces `con_type_debug` for `"GamerProfile_LogInProfile took"`, `"connection status has changed"`, `"signed in to live"`, `"Reading profile"`, `"Loaded zone"`, `"Loading fastfile"`, `"nat type is Open"`, `"LOADING..."`, `"xuid"`, and `"execing"`.
- `com_printf_stub` handles `"^1debug:^3 "` specially through `dispatch_split_debug_message(result.substr(10))`, with `skip_dispatch_log` preventing duplicate log writes.
- `com_printf_stub` dispatches `"Velocity change:"` only when `game::Dvar_FindVar("g_debugVelocity")` exists and `current.enabled` is true.
- `com_printf_stub` suppresses repeated `"XUserReadProfileSettings"` messages using static `xsignin`; the first occurrence emits `"Reading XUserProfileSettings"` and omits the original message when it contains `"took 0ms"`.

## Logging and Version Contracts

- `get_log_paths() -> std::vector<std::filesystem::path>` tries `current_path() / "consolation" / "console.log"`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Project-Consolation/console.log`, and `%TEMP%/Project-Consolation-console.log`, in that order.
- `write_log(const std::string& message)` serializes initialization and appends through `utils::io::write_file`; the first writable path receives `"console: logging to %s\n"`, and messages without a trailing newline receive `"\n"`.
- `write_log` uses `log_mutex`, `log_initialized`, and `log_path`; failure across all paths emits `OutputDebugStringA("console: failed to open console.log\n")` and disables further writes.
- `skip_dispatch_log` is `thread_local`; `printf_stub` and direct command submission log independently, while `com_printf_stub` prevents duplicate dispatch logging.
- `build_display_version() -> std::string` combines `VERSION_PRODUCT`, `VERSION_BUILD` (default `"0"`), the first seven characters of `GIT_HASH`, `"-dbg-"` under `DEBUG` or `"-nightly-"` otherwise, and `"-dirty"` when `GIT_DIRTY` is true.
- `normalize_build_date(const char* raw_date) -> std::string` returns `{}` for null input and repeatedly collapses adjacent spaces via the exact search pattern `"  "` to normalize `__DATE__`.
- `component::post_load()` formats the title as `"Project: Consolation [" + build_display_version() + " | " + normalize_build_date(__DATE__) + " " + __TIME__ + "] - Console"`.

## Coupling and Synchronization

- `printf_hook` and `com_printf_hook` depend on `utils::hook::detour`; `invoke_printf` falls back to `std::printf` when `printf_hook.get_original()` is unavailable.
- `game_console::append_output`, `game::Cbuf_AddText`, `game::CL_ConsolePrint`, `game::Dvar_FindVar`, `game::main_window`, and `game::Sys_ShowConsole` form the game integration boundary.
- `print_mutex` is recursive because `dispatch_message`, `clear_output`, and `update` nest console-rendering operations; `log_mutex` serializes lazy log-file initialization and writes.
- `con.thread` and `con.kill_event` define shutdown signaling; `CancelSynchronousIo` handles a potentially blocked console read before `con.thread.join()`.

**game_console.cpp does hook-driven in-game console overlay rendering, input handling, command/dvar autocomplete, output buffering, history management, and version display for the `game_console` component.**

## Public Interface

- `bool is_active()` returns the process-global `overlay_active` state.
- `void append_output(std::string_view text)` queues console output under `get_pending_output_mutex()`, ignores empty text or `process_shutting_down`, and caps the pending queue at `max_console_lines * 2` entries.
- `void toggle()` invokes `toggle_overlay_state()` to open or close the overlay.
- `class component final : public component_interface` registers through `REGISTER_COMPONENT(game_console::component)`, initializes `console_state`, installs scheduler callbacks, and clears hooks during destruction.

## Runtime Integration

- `component::post_load()` allocates `con`, registers `con_outputHeightScale` through `dvars::Dvar_RegisterFloat("con_outputHeightScale", "Height scale for the shift-tab console output pane.", 0.72f, 0.20f, 0.98f, game::dvar_flags::saved)`, and schedules initialization on `scheduler::main`.
- `component::post_load()` schedules `install_hooks_if_ready()` every `50ms`, guarded output flushing, F1/OEM-key toggles, and `safe_process_console_input()` every `16ms`.
- `install_hooks_if_ready()` creates `cl_console_print_hook` against `game::CL_ConsolePrint.get()`, `cl_key_event_hook` against `game::CL_KeyEvent_.get()`, and `con_set_console_rect_hook` against `game::Con_SetConsoleRect.get()` once `get_window()` returns a valid `HWND`.
- `cl_console_print_stub(int local_client_num, int channel, const char* txt, int duration, int pixel_width, int flags)` mirrors `txt` into `append_console_text()` before forwarding all arguments through `cl_console_print_hook.invoke<void>()`.
- `con_set_console_rect_stub()` invokes the original `Con_SetConsoleRect` detour and then calls `draw_console_overlay()`.
- `cl_key_event_stub()` preserves the x86 register/stack ABI, calls `cl_key_event_body()`, swallows focused-game events when `should_swallow_key_event()` returns true, and otherwise forwards to `call_original_cl_key_event()`.
- `component::pre_destroy()` sets `process_shutting_down`, resets readiness flags, disables `overlay_active`, clears `cl_key_event_hook`, `cl_console_print_hook`, and `con_set_console_rect_hook`, then nulls `con`.
- `scheduler::on_shutdown()` resets `component_ready`, `hooks_installed`, `console_print_hook_installed`, `con_outputHeightScale`, keyboard state, and overlay state.

## State Model

- `console_state` stores `input`, `cursor`, `selection_start`, `selection_end`, `history_index`, history snapshot fields, `scroll_offset`, `output_visible`, `output_fullscreen`, `history`, `lines`, autocomplete matches/query/choice, query offsets, selected match index, and `may_auto_complete`.
- `overlay_active` controls visibility; `component_ready`, `hooks_installed`, `console_print_hook_installed`, and `process_shutting_down` gate lifecycle-sensitive operations.
- `key_was_down`, `key_is_down`, and `key_next_repeat_time` implement polling-based edge detection and repeat timing for 256 virtual-key slots.
- `get_pending_output_queue()` and `get_pending_output_mutex()` return leaked process-lifetime singletons, allowing output calls from outside the main rendering/input loop.
- `cached_command_names` and `cached_dvar_names` cache sanitized command and dvar identifiers; cache rebuilding traverses at most `4096` command nodes and `16384` nodes per each of `256` dvar hash buckets.

## Version and Prompt Contracts

- `build_display_version()` formats `VERSION_PRODUCT + "(" + VERSION_BUILD + ")" + ("-dbg-" or "-nightly-") + first-seven-character-GIT_HASH`, appending `"-dirty"` when `GIT_DIRTY` is true; `VERSION_BUILD` defaults to `"0"` when undefined.
- `build_prompt_version()` formats debug builds as `VERSION_PRODUCT + "-dbg"`, release builds as plain `VERSION_PRODUCT`, other builds as `VERSION_PRODUCT + "-nightly"`, followed by `" [" + short_hash + "]"` where dirty hashes use `"-dirty"`.
- `build_full_version_string()` formats `"Project: Consolation " + VERSION_PRODUCT + build_suffix + " build " + short_hash + dirty_suffix + " " + __DATE__ + " " + __TIME__ + " win-x86"`.
- `build_console_prompt()` returns `"Project: Consolation " + build_prompt_version() + " >"`.
- `draw_output_window()` displays `build_full_version_string()` as the footer, while `draw_input()` displays `build_console_prompt()` before `con->input`.

## Output Processing

- `append_console_text(const char* text)` removes carriage returns, splits on `'\n'`, and appends non-empty segments through `append_line()`.
- `append_line(const std::string& line)` suppresses consecutive duplicate lines and invokes `trim_console_lines()`.
- `trim_console_lines()` retains only the newest `max_console_lines == 128u` entries and clamps negative `con->scroll_offset` to zero.
- `flush_pending_output()` swaps the mutex-protected pending deque into a local deque, then feeds each queued string to `append_console_text()`.
- `strip_colors(std::string_view text)` removes `^` followed by an ASCII digit and removes `'\r'`.
- `strip_carriage_returns(std::string_view text)` removes every `'\r'`.
- `sanitize_display_text(std::string_view text)` applies `strip_colors()` and removes all bytes below ASCII `32` or above ASCII `126`.
- `try_copy_c_string(const char* text, std::string& out)` copies at most `511` bytes inside `__try/__except`, rejects null/empty input and access violations, and always terminates `buffer[511]`.
- `append_output()` queues raw text; `append_console_text()` performs line splitting; `sanitize_display_text()` is reserved for safe visible metadata/value rendering.

## Command and Dvar Discovery

- `to_lower(std::string value)` performs unsigned-character `std::tolower` conversion in place.
- `is_reasonable_console_token(std::string_view value)` accepts alphanumerics plus `_`, `-`, `+`, `.`, `:`, `/`, `\`, `*`, `?`, and `@`; all other characters reject the token.
- `safe_read_cmd_name(game::cmd_function_s* current, game::cmd_function_s** next_out, char* name, std::size_t name_size)` safely reads `current->next` and `current->name` with bounded copying and `__try/__except`.
- `safe_read_dvar_name(game::dvar_s* current, char* name, std::size_t name_size)` safely copies `current->name` with bounded copying and exception shielding.
- `safe_read_dvar_description(game::dvar_s* current, char* description, std::size_t description_size)` safely copies `current->description` with bounded copying and exception shielding.
- `safe_read_dvar_hash_entry(game::dvar_s* current, game::dvar_s** next_out, char* name, std::size_t name_size)` safely reads `current->hashNext` and `current->name`.
- `rebuild_auto_complete_cache()` deduplicates command and dvar names case-insensitively using `std::unordered_set<std::string>`, filters through `is_reasonable_console_token()`, and refreshes both global caches.
- `try_get_dvar_value_ptr(game::dvar_s* dvar, game::DvarValue value, const char** value_out)` calls `dvars::Dvar_ValueToString()` under `__try/__except` and rejects null converted values.
- `try_copy_dvar_domain(game::dvar_s* dvar, game::dvar_type& type_out, game::DvarLimits& domain_out)` safely copies `dvar->type` and `dvar->domain`.
- `is_dvar_command_token(std::string_view token)` recognizes exactly `set`, `seta`, `sets`, `reset`, `toggle`, and `togglep`, case-insensitively.
- `gather_auto_complete_matches(std::string input, bool exact)` ranks matches as exact, dvar-prefix, command-prefix, dvar-contained, and command-contained; each group sorts with `_stricmp`, and exact mode returns only case-insensitive equality matches.
- `gather_auto_complete_matches()` prioritizes dvars over commands within prefix and substring groups and deduplicates by lowercase identifier.
- `refresh_auto_complete()` strips one leading `/` or `\`, treats the first token as an exact command query when a space exists, treats the remainder as a dvar argument for `is_dvar_command_token()`, and retries after `rebuild_auto_complete_cache()` when no matches appear.
- `get_auto_complete_common_prefix()` computes the case-insensitive longest common prefix across `con->auto_complete_matches`.
- `sync_auto_complete_choice()` wraps `auto_complete_selected_index` modulo match count and updates `auto_complete_choice`.
- `cycle_auto_complete_choice(int direction)` wraps selection across all matches, supporting forward and backward cycling.
- `commit_auto_complete_choice(bool append_space)` replaces the tracked query with `auto_complete_choice` through `apply_auto_complete_text()`.
- `apply_auto_complete_text(std::string text, bool append_space)` replaces the query range, advances `con->cursor`, optionally inserts one space while `cursor < max_input_chars`, clears selection, and refreshes autocomplete.
- `handle_auto_complete()` commits a single match with a trailing space, inserts a longer common prefix without a space, or cycles among multiple matches.

## Input Editing and Clipboard

- `set_overlay_active(bool active)` resets keyboard state and autocomplete; opening resets history/output navigation, while closing clears input and cursor state.
- `clear_auto_complete()` clears all autocomplete fields and sets `may_auto_complete` false.
- `clear_input_line()` empties `con->input`, moves the cursor to zero, and clears autocomplete.
- `set_cursor_position(std::size_t cursor)` clamps the cursor to `con->input.size()` and clears selection.
- `select_entire_input()` selects `[0, input.size()]` and moves the cursor to the end.
- `delete_input_selection()` erases the normalized selection range, moves the cursor to its beginning, and invalidates the history snapshot.
- `insert_character(char ch)` replaces any selection, enforces `max_input_chars == 240u`, inserts at the cursor, invalidates the snapshot, and refreshes autocomplete.
- `insert_text(std::string text)` removes `'\r'`, `'\n'`, and `'\t'`, truncates to the remaining `max_input_chars == 240u` capacity, inserts at the cursor, and refreshes autocomplete.
- `insert_wide_text(const WCHAR* text, int length)` converts each UTF-16 code unit through `WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP, ...)` and accepts printable bytes `>= 32` excluding `127`.
- `paste_from_clipboard()` reads `CF_TEXT` through `OpenClipboard()`, `GetClipboardData()`, and `GlobalLock()`, then delegates insertion to `insert_text()`.
- `copy_text_to_clipboard(std::string_view text)` writes a null-terminated `CF_TEXT` global allocation through `EmptyClipboard()` and `SetClipboardData()`.
- `handle_ctrl_shortcut(int vk)` maps Ctrl+A to select all, Ctrl+Shift+C to copy, Ctrl+V to paste, and Ctrl+L to clear output; Ctrl+C without Shift is passed through as non-handled.
- `clear_dead_key_state()` calls `ToUnicode(VK_SPACE, MapVirtualKeyA(VK_SPACE, MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC), ...)` with a zeroed keyboard state to consume dead-key state.
- `handle_text_key(int vk)` obtains `GetKeyboardState()`, translates through `MapVirtualKeyA()` and `ToUnicode()`, inserts translated text, and clears dead-key state for negative `ToUnicode()` results.

## History and Command Execution

- `trim_history()` retains at most `max_history_entries == 32u` newest commands.
- `save_history_snapshot()` stores input, cursor, and selection only when `history_snapshot_valid` is false.
- `restore_history_snapshot()` restores clamped snapshot fields, normalizes empty selection to the cursor, clears validity, and refreshes autocomplete.
- `history_up()` saves the editable snapshot on first navigation, moves toward older entries, loads the selected history command, and refreshes autocomplete.
- `history_down()` moves toward newer entries, restores the snapshot after the newest entry, or clears input when no snapshot exists.
- `execute_input()` optionally commits autocomplete, appends `"] " + con->input` to visible output, deduplicates adjacent history entries, trims history, sends `con->input + "\n"` through `game::Cbuf_AddText(0, command.c_str())`, then clears input/navigation/autocomplete state.
- `handle_special_key(int vk)` maps `VK_ESCAPE` to close, `VK_RETURN` to execute, `VK_BACK`/`VK_DELETE` to deletion, arrows/Home/End to cursor/history/navigation, `VK_PRIOR`/`VK_NEXT` to six-line scrolling, and `VK_TAB` to autocomplete or Shift/Ctrl output-pane toggles.
- `scroll_output(int amount)` changes `con->scroll_offset` only when output is visible; autocomplete match view reverses the sign relative to normal output scrolling.
- `handle_full_console_toggle_press()` opens the overlay if necessary and toggles `output_visible` plus `output_fullscreen`; the full-console view is reached through Shift+OEM key.
- `toggle_overlay_state()` delegates state transitions to `set_overlay_active()`.

## Keyboard and Focus Contracts

- `get_window()` returns `*game::main_window`.
- `is_game_focused()` requires a valid window and `GetForegroundWindow() == hwnd`.
- `is_key_down(int vk)` tests `(GetAsyncKeyState(vk) & 0x8000) != 0`.
- `is_modifier_down(int vk, int left_vk, int right_vk)` combines polled aggregate, left/right cached, and left/right OS key states.
- `is_any_shift_down()` checks `VK_SHIFT`, `VK_LSHIFT`, and `VK_RSHIFT`; `is_any_ctrl_down()` checks `VK_CONTROL`, `VK_LCONTROL`, and `VK_RCONTROL`.
- `process_console_input()` polls virtual keys `8..255`, recognizes first presses and repeatable-key repeats, uses a `350u` initial repeat delay and `45u` repeat interval, and excludes F1, `VK_OEM_5`, and `VK_OEM_102` from text insertion.
- `safe_process_console_input()` requires `component_ready`, `overlay_active`, a valid focused `HWND`, and non-shutdown state, then catches all structured exceptions around `process_console_input()`.
- `cl_key_event_body(int local_client_num, int key, int down, unsigned int time)` handles mouse-wheel scrolling on key-down and returns `1` when focused overlay input should be swallowed.
- F1 toggles `overlay_active`; OEM-5 and OEM-102 toggle normally, while Shift+OEM-5 or Shift+OEM-102 toggles the full output console.
- `debug_log_toggle(const char* key_name)` is compiled as a no-op in release and retains a disabled debug logging block under `DEBUG`.

## Rendering

- `get_console_font()` returns `*game::con_font` when available, otherwise registers `"fonts/normalFont"` through `game::R_RegisterFont()`.
- `get_white_material()` registers the `"white"` material through `game::Material_RegisterHandle()`.
- `resolve_layout_width(const game::ScreenPlacement& scr_place)` prefers the larger positive real viewport dimension, then virtual viewable dimension, then `640.0f`.
- `resolve_layout_height(const game::ScreenPlacement& scr_place)` prefers the smaller positive real viewport dimension, then virtual viewable dimension, then `480.0f`.
- `get_overlay_bounds()` uses the client rectangle when available, otherwise `game::ScrPlace_GetViewPlacement()`, with six-pixel screen margins, minimum bounds `634.0f × 474.0f`, and font-derived visible line/width calculations.
- `draw_box(float x, float y, float width, float height, float* color)` draws a filled rectangle and two-pixel darkened borders through `game::R_AddCmdDrawStretchPic()`.
- `draw_text(const char* text, float x, float y, float* color, float scale)` draws text through `game::R_AddCmdDrawText()` with `0x7FFFFFFF` character limit.
- `draw_text_shadowed()` draws `overlay_shadow_color` at `+1.0f,+1.0f` before the requested text.
- `draw_input_box()` and `draw_hint_box()` construct bordered panels from `draw_box()`.
- `draw_hint_text()` positions lines using `font_height`, line index, `15.0f` vertical padding, and optional offsets.
- `draw_dvar_match_details()` safely renders current, latched, default, description, and domain data; unavailable values use `"<unavailable>"`, and latched dvars are detected with `game::dvar_flags::latched`.
- `draw_input()` renders the prompt, selection highlight, input text, blinking `|` caret, and autocomplete; the caret blink period is `500ms`.
- `draw_input()` displays `"%i matches (too many to show here, press shift+tilde to open full console)"` when matches exceed `max_auto_complete_matches == 24u`.
- `draw_output_scrollbar()` scales the slider by `visible_lines / total_lines` and positions it using `con->scroll_offset`.
- `draw_output_window()` uses `con_outputHeightScale` clamped to `[0.20f, 0.98f]` with fallback `0.72f` for non-fullscreen output, while fullscreen output uses scale `1.0f`.
- `draw_console_overlay()` renders only when `is_active()`, `con`, valid bounds, and non-shutdown state exist; it draws output before input when `con->output_visible` is true.

- `GIT_HASH`, `GIT_DIRTY`, `VERSION_PRODUCT`, `VERSION_BUILD`, `DEBUG`, and `NDEBUG` control observable version text.

- [component_interface.hpp](./component_interface.hpp) — Defines `component_interface` with virtual lifecycle hooks, import handling, support filtering, and `game::XAssetType` identification.
- [component_loader.hpp](./component_loader.hpp) — Declares `component_loader`, `premature_shutdown_trigger`, `installer<T>`, `get<T>()`, and `REGISTER_COMPONENT(name)`.
- [component_loader.cpp](./component_loader.cpp) — Implements component registry ownership, lifecycle dispatch, cleanup, import resolution, exception handling, and shutdown signaling.

## API Surface

`component_interface` exposes `~component_interface()`, `post_start()`, `post_load()`, `pre_destroy()`, `load_import(const std::string&, const std::string&) -> void*`, `is_supported() -> bool`, and `get_type() -> game::XAssetType`.

`component_loader` exposes `register_component(std::unique_ptr<component_interface>&&)`, `post_start() -> bool`, `post_load() -> bool`, `pre_destroy() -> void`, `clean() -> void`, `load_import(const std::string&, const std::string&) -> void*`, `trigger_premature_shutdown() -> void`, and `get_components() -> std::vector<std::unique_ptr<component_interface>>&`.

`get<T>()` compares exact `typeid` values and returns `nullptr` when no matching component exists; `installer<T>` enforces `T : component_interface` and registers `std::make_unique<T>()`.

## File Relationships

`REGISTER_COMPONENT(name)` creates an anonymous-namespace static `component_loader::installer<name>`, which transfers each `name` instance into the registry returned by `get_components()`.

`post_start()` invokes `component_interface::post_start()` once, while `post_load()` invokes `clean()` before dispatching `component_interface::post_load()` once.

`clean()` calls `component_interface::pre_destroy()` before removing unsupported components, and `pre_destroy()` calls `component_interface::pre_destroy()` for every retained component.

`load_import()` queries every `component_interface` and returns the last non-null import pointer.

## Behavioral Contracts

`component_interface::load_import()` returns `nullptr`, `component_interface::is_supported()` returns `true`, and `component_interface::get_type()` returns `game::ASSET_TYPE_INVALID` by default.

`post_start()` and `post_load()` use static `handled` sentinels, return immediately on repetition, return `false` for `premature_shutdown_trigger`, and otherwise return `true`.

`premature_shutdown_trigger::what()` returns `"Premature shutdown requested"`; `trigger_premature_shutdown()` throws `premature_shutdown_trigger`.

`post_start()` and `post_load()` wrap `std::exception`, `const char*`, and unknown exceptions as `std::runtime_error` using `post_start failed in {}: {}` and `post_load failed in {}: {}`.

`log_component_event()` emits `[component_loader] {} {}\n` through `OutputDebugStringA`, `std::printf`, and `std::fflush(stdout)`.

`get_components()` owns a process-wide registry through a function-local static `std::unique_ptr` with a `std::function` deleter; registry destruction calls `pre_destroy()` before deleting the vector.

`typeid(*component_).name()` identifies runtime component types, and registry iteration follows Registry plus Chain-of-Responsibility dispatch patterns.
